title: Reliability-Based Back Analysis of Deep Urban Excavations Using Field Monitoring and Random Field Finite Elements
PUBLIC SECTOR READINESS FOR PERMISSIONED BLOCKCHAIN FINANCIAL REPORTING IN GHANA: BUILDING STRONG INSTITUTIONS AND RESILIENT DIGITAL INFRASTRUCTURE
container-title: International Journal of Accounting & Finance Review
items.abstract: <jats:p>Periodic, batch-based public financial reporting in developing countries weakens accountability, yet little is known about whether public institutions are ready to adopt permissioned blockchain for real-time reporting. This study examines how technological, human capital, regulatory and legal, organisational, leadership and political will, and data security and privacy readiness shape adoption readiness intent for permissioned blockchain-based financial reporting in Ghana's public sector, an issue central to accountable and transparent institutions (SDG 16) and resilient digital infrastructure and innovation (SDG 9). The study uses survey data from 300 officials in ministries, local government authorities, state-owned enterprises and regulatory bodies, selected through proportional stratified sampling and analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling and one-way ANOVA. The results show that all six dimensions have significant positive effects on adoption readiness intent: technological readiness (β = 0.312, p < 0.001), human capital readiness (β = 0.274, p < 0.001), organisational readiness (β = 0.221, p < 0.001), regulatory and legal readiness (β = 0.198, p < 0.001), leadership and political will (β = 0.189, p < 0.001) and data security and privacy readiness (β = 0.163, p = 0.001). The model explains 69.3% of the variance in adoption readiness intent (R² = 0.693; Q² = 0.481). The findings suggest that infrastructure and skills drive readiness most strongly, that readiness is weakest in data security and privacy (M = 3.48) and the legal framework (M = 3.54), and that Greater Accra institutions score 0.67 points above Upper Region institutions on technological readiness.</jats:p>

title: An NMR Study of Dynamics in Aqueous Strong Acid Solutions. Part I. The B′ Coefficients
Resonant Excitation of the Boundary Distortion of a Cold Semi-Infinite Plasma by Electromagnetic Radiation
items.abstract: <jats:p>The effect of external electromagnetic radiation on the curvature of the boundary of a semi-infinite cold plasma, together with the parameters and properties of surface oscillations localized near this boundary, is considered. A new system of two equations has been derived from the known hydrodynamic description of cold electron plasma motion to analyze the nonlinear interaction of a strong electromagnetic field with an electrostatic wave at the plasma surface and with the cavity that appears at the plasma boundary. The self-consistent excitation of electrostatic waves and appearing cavities takes place under certain conditions and may be provided by special choices of initial-boundary magnitudes of perturbation parameters. The corresponding approximate description makes it possible to reveal basic peculiarities of perturbations under consideration and to identify methods of exciting such disturbances of a plasma boundary state. The investigated properties of the surface curvature can be used to obtain current information about the state of the plasma surface and for active influence on it by means, for example, of electromagnetic beams.</jats:p>

title: CO2 Hydrogenation to Methanol over Metal–Organic Framework Catalysts: Reaction Pathways and Catalyst Design Strategies
items.abstract: <jats:p>Conversion of CO2 into fuels and value-added chemicals is an emerging area that enables the evolution toward a circular carbon economy. CO2 can be utilized to produce methanol, ethanol, methane and light olefins through renewable hydrogen. Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) are an excellent platform for thermocatalytic CO2 hydrogenation to methanol, as their metal nodes, organic linkers, defects and confined pore environments can be engineered to enhance CO2 adsorption, H2 activation and stabilization of crucial reaction intermediates. However, many MOFs still suffer from drawbacks such as low thermal stability, limited mass transport, weak metal-support interaction and potential framework destruction under hydrogenation conditions, which can limit methanol productivity and long-term catalyst stability. This review summarizes recent progress in MOF-based catalysts and MOF-derived materials for CO2 hydrogenation to methanol, with a focus on reaction pathways, pore confinement, active-site design, catalyst stability, and structure-performance relationships. The advantages and remaining limitations of MOF systems are discussed in comparison with conventional heterogeneous catalysts, and future strategies are proposed for developing more selective, durable, and energy-efficient catalysts for sustainable methanol synthesis.</jats:p>

title: CFD Simulation and Optimization of Adiabatic Reaction Process of C-2 Hydrogenation
container-title: International Journal of Theoretical & Computational Physics
items.abstract: <jats:p>In this paper, the computational fluid dynamics (CFD) method has been used to simulate the gas flow and the catalytic hydrogenation process of the C-2 hydrogenation adiabatic reactor in a practical ethylene production unit of a chemical plant. The laminar finite-rate model was used for the chemical reaction model. The standard k -ε two-equation model was used for the turbulence Model. The exponent-function kinetic model was used for the reaction dynamics model. The simulation results were in good agreement with the actual industrial data obtained from the C-2 hydrogenation reactor, and the distributions of reaction parameters such as temperature and component concentrations in the reactor were further analyzed. Based on the validated CFD models, the structure and operating conditions of the reactor, as well as hydrogen load distribution ratios, are simulated for comparing the comprehensive performance metrics of ethylene selectivity and acetylene conversion rate; as a result, we can obtain the optimal temperature of 312 K, the optimal hydrogen/acetylene ratio of 0.10 as well as the optimal hydrogen load distribution ratio of 4:4:2, and the diameter/height ratio exerts a marginal effect on the selectivity, conversion rate and harmonic mean of the reactor.</jats:p>

title: WSGNN: Weak-Strong Ties-Aware Graph Neural Network for Link Prediction
container-title: International Journal of Interactive Multimedia and Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: <jats:p> Social network link prediction aims to reveal potential or future connections in a network by leveraging structural features or node attribute information. In recent years, graph neural network (GNN)-based link prediction methods have attracted widespread attention in link prediction. However, link prediction methods based on graph neural networks (GNNs) rarely consider network features from the perspective of strong and weak connections, thereby overlooking the representational ability of long-tail nodes during the message-passing process. To address the role of long-tail node features in the information propagation process of GNN-based link prediction methods, we propose a novel Weak-Strong Ties-Aware Graph Neural Network (WSGNN), characterizing node roles by combining degree centrality and betweenness centrality, and construct a parameterized module to enhance nodes based on centrality scores. The WSGNN achieves awareness of both strong and weak associations through two functional modules: a strong association perception module and a weak association enhancement module. The strong association perception module captures strong connections between nodes using degree centrality features at the shallow layers of the GNN; the weak association module captures weak connections between network nodes using betweenness centrality at the deep layers of the GNN, and activates bridge nodes to enhance information propagation across communities within networks. Experimental evaluations on six social network datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in terms of prediction performance compared to existing methods. This method not only improves the performance of GNN-based link prediction in static networks but also provides a novel perspective for extending structural role perception to temporal and heterogeneous networks.</jats:p>

title: Risperidone: Adverse cutaneous reaction managed without drug discontinuation
items.abstract: <jats:p>Antipsychotic agents can cause skin rashes in some patients, affecting compliance. Although more common with typical antipsychotics, atypical antipsychotics such as olanzapine and clozapine have also been associated with these reactions. While there is no way to predict such reactions, the mechanisms causing such reactions are being actively researched. We present a case study of a 36-year-old female who developed cutaneous reactions with oral risperidone. It was observed that reducing the dose of oral risperidone led to complete resolution of skin rashes, a novel approach that differed from previous reports requiring complete discontinuation.</jats:p>

title: A Single Ultrasonic Time-of-Flight Uniquely Determines Surface Heat Flux and Temperature Field: Proof and Temperature Field Experiment
items.abstract: <jats:p>Ultrasonic time-of-flight (TOF) is sensitive to the temperature along its propagation path, which offers a non-intrusive route to sense the thermal state inside solid structures. However, existing ultrasonic thermometry methods mostly rely on a dual-measurement strategy (TOF + boundary temperature) and lack a theoretical basis for inverting heat flux from a single TOF sequence alone. This paper establishes a thermo-acoustic measurement model incorporating thermal expansion correction and proves that, under one-dimensional transient heat conduction, a single TOF sequence is sufficient to recover both the surface heat flux and the internal temperature field without ambiguity. To solve the resulting inverse problem, we implement a conjugate-gradient algorithm regularized by the Morozov discrepancy principle as the stopping rule. Numerical validation under five heat flux profiles shows that the reconstruction error (NRMSE) stays below 0.65% with noise-free input data. More importantly, when realistic noise levels are introduced—specifically ±1 ns TOF jitter and ±2.5 °C temperature uncertainty, consistent with our instrument specifications—the single-TOF approach (M1) achieves NRMSE values between 9.8% and 24.2%, markedly below the hard-Dirichlet dual-measurement scheme (M2, using both TOF and boundary temperature, 88.7–155.6%) at the same noise point. We attribute this large gap to the different ways each noise source enters the inversion: TOF perturbations are effectively damped by the soft-constraint formulation and the discrepancy criterion, while boundary temperature errors are imposed as a Dirichlet hard constraint and therefore propagate directly into the estimated state field. The method is further applied to a flat plate heating experiment on 20# steel, in which the reconstructed heat flux is fed back through the forward conduction model and the resulting temperature history is compared against four thermocouples not used in the inversion. The reconstructed temperature field matches four embedded thermocouples within 2.58 °C RMS.</jats:p>

title: The lessons I wish to pass on to future generations of field primatologists
Temporal gating of radiation formation in nonlinear Thomson scattering
items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    The formation process of the radiation pattern in nonlinear Thomson scattering is investigated through single-electron simulations of an ultraintense, tightly focused, elliptically polarized Gaussian pulse. The angular pattern is found to be written not uniformly over the illumination window but inside a narrow temporal gate: relativistic beaming compresses the emission into a train of carrier-anchored bursts, and the cumulative radiation record freezes once the envelope-top bursts have passed, at 0.96 of the pulse-arrival time for
                    <jats:italic>L</jats:italic>
                    = 3 and 5 cycles and at 0.76 for
                    <jats:italic>L</jats:italic>
                    = 10. When the circular polarization symmetry is broken, the carrierenvelope phase (CEP) acquires a genuine response: at moderate amplitudes it changes neither the radiated energy nor the lobe positions, but selects which of the two long-axis burst families writes the record, producing a staircase dependence of the peak azimuth on the CEP. The response switches on as soon as the ellipticity deviates from unity and decays as $R\propto1/L^{2}$  with the pulse duration
                    <jats:italic>L</jats:italic>
                    , because the gate widens linearly with
                    <jats:italic>L</jats:italic>
                    while the parabolic envelope top admits sub-cycle misalignment only at second order. The in-gate bursts are few-attosecond flashes whose interference prints a harmonic comb onto the spectrum. The temporal gate thus turns radiation-pattern formation into a record-based observable with measurable fingerprints, and adds a new control handle for attosecond diagnostics and compact X/
                    <jats:italic>γ</jats:italic>
                    -ray sources.
                  </jats:p>

title: Radiation education across sectors and populations: a narrative review of research trends, methods, and gaps
items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Radiation education encompasses a broad spectrum of activities aimed at improving knowledge, attitudes, and literacy related to radiation safety across school, professional, and public settings. Despite a growing body of research—accelerated by the 2011 Fukushima Daiichi nuclear accident—the field remains fragmented, with individual studies and reviews addressing isolated populations or single educational settings. This narrative review provides a cross-sector synthesis of radiation education research, spanning school-based instruction, healthcare professional training, public and community literacy programmes, and emerging educational technologies. The literature was selected purposively and supplemented by hand-searching of reference lists; separately, the yields of searches in six databases (PubMed/MEDLINE, ERIC, Scopus, Ichushi-Web, CiNii Research, and J-STAGE) were recorded in September 2026 to document the searches, and the retrieved records were not assessed for inclusion. The review identifies three major research clusters: (1) school-based radiation education in post-Fukushima Japan, shaped by a national curriculum revision that predated the accident and by post-accident supplementary textbooks; (2) knowledge–attitude–practice studies among healthcare workers across multiple countries, consistently revealing suboptimal radiation protection literacy; and (3) innovative educational technologies, including problem-based learning, virtual reality, and game-based approaches, predominantly evaluated in professional training contexts. Critical research gaps include the limited evaluation of community-based programmes outside Japan, the predominance of short-term knowledge outcomes with few studies measuring sustained behavioural change, and the near-absence of cross-sector comparative research. This review offers a synthesis of radiation education research across sectors and proposes priorities for future investigation, including the development of cross-sector comparable measures of radiation literacy and longitudinal studies of behavioural change.</jats:p>

title: Social Support and Athlete Burnout Among Track and Field Athletes in The Special Region of Yogyakarta: The Moderating Role of Sex
container-title: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF MULTIDISCIPLINARY RESEARCH AND ANALYSIS
items.abstract: <jats:p>This study aimed to examine the relationship between social support and athlete burnout and to investigate the moderating role of sex among track and field athletes in the Special Region of Yogyakarta, Indonesia. A quantitative approach with a cross-sectional correlational design was employed. The participants were 78 athletes, consisting of 42 males and 36 females, selected using a total sampling technique. Data were collected using the PASS-Q to measure social support and the ABQ to assess athlete burnout. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and moderated regression analysis with PROCESS Macro Model 1. The results revealed that social support was negatively and significantly associated with athlete burnout (b = −0.915; p < 0.001). Sex significantly moderated this relationship, as indicated by a negative and significant interaction coefficient (b = −1.073; p < 0.001; ΔR² = 0.207). Conditional effect analysis showed that the negative relationship between social support and athlete burnout was stronger among female athletes (b = −1.492; p < 0.001) than among male athletes (b = −0.420; p < 0.001). The research model explained 78.4% of the variance in athlete burnout (R² = 0.784). These findings indicate that social support is associated with lower levels of athlete burnout, although the strength of this relationship differs by sex. The results highlight the importance of developing social support systems that are responsive to athletes' needs within sports development environments.</jats:p>

Geomagnetic Field Variations Associated with Seismic Energy Release: Analysis of Observatory Data from 2021–2025
items.abstract: <jats:p>This study investigates the long-term variations in the mean total geomagnetic field intensity (T, not to be confused with the SI unit tesla) observed during 2021–2025 at the ART and NVS geomagnetic observatories (Russia), IZN (Türkiye), JAI (India), and Yangibozor (YNBZ, Uzbekistan). One-minute geomagnetic observations obtained from the INTERMAGNET database were used to calculate daily and annual mean values. To quantify the annual rate of change of the total field intensity, used here as a proxy for secular variation, a linear regression slope (nT/year) was determined for each observatory and each year. The calculated regression slopes were spatially interpolated using Geographic Information System (GIS) techniques to assess regional variations in the rate of geomagnetic field change. The results revealed spatial differences in regression slope values among the selected observatories, indicating regional differences in the rate of change of the total field. These differences may reflect geodynamo processes in the Earth's outer core, regional geomagnetic characteristics, and the influence of external geomagnetic field sources, which could not be fully separated in this study. In addition, the annual cumulative seismic energy of earthquakes with magnitudes M ≥ 4.0 occurring within a 200 km radius of each observatory was calculated and compared with the corresponding regression slopes. The results indicate that no consistent linear relationship exists between long-term geomagnetic field variations and annual seismic energy. Similar temporal tendencies were observed at some observatories but not at others, and they do not demonstrate a causal relationship.</jats:p>

Information Geometry of Non-Extensive Statistical Field Theories
container-title: International Journal of Modern Physics A
items.abstract: <jats:p>We study the information-geometric structures of non-extensive statistical field theories based on Tsallis q-deformations formulated within the escort-distribution framework. The q-Fisher metric, affine connections, and divergence functionals are derived in both the source and field-expectation parametrizations. We find a structural mismatch specific to q ≠ 1: the escort covariancedriving the q-Polchinski flow does not coincide with the Legendre-Hessian metric, so the non-extensive renormalization group does not reduce to the standard closed Wetterich equation. The mismatch is computed exactly for free q-field theory, where the two differ by a q- and regulator-dependent constant factor, and whether the flow can be recast as a closed functional equation on the effective action alone is left open.The connections to Kaniadakis statistics and general f-divergences are also discussed.</jats:p>

title: Microbiota-nutrition sequential therapy for refractory radiation proctitis: A case report
items.abstract:
<jats:p>BACKGROUND</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Gut dysbiosis is closely associated with radiation-induced intestinal injury. This study aimed to preliminarily assess the efficacy and safety of fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) combined with immunomodulatory enteral nutrition (IEN) for the treatment of refractory radiation proctitis.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>CASE SUMMARY</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>A 49-year-old woman with prior cervical cancer treated by hysterectomy 4 years earlier presented with left inguinal lymphadenopathy. Following radiotherapy, the patient experienced lower abdominal pain, diarrhea, and hematochezia, diagnosed as radiation enteritis. The patient underwent two FMT with adjunctive IEN support. Symptoms alleviated from Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events grade 3 proctitis to grade 2 after the first FMT, and further to grade 1 after the second. Nutritional and immune indices improved obviously: Body mass index (20.28 kg/m2→24.34 kg/m2), total protein (63.7 g/L→73.7 g/L), albumin (35.8 g/L→40 g/L), lymphocyte count (0.94× 109/L→1.37 × 109/L) and lymphocyte percentage (18.2%→34.8%) rose, while procalcitonin dropped from 0.07 ng/mL to 0.03 ng/mL. The Vienna Rectoscopy Score declined from 25 to 16 post-FMT1 and 5 post-FMT2. Pro-inflammatory cytokines tumor necrosis factor-α (2.29 pg/mL→1.51 pg/mL), interferon (IFN)-γ (0.73 pg/mL→0.16 pg/mL) and interleukin (IL)-6 (9.40 pg/mL→3.60 pg/mL) decreased significantly, while anti-inflammatory IL-4 (0.97 pg/mL→1.16 pg/mL) and IL-10 (0.70 pg/mL→0.86 pg/mL) slightly increased. IL-2 and IL-1β rose mildly, and IL-8 elevated moderately. Sequential FMT restored gut Shannon diversity; principal coordinates analysis verified microbiota remodeling close to donor profiles, with reduced Escherichia-Shigella  and enriched beneficial genera Faecalibacterium , Bacteroides  and Ruminococcus .</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>CONCLUSION</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>In this patient, FMT combined with immunomodulatory nutrition was associated with restoration of gut microbiota, alleviation of symptoms, and improvement in nutritional and immune parameters in refractory radiation proctitis, suggesting a potential therapeutic strategy that warrants further validation.</jats:p>

title: Agrobiological and ecological determinants of legal regulation in Russian field crop production
items.abstract: <jats:p>This study examines the agrobiological foundations and regulatory framework governing field crop production in the Russian Federation. The research evaluates the alignment between agronomic crop classifications, plant physiology, phytosanitary dynamics, grain quality standards, and statutory requirements. Terminological analysis reveals conceptual overlap between field crop production and adjacent sectors, specifically vegetable growing and meadow management. To eliminate this ambiguity, the study distinguishes between a narrow legal interpretation restricted to grain cultivation and a broad interpretation encompassing all arable field crops. The analysis substantiates the necessity of codifying six biological crop groups alongside the statutory categories of "field crop production activity," "field crop farm" (as a commercial producer eligible for state support), and "field crop enterprise" (as a property complex). Comparative assessment of cultivar ontogenesis, vernalization thresholds, economic thresholds of weed harmfulness, and state quality standards confirms that legal norms must incorporate biological and ecological parameters. Based on these findings, six legislative proposals are formulated to establish producer rights, phytosanitary obligations, and quality requirements within a specialized federal law on field crop production.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>Pencatatan persediaan dan pengendalian stok merupakan aspek penting dalam menjaga ketersediaan produk dan keakuratan catatan akuntansi di kantin sekolah. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengkaji praktik pencatatan persediaan dan pengendalian stok di Kantin Kesatuan Bangsa School serta mengidentifikasi kendala yang memengaruhi keakuratan pencatatan. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan deskriptif kualitatif melalui wawancara dengan pengelola kantin dan staf akuntansi, observasi, serta pemeriksaan dokumen pendukung berupa faktur dan bukti transaksi. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan beberapa kendala, meliputi pencatatan harian yang belum lengkap, pemindahan data secara manual, keterlambatan penyerahan dokumen transaksi, serta pencatatan barang retur, rusak, atau tidak layak jual yang belum konsisten. Selain itu, transaksi QRIS pada malam hari atau akhir pekan dapat tercatat dalam mutasi rekening pada hari kerja berikutnya sehingga memerlukan rekonsiliasi. Kegiatan PKL juga mencakup pemeriksaan sisa persediaan di Kantin Putra dan Kantin Putri menggunakan faktur sebagai acuan. Temuan ini menegaskan pentingnya pencatatan persediaan yang konsisten, dokumentasi lengkap, pemeriksaan stok berkala, dan rekonsiliasi untuk meningkatkan keandalan informasi akuntansi serta pengendalian persediaan</jats:p>

title: A field–Numerical framework for the design of disconnected piled raft foundations in stratified cohesive soils
items.abstract: <jats:p xml:lang="en">This study investigates the performance of disconnected piled raft foundations (DPRFs) in stratified cohesive soils through field load testing, empirical interpretation, and advanced finite element simulations. A full-scale instrumented barrette pile test in İzmir, Türkiye provided settlement and shaft resistance profiles for model calibration. Field response was interpreted using hyperbolic load–settlement relations and qs–cu correlations, offering benchmarks between measured and predicted capacities. Numerical analyses incorporated nonlinear soil behavior and staged construction, with calibration ensuring predictive accuracy within ±20%. Back-analysis confirmed interface formulations and enabled evaluation of settlement, stiffness degradation, shaft/toe resistance mobilization, and energy absorption. Parametric analyses on disconnected piled raft (DPRF) systems revealed that cushion stiffness and pile spacing dominate settlement and load transfer, while pile modulus and raft thickness are secondary. Results showed that optimized DPRF systems can reach ~67% of connected piled raft stiffness, offering a practical, performance-based alternative in cohesive soils.</jats:p>

title: Task-dependent predictability of gamma passing rates in stereotactic body radiation therapy using UCoMX plan-complexity features: a patient-group-aware machine learning benchmark
items.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Treatment-plan complexity metrics have been proposed for predicting patient-specific quality assurance outcomes, but their predictive value may depend on the gamma criterion and task definition. This study evaluated the task-dependent predictability of gamma passing rates (GPRs) in stereotactic body radiation therapy (SBRT) using Universal Complexity Metrics Extractor (UCoMX) plan-complexity features.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The retrospective cohort included 206 SBRT plans from 163 patients. Nineteen numerical UCoMX features were evaluated in patient-group-aware nested cross-validation. The benchmark included full-cohort binary classification of G31 (GPR evaluated using the 3%/1 mm criterion) and G32 (GPR evaluated using the 3%/2 mm criterion), continuous G32 regression, and joint G31–G32 endpoint modeling. A secondary exploratory analysis compared clearly separated G31 outcomes, defined as low-GPR (&lt;90%) and high-GPR (≥98%) groups. Predictions were obtained from pooled outer-fold out-of-fold evaluations. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis was performed for the extreme-outcome Logistic Regression model using held-out outer-fold records.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Predictive performance varied across GPR endpoints and task formulations. In the full-cohort analyses, G31 classification achieved a best ROC-AUC of 0.642 (95% CI: 0.563–0.718) and a PR-AUC of 0.710 against a failure prevalence of 0.592, whereas the best G32 classification ROC-AUC was 0.611 (95% CI: 0.527–0.692). Continuous G32 prediction showed limited added value over fold-specific null predictors, with a best learned-model MAE of 3.241 percentage points compared with 3.245 for the training-set median null predictor. In contrast, the exploratory G31 extreme-outcome analysis achieved a pooled outer-fold ROC-AUC of 0.831 (95% CI: 0.716–0.926), with a balanced accuracy of 0.700, sensitivity of 0.567, and specificity of 0.833. SHAP analysis identified prescribed dose, dose-normalized monitor units, leaf travel, and modulation-related complexity measures as leading contributors to model predictions.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The predictive performance of the UCoMX-centered plan-level predictor representation varied across the gamma criteria and task formulations evaluated. While full-cohort prediction at the 95% analytical threshold remained challenging, substantially stronger discrimination was observed for separated G31 outcomes. These findings demonstrate that the combined UCoMX-derived plan-level and treatment-characteristic representation contains meaningful predictive information under specific task formulations and provide a basis for developing more informative GPR prediction models through integration with additional dosimetric, geometric, or delivery-related predictors.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title:
Double-Hybrid Multiconfigurational
Pair-Density Functional
Theory
container-title:
Journal of Chemical Theory
and Computation
items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>We introduce double-hybrid (DH) multiconfigurational pair-density functional theory (DH-MC-PDFT), a method that extends the DH design principle of Kohn–Sham density functional theory to strongly correlated systems described by a multiconfigurational reference wave function. In DH-MC-PDFT, the energy is expressed as a combination of the complete active space self-consistent field (CASSCF) classical energy, a fraction of nonlocal CASSCF exchange-correlation, the on-top pair-density functional energy, and a perturbative partially contracted second-order n-electron valence state perturbation theory (PC-NEVPT2) correction, with two mixing parameters controlling the balance between these contributions. Using the MC25 on-top functional [ Zhang, D.; et al.J. Chem. Theory Comput.2025, 21, 10945–10960]., the DH-MC25 functional is proposed, in which the parameters are optimized against training data derived from the potential energy curve of the Cr2 molecule. The method is benchmarked on a comprehensive set of databases covering bond dissociation energies, potential energy curve shape descriptors, atomic excitation energies, and total atomization energies. DH-MC25 achieves a mean unsigned error of 2.79 kcal/mol across the full validation set, outperforming both its parent functional MC25 and NEVPT2 by approximately 30% and 34%, respectively. The consistent improvement across structurally and chemically diverse benchmark datasets demonstrates that DH-MC-PDFT is a robust and broadly applicable strategy in multiconfigurational quantum chemistry.</jats:p>

title:
Synergistic Iodide/Capacitive Ion Storage in a Fluorinated Carbon Black Matrix Toward 1.9 V High‐Energy‐Density Zn‐I
                    <sub>2</sub>
                    Batteries
items.abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Aqueous zinc‐iodine (Zn‐I
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    ) batteries hold promise for high‐safety, large‐scale energy storage. However, their performance is hindered by the polyiodide shuttle effect and the low voltage plateau (∼1.2 V). Herein, we enhance the capacitive behavior under high voltage by introducing a fluorinated carbon black (CF
                    <jats:sub>20</jats:sub>
                    ) matrix into a I
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    /activated carbon (AC) cathode. The CF
                    <jats:sub>20</jats:sub>
                    matrix attracts more ions into AC at high potential and enhances the capacitive ions storage behavior. When both AC and iodine are counted, the specific cathode capacity increases from 117.9 mAh g
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    (up to 1.6 V) to 163.4 mAh g
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    (up to 1.9 V), equivalent to 329.8 mAh g
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    counting iodine only. Meanwhile, the CF
                    <jats:sub>20</jats:sub>
                    matrix effectively chemisorbs polyiodides, acting as a shuttle suppressor. The full cell retains >85% initial capacity after 6500 cycles at 4 A g
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    . When the mass loading is increased to 32.46 mg cm
                    <jats:sup>−2</jats:sup>
                    , it delivers a record areal capacity of 2.92 mAh cm
                    <jats:sup>−2</jats:sup>
                    . When paired with a ∼7 um Zn foil (N/p = 1.4), the full cell retains 83% capacity over 900 cycles, demonstrate an energy density as high as 204 Wh kg
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    . This work provides a viable paradigm to activate capacitive contribution in Zn‐I
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    system toward high‐voltage, high‐energy‐density aqueous batteries.
                  </jats:p>

title: HEPTAPOD: Orchestrating high energy physics workflows towards autonomous agency
items.abstract: <jats:p>Many workflows in high-energy-physics (HEP) stand to benefit from recent advances in transformer-based large language models (LLMs). While early applications of LLMs focused on text generation and code completion, modern LLMs now support orchestrated agency: the coordinated execution of complex, multi-step tasks through tool use, structured context, and iterative reasoning. We introduce the HEP Toolkit for Agentic Planning, Orchestration, and Deployment (HEPTAPOD), an orchestration framework designed to integrate external LLMs into general HEP workflows spanning theoretical calculations, simulation, and data analysis. The framework enables LLMs to interface with domain-specific tools and to construct and manage diverse HEP pipelines while preserving transparency, reproducibility, and human oversight. To demonstrate these capabilities, we present a representative case study in the context of a Beyond the Standard Model (BSM) Monte Carlo signal validation that spans model generation, event simulation, and analysis within an established, reproducible workflow. HEPTAPOD provides a structured and auditable layer between human researchers, LLMs, and computational infrastructure, establishing a foundation for transparent, human-in-the-loop systems.</jats:p>

title: Confined iodine and accelerated redox kinetics enable high-rate Zn-iodine batteries
items.abstract: <jats:p>Zinc-iodine batteries have attracted considerable attention owing to their high safety and low cost. However, their further development is hindered by the polyiodide shuttle effect and sluggish iodine redox kinetics. Here, we employed a synergistic strategy combining pore size regulation and nitrogen doping to design an iodine-loaded, nitrogen-doped reduced graphene oxide cathode (I2@RGO-3) for enhanced iodine confinement and redox kinetics. The abundant microporous/mesoporous structure of the RGO framework physically confines electroactive iodine species, while the graphitic-N-rich interface facilitates interfacial charge transfer and promotes iodine redox kinetics. The as-prepared I2@RGO-3 cathode demonstrates an outstanding rate capability, delivering a specific capacity of 172.23 mAh g-1 at 0.5 A g-1, and even at a high current density of 20 A g-1, it still retains 110.52 mAh g-1, corresponding to a capacity retention of approximately 64.17%. It also exhibits stable cycling performance over 5,000 cycles. The synergistic strategy of pore size regulation and atomic doping proposed in this contribution provides new insights into the design of high-performance zinc-iodine battery cathodes.</jats:p>

title: Inertial limit of global weak solutions for compressible Navier–Stokes
container-title: Proceedings of the Royal Society of Edinburgh Section A: Mathematics
items.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    We investigate the inertial limit of the compressible Navier–Stokes system posed on the
                    <jats:inline-formula>
                      <jats:alternatives>
                        <jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" mime-subtype="png" content-type="simple" xlink:href="S0308210526101929_inline1.png">
                          <jats:alt-text content-type="machine-generated">3</jats:alt-text>
                        </jats:inline-graphic>
                        <mml:math xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" xmlns:mnf="http://cambridge.org/core/manifest" xmlns:cup="http://contentservices.cambridge.org" xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:m="http://cambridge.org/core/metadata" xmlns:core="http://cambridge.org/core" xmlns:c="http://cambridge.org/core/content">
                          <mml:mn>3</mml:mn>
                        </mml:math>
                        <jats:tex-math>$3$</jats:tex-math>
                      </jats:alternatives>
                    </jats:inline-formula>
                    -dimensional torus, allowing for regions of vacuum. Considering global-in-time finite-energy weak solutions of a scaled system, we rigorously establish convergence to a limiting system in which the momentum equation reduces to a stationary elliptic balance between pressure and viscous forces. In this limit, the scaled kinetic energy vanishes, reflecting an overdamped regime, and the limiting weak solution satisfies an exact energy equality. Our analysis relies on uniform a priori estimates, renormalized techniques, and compactness arguments in the Lions–Feireisl framework, providing a mathematically rigorous analysis for the overdamped dynamics arising from vanishing inertia in compressible viscous flows.
                  </jats:p>

title: Drip Irrigation Improves Yield Formation by Regulating Assimilate Allocation in High-Density Summer Maize
items.abstract: <jats:p>With increasing pressure on arable land resources in China, increasing planting density has become the most effective agronomic measure for boosting maize yield per unit area. However, high-density planting intensifies competition for resources such as water and nutrients in summer maize, thereby limiting yield increases. Drip fertigation (DI) serves as a key strategy for high-yield cultivation of densely planted summer maize. Based on a two-year field experiment, this study systematically investigated the physiological regulation mechanisms by which DI promotes grain yield formation of densely planted summer maize. The results showed that with increasing planting density, enzyme activities in leaves and grains as well as vascular bundle number and area exhibited a decreasing trend. Grain filling characteristics and yield decreased accordingly. Compared with conventional water and fertilizer management (BI), DI treatment consistently increased sucrose content and sucrose metabolism-related enzyme activities in the ear leaf, improved vascular bundle structures in the ear node and cob peduncle, and increased phloem area. It also enhanced grain filling characteristics, thereby increasing grain weight and yield. Denghai 605 (DH605) had a larger phloem area, but this decreased rapidly as planting density increased. MY73 exhibited a more pronounced advantage in vascular bundle number and high-density tolerance, with the planting density at maximum yield exceeding that of DH605. In summary, drip fertigation enhanced assimilate allocation by coordinating assimilate production, transport, and accumulation, thereby improving grain filling and yield formation under high-density planting. It is a key agronomic practice for achieving high and stable yields in summer maize.</jats:p>

title: Determination of Reference Density from Measured Density and Temperature Data: A Diesel Fuel Case Study
items.abstract: <jats:p>Accurate density measurement is essential in oil and liquid petroleum product handling, particularly in mass and volumetric flow measurement, loss control, and quality assurance processes. Reference density values are commonly determined using standard API tables, which provide a standardized procedure for correcting measured density to reference conditions. The proposed method is evaluated using experimental data acquired during a diesel fuel transfer operation at the “Ilinden”–Makpetrol Skopje terminal in North Macedonia. Density and temperature were monitored using a Micro Motion ELITE Coriolis flow meter. Based on the collected data, the reference density was calculated using the proposed formulation and compared with values obtained from API reference tables. The results show a difference between the reference density values obtained using the two approaches. The proposed approach provides an alternative means of estimating reference density from measured process data. Further validation using independent reference measurements and additional petroleum products under different operating conditions is required to establish its accuracy and applicability.</jats:p>

title: Air Stability of Cathode Prelithiation Agents for High‐Energy Lithium‐Ion Batteries: Degradation Mechanisms and Stabilization Strategies
items.abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    High‐energy‐density lithium‐ion batteries are constrained by irreversible lithium loss during the first cycle, which reduces initial Coulombic efficiency and attainable energy density. Cathode prelithiation compensates for lithium consumed by solid–electrolyte interphase (SEI) formation and interfacial side reactions through highly active lithium sources, thereby increasing the reversible capacity of full cells. However, the high lithium chemical potential and reactivity of prelithiation agents promote reactions with atmospheric H
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    O and CO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    , causing active‐lithium loss, surface passivation, and impaired processability. This Review examines the associated degradation mechanisms and stabilization strategies. Air‐induced degradation is classified into two evidence‐supported pathways: hydrolysis and carbonation of binary lithium compounds, and surface‐lithium loss from lithium‐rich transition‐metal oxides, potentially accompanied by near‐surface reconstruction. Stabilization strategies based on protective coatings, bulk‐structure regulation, and intrinsically stable materials are evaluated in terms of environmental isolation, reaction kinetics, and lithium‐donation capability. Remaining challenges include nonstandardized testing, insufficient long‐term durability, and limited manufacturing compatibility. Establishing multiscale structure–property relationships among lithium‐compensation capability, air stability, and engineering performance is essential for practical implementation.
                  </jats:p>

title: Density-gradient effect in high-harmonic generation in gases
items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>High-harmonic generation (HHG) in gaseous targets is the most widespread method to produce coherent extreme-ultraviolet (XUV) pulses with sub-femtosecond duration. However, this process has intrinsically low efficiency, and substantial research and development is devoted worldwide to increase the achievable photon flux through this highly nonlinear light–matter interaction process. In this work, we show the strong interplay of phase matching and absorption in gas-pressure gradients, substantially affecting macroscopic HHG efficiency. Through detailed experimental analysis and supporting numerical studies, we highlight their significance, particularly at the boundaries of the interaction volume. The concluded results have implications in the massively expanding application possibilities of HHG sources requiring high photon flux, for example in the semiconductor industry, in nanoscale imaging of biological and industrial samples, or in nonlinear optics in the XUV regime.</jats:p>

title: Electrochemical Study of the Adsorption and Protective Film Mechanism of Siam Leaf Extract on High Strength Low Alloy Steel in Combined Sour and Sweet Corrosive Conditions
items.abstract: <jats:p>Corrosion of high-strength low-alloy (HSLA) steel in oil and gas production systems is a major challenge, particularly under environments containing dissolved carbon dioxide (CO₂) and hydrogen sulphide (H₂S). The combined presence of these corrosive gases can accelerate metal dissolution and compromise the integrity of pipelines and related infrastructure. This study investigates the corrosion inhibition potential of siam (Chromolaena odorata) leaf extract on HSLA steel exposed to combined CO₂–H₂S brine, with emphasis on its electrochemical performance, adsorption behaviour and surface protection characteristics. The inhibitor was evaluated at concentrations of 100, 200, 300, 400 and 500 mg/L against an uninhibited control. Open-circuit potential (OCP), electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) and potentiodynamic polarisation (PDP) were employed to assess changes in corrosion behaviour. Surface morphological examination was conducted using scanning electron microscopy (SEM), while elemental composition and possible corrosion-product phases were considered through energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) and X-ray diffraction (XRD), respectively. The electrochemical results indicated a concentration and time dependent improvement in corrosion resistance, with 400 mg/L producing the most favourable performance. At this concentration, the inhibition efficiencies reached 79.7% and 82.3% based on EIS and PDP measurements, respectively. The OCP shifted to a more positive potential, reaching −579 mV after 120 h, while the charge-transfer resistance increased, indicating improved resistance to interfacial corrosion reactions. A slight reduction in performance was observed at 500 mg/L, suggesting that increased extract concentration did not necessarily result in enhanced protection. The SEM observations further indicated comparatively improved surface preservation at 400 mg/L, supporting the electrochemical findings. The results implies that Siam leaf is a potential plant-derived corrosion inhibitor for HSLA steel in combined sweet and sour corrosive environments. Its application may provide a basis for developing more environmentally considerate corrosion-control alternatives for oil and gas infrastructure.</jats:p>

title: Ion–Confinement Strategy for Electrically Debondable Ionoadhesive Tapes With Exceptional Reliability
items.abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    The electrical debonding behavior of ionoadhesives shows great potential in promoting the circular economy; however, the moisture absorption or ionic liquid leakage of existing ionoadhesives seriously deteriorates the service reliability and significantly hinders the development of this field. Here, we propose an ion–confinement strategy for designing electrically debondable ionoadhesive tapes by confining the ionic liquid within polyacrylate nanospheres. The resulting ionoadhesive tapes simultaneously possess excellent interfacial toughness (890–1680 J m
                    <jats:sup>−2</jats:sup>
                    ), high ionic conductivity (6.25 × 10
                    <jats:sup>−6</jats:sup>
                    −1.91 × 10
                    <jats:sup>−5</jats:sup>
                    S m
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    ), high electrical debonding efficiency under 15 V direct current (DC) voltage (>98% within 2 min), and exceptional reliability under harsh conditions. Moreover, this work elucidates the difference in the interaction and ion transport mechanism of cations and anions in polyacrylate polymers, which causes distinct electrical debonding behavior under forward and reverse voltages. This unique electrical debonding behavior offers an effective strategy for precisely controlling the debonding position by simply adjusting the direction of electricity. It is believed that this study provides a theoretical and practical basis for designing ionoadhesives with exceptional reliability and inspires future research on the development of ionically conductive materials.
                  </jats:p>

title: Filling Transition and Microchannel Replication in Injection-Molded High-Flow PFA Microfluidic Chips
items.abstract: <jats:p>Perfluoroalkoxy polymer (PFA) is suitable for chemically resistant microfluidic devices, but complete cavity filling does not necessarily ensure accurate replication of microscale channels. In this study, the filling transition and microchannel replication of injection-molded high-flow PFA substrates were investigated using a three-factor, three-level L9 orthogonal array. Nozzle temperature, mold temperature, and holding pressure were varied, and macroscopic filling was evaluated using projected fill-area ratio and part mass. The actual mold-rib geometry was measured by three-dimensional surface profilometry, and molded channels with nominal widths of 100, 300, and 500 μm were evaluated from optical cross-sectional images. Complete filling was achieved under five of the nine molding conditions, with projected fill-area ratios of 95.74–96.77% and part masses of 1.749–1.757 g. Nozzle temperature had the largest effect on macroscopic filling, followed by mold temperature and holding pressure. Under complete-filling conditions, the opening-width, bottom-width, and depth replication ratios were 77.1–113.2%, 89.6–99.0%, and 83.7–96.5%, respectively. These results show that macroscopic filling and local microchannel replication should be evaluated separately when defining the molding window for PFA microfluidic substrates.</jats:p>

title: Regulation of proton transference for stable and efficient reactive capture of CO2 from air
Energy‐Efficient, High‐Performance Ammonia Decomposition Over Iron Wool Under Magnetic Induction Heating
items.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Ammonia decomposition reaction is one of the main pillars of carbon‐free energy storage strategies using renewable materials and energy resources. However, the full potential of NH
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    as an energy carrier has been largely limited by the high energy requirements and complexity of thermocatalytic systems. In this study, a rational, step‐by‐step design and fabrication of iron wool‐based catalytic systems induced by magnetic induction heating have been developed and demonstrated. Iron wool, a cheap and abundant material, achieved >99% conversion at a temperature of 520 °C, a gas hourly space velocity (GHSV) of 18,000 mL g
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                     h
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    , and specific energy consumption (SEC) of 1.45 kWh/mol H
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    . The formation and propagation of iron nitride species led to structural degradation and reorganization of the iron wool, diminishing its heating efficiency and its catalytic performance during cyclic operations. Mixing iron wool with SiRAlOx‐supported Ni led to full ammonia decomposition at an elevated GHSV of 30,000 mL g
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                     h
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    after only ca. 6 min for temperatures below 470 °C. Furthermore, using SiRAlOx‐supported Ru (1.5–3.3 wt% Ru) resulted in a decreased SEC of 0.73 kWh/mol H
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    while the catalytic stability was largely maintained, as evidenced by a 4%–13% temperature drop.
                  </jats:p>

title:
Domain refinement and constrained polar dynamics enable high-energy-storage in mixed-valence Pr-doped NaNbO
                    <sub>3</sub>
                    -based lead-free ceramics
items.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    The development of high-performance dielectric ceramics is critical for advanced pulsed power capacitors, yet reconciling mutually exclusive energy-storage parameters remains a formidable challenge. Here, we achieve a superior recoverable energy density (W
                    <jats:sub>rec</jats:sub>
                    ) of ~5.4 J/cm
                    <jats:sup>3</jats:sup>
                    with a high efficiency (η) of ~90.2% in a lead-free Pr
                    <jats:sub>6</jats:sub>
                    O
                    <jats:sub>11</jats:sub>
                    -doped NaNbO
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    -BaTiO
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    -SrZrO
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    composition near the morphotropic phase boundary. This material also delivers exceptional charge-discharge capabilities, including a power density of ~254.7 MW/cm
                    <jats:sup>3</jats:sup>
                    , a discharge energy density of ~1.4 J/cm
                    <jats:sup>3</jats:sup>
                    , and an ultrafast discharge rate below 30 ns. Multiscale structural analyses reveal that mixed-valence Pr
                    <jats:sup>3+</jats:sup>
                    /Pr
                    <jats:sup>4+</jats:sup>
                    effectively disrupts the long-range ferroelectric ordering, promoting the formation of highly dynamic and polymorphic polar nanoregions. The electricfield response of these polar nanoregions is further constrained by local defect dipoles arising from Pr-induced charge imbalances, which delays polarization saturation while suppressing hysteresis. In addition, the Pr-doping-induced grain refinement, together with a wide bandgap inherited from the NaNbO
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    matrix, synergistically enhances dielectric breakdown strength. Collectively, the synergy between domain refinement and constrained polar dynamics enables the concurrent optimization of W
                    <jats:sub>rec</jats:sub>
                    and η, offering a broadly applicable strategy for designing advanced dielectrics for capacitive energy-storage applications.
                  </jats:p>

title: “We firmly expect to see a further increase in power density”
Codebase release 1.0 for HEPTAPOD
items.abstract: <jats:p>Many workflows in high-energy-physics (HEP) stand to benefit from recent advances in transformer-based large language models (LLMs). While early applications of LLMs focused on text generation and code completion, modern LLMs now support orchestrated agency: the coordinated execution of complex, multi-step tasks through tool use, structured context, and iterative reasoning. We introduce the HEP Toolkit for Agentic Planning, Orchestration, and Deployment (HEPTAPOD), an orchestration framework designed to integrate external LLMs into general HEP workflows spanning theoretical calculations, simulation, and data analysis. The framework enables LLMs to interface with domain-specific tools and to construct and manage diverse HEP pipelines while preserving transparency, reproducibility, and human oversight. To demonstrate these capabilities, we present a representative case study in the context of a Beyond the Standard Model (BSM) Monte Carlo signal validation that spans model generation, event simulation, and analysis within an established, reproducible workflow. HEPTAPOD provides a structured and auditable layer between human researchers, LLMs, and computational infrastructure, establishing a foundation for transparent, human-in-the-loop systems.</jats:p>

title: A permissioned blockchain-based transactive architecture for smart contract-driven P2P energy trading in prosumer communities
items.abstract: <jats:p xml:lang="en">The growth of distributed renewable generation has increased the number of prosumers who both generate and consume electricity. This paper proposes a permissioned blockchain architecture for peer-to-peer (P2P) energy settlement in prosumer communities. A structured review of 62 peer-reviewed studies published between 2015, and June 2026 informs the design. The architecture combines a private Ethereum network using Quorum Byzantine Fault Tolerant (QBFT) consensus, four interacting smart contracts, a multi-oracle metering bridge, and a network-feasibility oracle operated by the distribution system operator (DSO). Its contributions are interval-level energy allocation with controls against double assignment, shared-capacity accounting across concurrent contracts, a specification for four forms of oracle redundancy, a smart-contract state-transition model covering normal and error paths, and a token-flow model that reconciles payments and collateral under normal delivery, surplus, shortfall, DSO curtailment, and oracle timeout. The evaluation comprises a synthesis of the coded literature, security threat modelling, and an illustrative settlement reconciliation. Empirical performance evaluation is deferred to a companion testnet study.</jats:p>

title: Where Are Poland’s Agricultural Biogas Plants? Livestock Density and Municipal Context
items.abstract: <jats:p>Are agricultural biogas plants in Poland more common in municipalities with high livestock densities? We linked the October 2026 register of the National Support Centre for Agriculture with livestock data from the 2020 Agricultural Census and municipal characteristics from 2025. We mapped registered presence across 2479 municipalities and fitted logistic regression models to 2004 municipalities with complete data. Registered plants were more common at higher pig stocking densities: 18.4% of municipalities in the highest decile had a registry entry, compared with 7.6% in the estimation sample. For cattle, the upper-quartile share (7.8%) was close to the overall share, and cattle density was not statistically significant after adjustment for other municipal characteristics. Registered presence was also associated with larger municipal area and lower population density. Both quadratic and spline models indicated increasing predicted probabilities at higher pig densities, while the pattern at very low densities depended on model specification. Livestock maps can help identify areas for further assessment, but project decisions require evidence on collectible feedstock, supply across municipal boundaries, and site feasibility.</jats:p>

                      Self-propagating high-temperature synthesis (SHS) has emerged as a promising alternative to conventional solid-state and carbothermal reduction methods for producing aluminum oxynitride (γ-AlON), a transparent polycrystalline ceramic known for its outstanding optical and mechanical properties. This review presents a comprehensive overview of the development of SHS-based routes for AlON synthesis over the past two decades, ranging from early combustion of aluminum powders in air to more advanced chemically activated processes capable of producing phase-pure powders suitable for transparent ceramic applications. The review first examines the thermodynamic and kinetic features of aluminum combustion in air, which provide the foundation for understanding the counterintuitive formation of nitrides and oxynitrides in an oxygen-containing atmosphere. A key issue in this field is the stoichiometric limitation of the Al–Al

Several strategies developed to overcome this challenge are discussed, including thermally coupled SHS with external heat supplied by “chemical fovens”, combined centrifugal casting–SHS process based on highly exothermic thermite-type reactions involving CrO

title: A Concise Review of Catalytically Active Materials Produced via Self-Propagating High-Temperature Synthesis
container-title: International Journal of Self-Propagating High-Temperature Synthesis
items.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>More than half a century has passed since the advent of self-propagating high-temperature synthesis (SHS) [1]. During this period, numerous SHS-based methods have been established for fabricating both structural and functional materials, including catalytically active systems. Although recent reviews [2–5] have outlined the principal synthesis strategies and catalytic performances of SHS-derived materials, the field continues to advance rapidly, and many new studies have emerged in recent years. The present review therefore aims to systematize and summarize these latest developments in SHS preparation of catalytic materials and to evaluate their performance across a broad spectrum of chemical processes.</jats:p>

title: Investigation of quantum chemical parameters of hemp (Cannabis sativa) components (CBD, CBN, THC) using density functional theory (DFT)
items.abstract: <jats:p xml:lang="en">The hemp plant holds significant importance in various fields such as industry, medicine, and chemistry due to its rich and potent chemical composition. In this study, the electronic properties of three major phytocannabinoids found in hemp (Cannabis sativa)-cannabidiol (CBD), tetrahydrocannabinol (Δ9-THC), and cannabinol (CBN)-were examined in detail using density functional theory (DFT). The electronic structures of CBD, THC, and CBN were theoretically analyzed via the DFT method, and their reactivity potentials and quantum parameters were evaluated based on the highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) and lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO) energy levels. It was determined that the energy gap between the HOMO and LUMO orbitals, which governs electron transfer, decreases in the order CBD–THC–CBN (5.59, 5.13, and 4.82 eV). The findings indicate that the CBD, THC, and CBN molecules possess high stability. These theoretical descriptors provide valuable insights into the potential biological interactions and applications of hemp-derived compounds.</jats:p>

title: From energy crisis to solar boom: the political economy of decentralized clean energy transition in Pakistan
items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Since 2022, Pakistan has experienced a rapid surge of rooftop solar photovoltaic (PV) adoption as households and businesses increasingly shift toward distributed solar systems to reduce dependence on the national grid. This unprecedented shift raises critical questions for energy governance, energy system sustainability, and energy justice, particularly regarding how distributed, user-driven innovations can reshape a clean energy transition beyond formal policy and planning frameworks. The paper examines the drivers of this solar power boom through an integrative political economy framework combining market, socio-technical, and governance dynamics. It draws on 38 semi-structured interviews with policymakers, representatives of regulatory bodies, electricity utilities, solar businesses, industry experts, and think tanks, alongside documentary analysis. The study offers a distinctive explanation of how distributed, people-led solar adoption can drive rapid transformation and reshape established electricity systems in a large developing country such as Pakistan, despite structural and institutional constraints.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Our findings show that rising tariffs, declining grid reliability, and governance inertia combined with falling global solar PV prices and affordable equipment imported from China have accelerated solar PV adoption in Pakistan. Informal market practices, alongside formal net-metering arrangements, have shaped this transition. However, the transition has generated uneven socio-economic outcomes and new distributional tensions associated with partial grid defection. The findings further reveal growing tensions between rapidly expanding distributed solar PV systems and existing regulatory frameworks, cost recovery and grid operations in Pakistan’s electricity sector. These tensions highlight emerging governance and equity challenges for sustainable energy transitions in Pakistan, with broader implications for the Global South.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The paper contributes to debates on sustainable energy transitions in the Global South by advancing an integrative political economy perspective on decentralized clean energy systems. It demonstrates how interactions among market pressures, socio-technical diffusion, and institutional dynamics can simultaneously disrupt incumbent energy regimes and reproduce underlying infrastructural dependencies in the processes of clean energy transition. This underscores the need for adaptive policy frameworks and inclusive governance approaches that integrate distributed energy systems into national policy and planning frameworks.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

A Note on the Spillover of Geopolitical Risks in Nigeria Into Global Energy Markets
items.abstract: <jats:p>This study investigates whether domestic geopolitical risks in Nigeria extend into global energy-related uncertainties. To fulfil this objective, it employs time-varying Granger causality tests covering the period from January 2012 to October 2022. Observable spillovers are identified during significant events such as the EndSARS protests, herdsmen attacks, and the kidnapping of Chibok schoolgirls. These findings illustrate how Nigeria’s geopolitical turmoil impacts not only the country’s oil production and local economy but also the global energy markets. The results indicate a feedback loop where Nigeria’s geopolitical challenges amplify uncertainties around the world’s energy supply, which can further compromise Nigeria’s internal security.</jats:p>

title: SPATIAL ASSESSMENT OF PUBLIC TRANSPORT ACCESSIBILITY USING POPULATION DENSITY AND GIS-BASED SERVICE RADIUS ANALYSIS IN URGENCH CITY, UZBEKISTAN
items.abstract: <jats:p>Public transport accessibility is a key determinant of sustainable urban mobility, yet rapid population growth, urban expansion, and increasing motorization can create spatial mismatches between residential demand and transit service coverage. This study addresses the problem of unequal pedestrian accessibility to public transport in Urgench, Uzbekistan, by assessing the spatial coverage of Route 4 bus stops in relation to population distribution. The methodology combines GIS-based population-density mapping, demographic cartography, and circular buffer analysis using 300 m and 500 m pedestrian service radii. Spatial overlay analysis was used to compare territorial and population coverage under the two accessibility standards and to identify densely populated areas with insufficient access. The results show that the 300 m radius covers approximately 569.6 ha and provides a more comfortable walking distance, whereas the 500 m radius expands coverage to approximately 970.4 ha but requires longer pedestrian trips. Several densely populated neighborhoods, including parts of Toza bog, Manguberdi Umid, Gulchilar, Olma bog, and Kohna qala, remain partially outside the 300 m accessibility zone, indicating a need for improved bus-stop distribution and pedestrian connections. The study’s contribution is an integrated, transferable GIS-based framework that links population density with transit service coverage to identify priority areas for accessibility improvement. The findings provide practical guidance for urban transport planners in Urgench and comparable medium-sized cities in Central Asia and other developing regions, supporting evidence-based decisions on bus-stop location, pedestrian infrastructure, and sustainable mobility planning.</jats:p>

title: Memory-based metaheuristic optimization for loss minimization and voltage stability in radial distribution networks using crow search algorithm
items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This study investigates the optimal placement and sizing of distributed generation (DG) units in radial distribution networks using a crow search algorithm (CSA) integrated with the backward/forward sweep (BFS) load-flow method. A multi-objective optimization framework based on a weighted-sum formulation is developed to minimize active and reactive power losses, voltage magnitude deviations, and steady-state voltage-angle deviations while satisfying bus-voltage, line thermal, DG capacity, and installation constraints. The performance of CSA is comparatively evaluated against particle swarm optimization (PSO), differential evolution (DE), and the grey wolf optimizer (GWO) through 30 independent runs under identical computational budgets on the IEEE 33-bus test system, with additional validation on the IEEE 69-bus system. For the IEEE 33-bus network, considering three DG units operating at a 0.95 power factor and a combined capacity of 1500 kW, CSA identifies buses 13, 25, and 30 as the optimal installation locations. The resulting configuration reduces active power losses from 202.68 to 70.06 kW and reactive power losses from 135.14 to 47.58 kVAr, corresponding to reductions of 65.4% and 64.8%, respectively. Furthermore, the minimum bus-voltage magnitude improves from 0.9131 to 0.9500 p.u., while the minimum static voltage stability index increases from 0.695 to 0.815. Comparative results indicate that all four algorithms identify practically equivalent best solutions. CSA achieves feasible solutions in all 30 independent runs, whereas PSO fails to produce feasible solutions in five runs. Nevertheless, DE and GWO demonstrate slightly better mean objective values than CSA, with improvements of 0.4% and 0.3%, respectively, indicating that CSA is competitive but does not establish overall superiority. A 1000-sample Monte Carlo assessment further reveals the sensitivity of the optimized configuration to variations in load demand and DG output, with the minimum voltage remaining at or above 0.95 p.u. in only 4.3% of the simulated scenarios. The observed voltage-angle deviations remain within approximately 1.1° and are interpreted exclusively as steady-state performance indicators rather than evidence of dynamic stability. Overall, the findings demonstrate that CSA provides a reliable and computationally competitive approach for DG allocation in radial distribution networks, although its performance should be assessed against alternative metaheuristic algorithms and under realistic operating uncertainties.</jats:p>

title: Orbit-Density Membership Functions Induced by Group Actions and Their Measure-Theoretic Extension
