Breast Cancer Diagnosis Using Machine Learning Algorithms: A Comparative Study of SVM and Random Forest
items.abstract: <jats:p>Breast cancer diagnosis is a useful setting for evaluating machine-learning classifiers because the cost of missing a malignant case is much greater than the cost of sending a benign case for additional examination. This paper compares a Support Vector Machine (SVM) and a Random Forest (RF) on the Wisconsin Diagnostic Breast Cancer (WDBC) dataset, which contains 569 cases described by 30 numerical cell-nuclei features. The data were divided into an 80% training set and a 20% test set. For the reproducible version of the experiment, the split used random_state=72, and the SVM features were standardized using statistics learned from the training data only. On the 114-case test set, RF achieved 96.49% accuracy and 93.02% recall for malignant tumors. SVM achieved 95.61% accuracy but a higher malignant recall of 95.35%. RF missed three malignant cases, whereas SVM missed two. The comparison therefore does not produce a single best model for every criterion: RF makes fewer errors overall, while SVM is slightly better at avoiding missed cancers. Correlation analysis also shows strong redundancy among size-related variables, especially radius, perimeter, and area. These results suggest that malignant‑class recall and feature multicollinearity should be core considerations in model comparison instead of secondary observations.</jats:p>

title:
Friction-Resistant
Cracking Sensor with Machine-Learning-Assisted
Signal Classification for Human–Machine Interfaces
items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Crack-based flexible sensors have considerable potential in intelligent robotics and human–machine interfaces, but weak adhesion between conductive metal films and stretchable elastomers can limit their durability during practical use. Here, we develop a friction-resistant cracking sensor combining interfacial embedding and conductive networks of polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) doped with carbon nanotubes (CNTs) and a metal silver (Ag). The sensor is constructed by thermally evaporating Ag nanoparticles onto semicured CNT-doped PDMS elastomer. The semicured interface produces a broader Ag distribution at the Ag-PDMS boundary, while the CNT network provides secondary conductive pathways after extensive cracking of the Ag film. The sensor combines these interfacial embedding, redundant CNT conduction pathways and vacuum-evaporation-based metallization to improve friction resistance. The Ag/CNTs@PDMS sensor exhibited an electrical working range of approximately 23.6%, compared with approximately 12.8% for Ag/PDMS, and remained electrically conductive after 500 frictions. The sensor was integrated into a soft robotic gripper to distinguish five sphere-size classes. A bidirectional gated recurrent unit (BiGRU) with temporal attention pooling achieved 89.95% test accuracy for size classification. The same model architecture was evaluated separately on a six-class surface electromyography (sEMG) data set and achieved 95.3% accuracy. The latter result demonstrates the applicability of the temporal classifier to a different signal modality rather than cross-domain generalization of the strain sensor. This study combines material design with temporal signal classification for flexible tactile sensing in robotics and human–machine interfaces.</jats:p>

title: A Hybrid Rule-Based and Machine Learning Framework for Detecting Data Quality Anomalies in Electronic Health Records
items.abstract: <jats:p>Data quality anomalies in electronic health records, including impossible values, unit errors, inconsistent fields, copied-forward results, calibration drift, and duplicates, corrupt research, quality measurement, and the machine learning models built on the data. Rule-based checks are transparent and precise but cover only what has been written down, while learning-based detectors can find the unexpected but are opaque and need labels. This paper presents a hybrid framework in which rules act as high-precision detectors, as features for a learning layer, and as a source of weak labels; an isolation forest and a gradient-boosted classifier cover the gaps that rules leave; a fusion step ranks records under a review budget; and reviewer feedback drives active learning and rule maintenance. We evaluate the framework on a synthetic EHR data set of 30,560 records with eight classes of injected anomaly, using a time-based split.......</jats:p>

Beyond Euclidean: A Conceptual Review of Distance Metrics and Dissimilarity Measures in Contemporary Machine Learning
items.abstract:
<jats:p>This paper presents a broad conceptual review of distance metrics and dissimilarity measures fundamental to the field of Machine Learning (ML). While ubiquitous algorithms like k-nearest neighbours, clustering methods, and support vector machines heavily rely on measuring similarity, the default choice of the Euclidean distance often obscures a deeper, application-specific consideration of data geometry. We aim to provide a broad perspective across diverse data types and domains, moving from classical vector norms to covariance-aware, angular, temporal, topological, probabilistic, image-based, and manifold-aware measures. Beyond a simple catalogue, we address several theoretical implications in the ML pipeline. These include the relationship between distance metrics and positive definite kernels, distance metric learning as a subfield dedicated to learning task-specific metrics, latent space fidelity as a way to analyse what distances in low-dimensional latent spaces reveal about semantic separation in the observed space, induced metrics arising from feature maps and learned representations, identifiability of distances as an advanced perspective on latent geometry, and computational complexity aspects. Ultimately, this paper argues that researchers and practitioners should critically evaluate the underlying geometric assumptions in their models, and that the selection of the appropriate distance metric is, in fact, an explicit modelling decision.

Keywords: distance metrics, dissimilarity measures, similarity learning, machine learning geometry, metric learning</jats:p>

title: Integrating machine learning with blockchain consensus: a scalable and secure Proof of Anomalous Transactions (PoAT) approach
items.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study presents a Proof of Anomalous Transactions (PoAT)-based consensus mechanism that combines machine learning-based transaction filtering with a hierarchical blockchain consensus to enhance scalability, security, and liveness. To the best of our knowledge, this is a novel approach that directly integrates machine learning into the core blockchain consensus process.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>An imbalance-corrected LightGBM model with SMOTE (Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique) was applied to label incoming transactions as valid, uncertain, or anomalous before block inclusion. Valid transactions are prepared for block formation by filtering anomalous transactions and generating verifiable proofs using a machine learning-based assessment process. According to this filtering phase, transactions are forwarded through a region-based parallel consensus structure, where distributed regional validators perform Byzantine fault-tolerant voting, cross-region verification, and global leader endorsement to guarantee reliable consensus. All classification and consensus decisions are ensured to be integrity-preserving through cryptographic proof generation and hash-based verification.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The experimental results indicate that the selected model achieved an F1-macro score of 0.9468 and an AUC (Area Under the ROC Curve) of 0.9916 for the anomaly detection. Analytical evaluation indicates a traffic-weighted transaction-processing latency of 5.40 ms and an upper-bound throughput scalability estimate from 185 transactions per second (TPS) per region to 1,850 TPS across 10 concurrent regions. Analytical evaluation suggests that the proposed PoAT framework, which is fortified by a multistage hierarchical verification mechanism and incorporates machine learning-based fraud detection, has the potential to accommodate up to 111,000 transactions within a single block during a 1-min block interval. A practical deployment using a FastAPI backend and React-based user interface further demonstrated the real-time applicability and usability of the proposed framework in a real-world scenario.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>These findings suggest that PoAT is a smart, secure, and scalable consensus model that is suitable for future blockchain systems.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: ANALISIS PREDIKTIF KESENJANGAN KOMPETENSI MENGGUNAKAN MACHINE LEARNING DENGAN INTEGRASI PURPOSE DAN COBIT
items.abstract: <jats:p>Konvergensi teknologi Industri 4.0 dan otomasi global telah menimbulkan pergeseran mendasar pada struktur permintaan pasar tenaga kerja sehingga diperlukan pemetaan kesenjangan kompetensi yang komprehensif dan antisipatif. Penelitian ini menyajikan kerangka analitis yang mengintegrasikan algoritme Machine Learning (Support Vector Machine, Random Forest, dan BERT) dengan Natural Language Processing untuk analisis kompetensi tenaga kerja secara prediktif, yang diimplementasikan dalam kerangka tata kelola TI COBIT 2019. Dengan fokus pada Kabupaten Bandung, Jawa Barat—tempat industri tekstil menyumbang 52% terhadap PDRB regional dan menyerap 1,8 juta pekerja dengan tingkat pengangguran 6,2% (232.000 jiwa)—penelitian ini mengevaluasi kerentanan struktural melalui data sensus empiris dari 116 pemangku kepentingan internal (pegawai Disnaker, staf TI SI-MASDA, dan instruktur BLK). Hasil penelitian menunjukkan kesenjangan signifikan: kapabilitas sistem saat ini (M=3,50/5,00) dibandingkan kebutuhan Dashboard AI/ML (M=4,45/5,00), dengan kesenjangan 0,94 poin, sementara kematangan tata kelola COBIT mencapai Level 3+ (M=3,90/5,00). Kesiapan implementasi tergolong tinggi (M=3,94/5,00) dengan prioritas utama meliputi analitik Big Data (M=4,76), percepatan pencocokan pekerjaan (M=4,74), dan aksesibilitas mobile (M=4,71). Kerangka yang diusulkan menyediakan analisis CV otomatis, prediksi kesenjangan kompetensi secara real-time, dan jalur pembelajaran yang dipersonalisasi, selaras dengan rencana strategis RPJMD 2025–2029. Temuan ini memposisikan Kabupaten Bandung secara baik untuk penerapan AI berbasis tata kelola dan memungkinkan transisi yang adil menuju green jobs, pertanian cerdas, serta ekosistem kerja jarak jauh.Kata kunci: Machine Learning, Kesenjangan Kompetensi, COBIT 2019, Tata Kelola TI, Natural Language Processing.</jats:p>

title: End-to-end deep learning versus machine learning for biomarker discovery in cancer genomes
items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Accurate determination of genomic biomarkers from tumor sequencing is fundamental to precision oncology. In practice, biomarker inference relies on computational pipelines that compress high-dimensional data into predefined summaries that may not fully capture the complexity of cancer genomes. Deep learning (DL) offers an end-to-end alternative by learning features directly from raw genomic data. However, clinical translation remains limited by insufficient validation and systematic comparisons with established machine learning (ML) baselines, particularly in real-world settings. Here, we compare state-of-the-art DL with ML on mutation data using microsatellite instability (MSI) and homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) prediction as oncologically relevant tasks. We aim to derive practical guidance on mode​ling strategies across data modalities and sequencing contexts.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      We trained supervised and self-supervised DL encoders alongside ML models using single nucleotide (SNVs) and copy-number variants (CNVs), and their multimodal combinations from TCGA, CPTAC, GENIE, and GeneseeqPrime
                      <jats:sup>®</jats:sup>
                      cohorts (
                      <jats:italic>n</jats:italic>
                       = 5,365). Model performance was evaluated across whole-exome (WES), pseudo and real panel datasets using confidence intervals and clinically motivated operating points. We benchmarked against established MSI and HRD tools, assessed calibration and applied explainability analyses.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>For MSI, DL and ML demonstrated similar generalization on WES data (PR-AUC 1.00 vs. 1.00). DL maintained comparatively high performance under (pseudo-) panel settings, with performance affected by cross-assay variability. For HRD, multimodal integration was the primary determinant of predictive performance, while DL and ML achieved similar external performance (PR-AUC 0.83 vs. 0.84). In panel-based settings, DL retained an advantage over ML (PR-AUC 0.94 vs. 0.89), while panel-specific training improved discrimination performance for both approaches. Comparisons with MANTIS/MSIsensor and HRProfiler/SigMA showed broad concordance, with tool-specific scores capturing related but distinct signals. Model interpretation indicated that both DL and ML relied on mutational patterns consistent with established biomarker biology.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Overall, predictive performance depended strongly on data availability and sequencing context. With information-rich inputs, DL generally matched classical ML, whereas the clearest advantages emerged in cross-assay and data-sparse settings. The best-performing DL models were lightweight and interpretable. With assay-specific calibration and independent validation, these models could provide complementary computational readouts from routine sequencing data.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Biochemical-descriptor-based machine learning for predicting liquid yield from fruit and nut processing residues
items.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Converting fruit, nut, and seed processing residues into liquid biofuels is limited by the high cost of experimental screening across diverse feedstocks. Although machine learning (ML) is widely used to model biomass pyrolysis, most studies rely on proximate analysis and random train - test splits, which overestimates predictive accuracy on unseen food-industry by-products. Here, we tested whether ML models trained on common agricultural and forestry residues can predict bio-oil yields from fruit and nut wastes, and assessed how feedstock composition affects transferability. We trained Linear Regression, Random Forest, and Multilayer Perceptron models on a harmonized dataset (n = 720) combining elemental composition, cell-wall biopolymers (cellulose, hemicellulose, lignin), proximate data, and operating conditions. Models were evaluated using both an 80/20 stratified split and out-of-distribution (OOD) testing on unseen fruit, nut, and seed residues, alongside single-core CPU training times. Random Forest achieved the highest in-distribution accuracy (R
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                    = 0.76, MAE = 4.88 percentage points) with low computational cost, but all models lost substantial accuracy under OOD transfer (AR
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                    = -0.25 to -0.40; OOD MAE = 8.3 - 10.1 percentage points). Permutation importance identified temperature, lignin, cellulose, and ash as the main predictors. These results define quantitative error margins and show that general pyrolysis models require local experimental recalibration before use on food-processing residues.
                  </jats:p>

Machine Learning-Aided Prediction of Compressive Strength Degradation in UHPC Exposed to Elevated Temperatures
items.abstract: <jats:p>Recently, Machine Learning (ML) has become an essential tool in materials research due to its ability to analyze complex datasets, identify hidden non-linear relationships, and support data-driven decision-making. Accurate prediction of post-heating residual compressive strength (Fcu) after cooling to ambient temperature is critical for ensuring structural safety and promoting sustainable infrastructure development under elevated temperatures; however, this remains challenging when using conventional empirical formulas, given the highly non-linear and interactive effects of mixture composition and thermal exposure, which motivates the use of data-driven ML approaches in this study. Seven ML algorithms (Random Forest (RF), Gradient Boosting Machine (GBM), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGB), Categorical Boosting (CATB), Gaussian Process Regression (GPR), Support Vector Regression (SVR), and Artificial Neural Network (ANN)) were applied to predict the compressive strength of Ultra-High-Performance Concrete (UHPC), using a dataset of 464 laboratory-tested specimens reported in previously published studies (112 unique mixtures across 25 studies) parameterized via unit-consistent matrix mass fractions, hierarchical binder and aggregate sub-ratios, fiber volume fractions, and governing mix ratios without requiring pre-measured ambient strengths. Among all models, CATB achieved the best predictive performance, with a testing Coefficient of Determination (R2) of 0.917, Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) of 13.45 MPa, Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 9.44 MPa, and Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) of 8.01%, while maintaining strong leakage-free generalization under 5-fold mixture-grouped cross-validation (Group K-Fold) (R2 = 0.892 ± 0.033), outperforming the remaining six models. Model interpretability via SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and two-way three-dimensional partial dependence plots (3D PDPs) identified exposure temperature as the most influential factor, with degradation initiating at 350 °C and acceleration markedly beyond 600 °C, followed by steel fiber (STF) and supplementary cementitious material (SCM) dosages. Specifically, a steel fiber volume fraction of 2.0–3.5% yielded the highest positive marginal contribution within the investigated dataset. Finally, the CATB model was deployed into a dedicated graphical user interface (GUI) and validated against an independent external experimental study, delivering a reliable, rapid decision-support tool for fire-resilient UHPC mix design without requiring preliminary ambient strength testing.</jats:p>

title: Near-Infrared Spectroscopy Coupled with Machine Learning for Predicting Multiple Soil Properties Across Land-Use Types and Environmental Zones
items.abstract: <jats:p>Near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy combined with machine learning offers a rapid and cost-effective method for large-scale soil characterization. However, how this approach performs across diverse land-use types and environmental zones at the national scale remains poorly understood. This study conducts a systematic evaluation of five machine learning algorithms for predicting 14 key soil properties, using the Austrian NIR soil spectral library. The analysis assessed the robustness of partial least squares regression (PLSR), elastic net (EN), support vector regression (SVR), random forest (RF), and LightGBM across different land-use types and environmental zones. The results demonstrate that predictive accuracy is highly specific to the target soil property and influenced by its environmental and land-use context. No single algorithm was universally optimal. Overall, PLSR and EN provided the most accurate and robust predictions for the majority of properties, while SVR also performed satisfactorily. In contrast, complex non-linear models generally underperformed, showing a pronounced susceptibility to overfitting in data-scarce contexts. Critically, the relative ranking of algorithms shifted depending on the specific land-use type and environmental zone. This work provides references for deploying NIR spectroscopy with machine learning in national-scale soil assessment programs, revealing that model performance is not uniform across different environmental and management contexts.</jats:p>

title: Quantifying self report bias in machine learning stroke classification from NHANES using Monte Carlo probabilistic bias analysis
items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Machine learning (ML) models for population-level stroke classification increasingly rely on self-reported outcomes from large-scale health surveys, yet the impact of outcome misclassification on reported performance is rarely quantified. We developed an ML pipeline to classify self-reported stroke using 20 routinely measured sociodemographic, clinical, and laboratory variables from 47,696 non-pregnant, examined adults pooled across nine NHANES cycles (2003–2023), of whom 1962 (4.1%) reported that a doctor or other health professional had told them they had a stroke. Imputation was fitted within training data only and applied to held-out rows without refitting. The primary model achieved a holdout AUROC of 0.790 (95% CI 0.769–0.810) and, at a threshold derived from out-of-fold training predictions, a balanced accuracy of 0.649, sensitivity of 0.411, and specificity of 0.887. SHAP analysis identified age, race and ethnicity, education, smoking status, and antihypertensive medication use as the most influential features. We then performed a probabilistic bias analysis over 1,000 Monte Carlo iterations, drawing self-report sensitivity from U(0.36, 0.98) and specificity from U(0.96, 0.996) and reconstructing the latent stroke outcome under nondifferential misclassification. Against the reconstructed outcome, median AUROC was 0.874 (95% simulation interval 0.830–0.911), approximately 0.08 above the naive estimate, with an implied true prevalence of 4.2% (2.3–8.2%) bracketing the observed 4.1%. Estimating latent risk by maximum likelihood without truncation gave a smaller gain (median AUROC 0.847, 0.777–0.907). Performance measured against self-reported labels therefore likely understates discrimination against the underlying outcome under nondifferential error, by an amount that depends on how latent risk is modeled. Digital health researchers should report misclassification-adjusted intervals alongside naive metrics when outcomes are self-reported.</jats:p>

They have a time finding new threats like zero-day attacks, advanced persistent threats, ransomware, phishing schemes and insider attacks. This is because they use methods that look for specific signatures and follow rules.
This paper is proposing a way of keeping our networks safe using Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning. The idea is to use these technologies to look at network traffic and what users are. Benchmark datasets will be used to see how well the proposed solution works. The role of Explainable Artificial Intelligence will also be looked at to make sure the machine learning models are transparent and can be understood. This will help build trust in the system.

title: Carboxymethyl Cellulose‐Based Janus Hydrogels With an Interpenetrated Interface for Stable Machine‐Learning‐Enabled Motion Recognition
items.abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Developing ionic‐conductive hydrogels that combine mechanical durability, stable ion transport, adhesion, and intelligent recognition remains challenging because heterogeneous networks are susceptible to fatigue and interfacial failure. Herein, a carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC)‐mediated Janus hydrogel with an interpenetrated interface was constructed using semi‐curing‐assisted infiltration. A soft ionic‐conductive network provided strain responsiveness, whereas the CMC‐reinforced acrylic acid/acrylamide network supplied load‐bearing capacity and reversible energy dissipation. The optimized hydrogel exhibited an ionic conductivity of 3.98 S·m
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    , tensile strength of 0.93 MPa, fracture strain of 1120%, and adhesion strength of up to 8.55 kPa. Molecular dynamics simulations revealed progressive damage through sacrificial‐bond rupture, delayed gap propagation, and residual bridge‐chain loading. The sensor retained distinguishable walking, jogging, running, and joint‐motion signals after 10 days of storage and maintained stable responses during cyclic deformation at 150% strain for 4500 s. Furthermore, a multichannel sensing system integrated with a machine‐learning model enabled reliable classification of nine hand gestures and real‐time robotic‐hand control. These findings provide an effective materials‐design strategy for durable flexible sensing and intelligent human‐machine interaction.
                  </jats:p>

title: ASSESSMENT OF SELECTED MACHINE LEARNING SYSTEMS IN PREDICTING THE RESILIENT MODULUS OF COHESIVE SOILS
container-title: FUTA JOURNAL OF ENGINEERING AND ENGINEERING TECHNOLOGY
items.abstract: <jats:p>Characterizing subgrade soils in terms of resilient modulus (MR) is crucial for pavement design. However, the process can be expensive and time-consuming, leading to the need for more efficient alternatives. This research investigates the effectiveness of using machine learning systems to predict the resilient modulus of cohesive subgrade soils. A dataset of 400 resilient modulus measurements obtained from in-situ cone penetration tests waere collected, along with an additional 200 prediction data points from past research. The combined dataset were then divided into training and testing subsets and used to develop two machine learning predicting systems: Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Back Propagation Neural Network (BPNN). The performance of these systems was evaluated using the sum of residuals (R) and the Mean Square Error (MSE) performance index. Among the SVM models tested, the one trained with a medium Gaussian kernel demonstrated the best predictive capability. For the BPNN, the most effective configuration included four input variables, fifteen hidden neurons, and thirty-three epochs. The BPNN system outperformed the SVM system, yielding higher predictability with training and testing R values of 0.98 and 0.92, and MSE training and test values of 19.84 and 90.16, respectively. In contrast, the SVM system produced training and testing R values of 0.92 and 0.72, with MSE training and test values of 47.75 and 223.73. This research demonstrates that machine learning systems can accurately predict the resilient modulus of soils, providing acceptable error levels for pavement design and construction.</jats:p>

title: Advanced Surface Coatings for Biosensors: A Review of Atmospheric Plasma Innovations
items.abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Biosensing relies on the precise engineering of the bio‐interface to achieve good performance (e.g., sensitivity, working range, stability) in complex samples. Despite their favorable properties, metals, polymers, carbon nanotubes, and paper remain challenging biosensing substrates due to surface inertness, biofouling, and poor biomolecule adhesion. Wet‐chemical modification can address these limitations but is frequently hindered by multi‐step protocols, chemical waste, and substrate‐specific constraints. This review demonstrates plasma as a versatile, more sustainable, and dry‐state alternative for the advanced (bio)functionalization of biosensor surfaces. Atmospheric plasma is discussed as a universal toolkit for creating high‐performance interfaces, including bioreceptor immobilization, engineered roughness, anti‐biofouling layers, and stabilization for shelf‐life by depositing tailored ultra‐thin films to enhance biosensor performance, essential for the next generation of biosensors.</jats:p>

title: Radiation monitoring in the scattered field of a clinical electron FLASH beam with Timepix4
items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>FLASH radiotherapy is an emerging technique, delivered at
  ultra-high dose rates, that holds promise for improving the
  treatment of certain cancers. Resolving the pulse structure of the
  beam is a major challenge in the primary field, where the extreme
  particle flux prevents accurate pulse-resolved measurements. Even in
  the scattered field, few instruments provide the precision required
  for radiation protection and beam monitoring. Single-particle
  counting detectors offer a way forward: the Timepix family of hybrid
  pixel detectors records each particle interaction individually, with
  its time of arrival and time over threshold. This work reports a
  first evaluation of a Timepix4 assembly bonded to a 300 μm
  p-on-n sensor in the scattered field of a clinical electron beam,
  inside and outside of the treatment room, at the Mobetron facility
  (CHUV, Lausanne), using a 9 MeV beam delivered at conventional
  (∼ 0.5 Gy/s) and high (30–230 Gy/s) dose rates. Individual
  beam pulses were resolved and counted in both modes, with repetition
  frequencies consistent with the machine settings. Within high dose
  rate pulses, progressive data loss from readout saturation distorts
  the recorded pulse shape, so the intra-pulse profile is not
  reliable, while pulse counting and timing are unaffected. Outside
  the treatment room, where passive dosimeters record only background,
  individual pulses were still resolved in high-dose-rate mode. These
  results establish Timepix4 as a viable pulse-resolved detector for
  radiation protection and out-of-field monitoring in FLASH RT,
  reliably resolving pulse timing and counts even at dose levels below
  what passive dosimeters can register.</jats:p>

                    <sub>6</sub>
                    hollow cathode DC plasma source for plasma ion-assisted electron beam deposition of optical coatings
container-title: Journal of Physics D: Applied Physics
items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    The Plasma Deposition Source (PDS) is a gridless source for plasma ion-assisted deposition (PIAD) of electron beam evaporated optical coatings. PDS geometry, electrical and water-cooling feedthroughs provide a retrofittable configuration to most vacuum deposition chambers. The PDS utilises an inductively heated (100 kHz) LaB
                    <jats:sub>6</jats:sub>
                    hot hollow cathode, providing large-surface-area thermionic emission of a DC glow discharge at low vacuum pressure in the deposition chamber (typically 2 × 10
                    <jats:sup>−4</jats:sup>
                    mbar). The PDS incorporates a pressure differential between axially separated cathode and anode regions, with typical pressures of 2 × 10
                    <jats:sup>−3</jats:sup>
                    mbar and 2 × 10
                    <jats:sup>−4</jats:sup>
                    mbar, respectively, providing enhanced LaB
                    <jats:sub>6</jats:sub>
                    hollow cathode performance, self-sustaining plasma operation and reduced substrate heat loading and particulate contamination from the cathode. Retarding field energy analyser and Langmuir probe plasma diagnostic measurements and Monte Carlo simulation are described and used to characterise and optimise plasma output and establish fundamental understanding of PDS operation. The PDS provides an optimal ion energy range (5–50 eV) and enhanced ion current density (ICD; ∼0.4 mA cm
                    <jats:sup>−2</jats:sup>
                    at 90 cm distance from the PDS to substrates) suitable for PIAD of densified amorphous optical thin films. Controllable PIAD over an extended deposition area is achieved using a tuneable magnetic field provided by a solenoid formed axially on the exterior of the anode assembly. Automated PDS control is described, providing stable output of plasma ion energy and current density. PIAD of densified single TiO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    and SiO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    layers (typical deposition rates of 0.6 and 0.7 nm s
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    , respectively) is demonstrated as a function of PDS parameters and plasma ion adatom arrival rate. The influence of the impinging plasma ions is shown to be a thresholding process, where a minimum ICD is required to achieve film densification with a typical ion-to-deposited adatom ratio of ⩾1.2. PIAD of an 11-layer TiO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    /SiO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    multilayer notch filter with no spectral drift over an extended substrate deposition area is also demonstrated.
                  </jats:p>

title: Dissociated orientation biases of local gamma oscillations and cross‐laminar delta‐gamma coupling in mouse primary visual cortex
items.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      Gamma‐band neural oscillations are implicated in sensory feature processing, yet their laminar organization and cross‐frequency coupling in the mouse primary visual cortex (V1) remain poorly defined. Using linear electrode arrays, we recorded local field potentials and multi‐unit activity across cortical layers in lightly anaesthetized adult male C57BL/6 mice during presentation of drifting grating stimuli. We systematically characterize orientation selectivity and phase‐amplitude coupling (PAC). Visual stimulation most strongly drove cross‐laminar PAC involving L6 delta phase (1–3 Hz) and L4 gamma amplitude (25–75 Hz) (hereafter L6–L4 PAC, where the first layer denotes the source of low‐frequency phase and the second layer the source of high‐frequency amplitude), with significantly greater coupling strength for L6–L4 PAC than for the reciprocal L4–L6 PAC. Notably, local gamma power exhibited a robust, consistent vertical preference, whereas L6–L4 PAC showed a significant horizontal bias. Dataset‐level analyses revealed that the vertical preference of gamma originated from consistent clustering of peak directions around vertical, whereas the horizontal bias of PAC emerged from the accumulation of weak, widely distributed individual deviations. These findings reveal a functional dissociation between local gamma oscillations and cross‐laminar PAC in mouse V1: gamma power shows a vertical bias that may carry orientation information, whereas L6–L4 delta‐gamma coupling shows a weaker horizontal bias and may reflect a form of cross‐laminar temporal co‐ordination.
                      <jats:boxed-text content-type="graphic" position="anchor">
                        <jats:graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" mimetype="image/png" position="anchor" specific-use="enlarged-web-image" xlink:href="graphic/tjp70959-gra-0001-m.png">
                          <jats:alt-text>image</jats:alt-text>
                        </jats:graphic>
                      </jats:boxed-text>
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Key points</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      <jats:list list-type="bullet">
                        <jats:list-item>
                          <jats:p>Visual stimulation drives robust cross‐laminar phase‐amplitude coupling (PAC) from layer 6 delta‐phase (1‐3 Hz) to layer 4 gamma‐amplitude (25‐75 Hz), with significantly stronger coupling than the reverse direction (L4 → L6). Local gamma power (25‐75 Hz) exhibits a consistent, depth‐invariant preference for vertical orientations across all cortical layers.</jats:p>
                        </jats:list-item>
                        <jats:list-item>
                          <jats:p>In contrast, L6 → L4 PAC shows a significant horizontal bias, revealing a functional dissociation between local gamma oscillations and inter‐laminar coupling.</jats:p>
                        </jats:list-item>
                        <jats:list-item>
                          <jats:p>Single‐trial analyses show that gamma's vertical preference arises from tight clustering of peak directions, whereas PAC's horizontal bias emerges from weak, scattered individual deviations summing to a population effect.</jats:p>
                        </jats:list-item>
                        <jats:list-item>
                          <jats:p>These findings suggest that local gamma power encodes feature‐specific orientation information, while L6 → L4 δ‐γ coupling provides a stimulus‐engaged, horizontally biased rhythmic scaffold for inter‐laminar coordination.</jats:p>
                        </jats:list-item>
                      </jats:list>
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Exact Norms of the Hilbert Integral Operator on Mellin-Adapted Lorentz–Gamma Spaces
Coefficient of Variation Charts for Gamma Process
items.abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    The coefficient of variation (CV) chart is widely used in manufacturing to monitor processes where the mean fluctuates, and the standard deviation is proportional to the mean. Conventional CV charts assume that the quality characteristic is normally distributed and perform poorly when the data follows a gamma distribution. To address the aforesaid limitation, this study develops the Shewhart CV – Gamma (SH CV – Gamma) chart, to enable the monitoring of the CV for gamma‐distributed processes. The proposed SH CV – Gamma chart is constructed based on the gamma quality characteristic that is transformed into a quality characteristic with an approximate normal distribution using the Wilson‐Hilferty approximation. This study also evaluates the impact of measurement errors through the SH CV – Gamma chart for measurement errors (called SH CV – Gamma ME chart) using two performance metrics, which are the average run length (ARL) and expected ARL (EARL). Numerical results show that a larger gamma shape parameter produces narrower control limits, which reduce the ARL and EARL values. Measurement errors are found to reduce the SH CV – Gamma ME chart's detection ability but increasing the value of the coefficient
                    <jats:italic>B</jats:italic>
                    in the linear covariate error model improves the performance of the SH CV – Gamma ME chart. Additionally, taking multiple measurements (
                    <jats:italic>m</jats:italic>
                    ) has minimal effect in alleviating the influence of measurement errors. A practical example is provided to demonstrate the implementation and effectiveness of the proposed chart.
                  </jats:p>

title: Numerical analysis of bone cell growth potential in beam-based lattice structures
items.abstract: <jats:p xml:lang="en">Porous structures have been shown to possess considerable potential for promoting bone regeneration. This capacity is attributable to the ability of such structures to emulate the mechanical and biological environment of natural bone. These cells have been shown to promote cell adhesion, proliferation, and nutrient transport, which renders them particularly well-suited for applications in tissue engineering. The present study evaluates four beam-based lattice structures -Cubic Body-Face Centered Cubic (CBFCC), Cubic Face-Centered Cubic (CFCC), Kelvin, and Octet Truss- in terms of their geometric and flow-related properties to assess their suitability for bone regeneration. Scaffolds with porosities of 50%, 60%, 70%, and 80% were modeled to investigate the effects of geometry. To this end, numerical analyses were conducted under laminar flow conditions to evaluate permeability, wall shear stress (WSS), and flow velocity. The findings of the study suggest a correlation between increasing porosity and the following outcomes: increased flow inlet areas, reduced pressure drops, and enhanced permeability. The observed scaffold permeability values were found to fall within the range reported for human trabecular bone, thereby supporting effective nutrient transport and metabolic waste removal. WSS analysis revealed that 30.28% to 74.64% of the scaffold surfaces were within the optimal range of 10–30 mPa, which is conducive to bone cell development. The flow velocities remained within physiological laminar limits, thereby ensuring appropriate mechanical stimulation and uniform flow distribution throughout the scaffolds. In summary, the beam-based lattice architectures exhibited a balanced relationship between structural characteristics and flow performance. This study provides a comprehensive evaluation of their potential for bone regeneration and establishes a foundation for future experimental validation.</jats:p>

title: Combined effects of gamma alumina and carbon black nanoparticles on fines migration mitigation and wettability alteration in sandstone reservoirs, culminating in enhanced oil recovery
items.abstract: <jats:p>Nanoparticles are of significant interest in oil production as they not only alter formation wettability but also hinder fines detachment. However, existing literature contains few studies assessing the combined mechanisms of nanoparticles on wettability alteration and fines migration mitigation. In the current study, gamma alumina and carbon black nanoparticles were prepared at an optimum concentration (determined via pH, electrical conductivity, zeta potential, and interfacial tension (IFT) experiments). The applicability of electrical conductivity measurements was thoroughly discussed as supporting measurements alongside zeta potential analyses. Moreover, the performance in wettability alteration under various salinities and temperatures was evaluated by IFT and contact angle measurements. Finally, the impacts of both nanoparticles on shifting the wettability and hindering migration were analyzed using core flooding under conditions promoting fines migration and compared with a designed minimum fines migration stimulation flooding scenario for the crude oil from the Gachsaran oil field. The IFT and contact angle experimental results demonstrated that, in most cases, at the ideal concentration of 500 ppm, elevated temperatures representing the reservoir environment result in lower IFTs and more extensive wettability alterations to water-wet conditions. Moreover, IFT tests at the same nanoparticle concentration across various salinities identified an optimum salinity at which nanoparticles were the most effective, demonstrating a non-monotonic relationship between salinity and nanoparticles’ performance. Furthermore, based on the present findings, it is hypothesized that gamma alumina nanoparticles improve oil recovery through wettability alteration and fines stabilization, and carbon black nanoparticles enhance recovery by wettability alteration from strongly oil-wet to intermediate-wet, yielding recovery factors of approximately 67.15% and 57.21% in distilled water, respectively.</jats:p>

title: Task-dependent predictability of gamma passing rates in stereotactic body radiation therapy using UCoMX plan-complexity features: a patient-group-aware machine learning benchmark
items.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Treatment-plan complexity metrics have been proposed for predicting patient-specific quality assurance outcomes, but their predictive value may depend on the gamma criterion and task definition. This study evaluated the task-dependent predictability of gamma passing rates (GPRs) in stereotactic body radiation therapy (SBRT) using Universal Complexity Metrics Extractor (UCoMX) plan-complexity features.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The retrospective cohort included 206 SBRT plans from 163 patients. Nineteen numerical UCoMX features were evaluated in patient-group-aware nested cross-validation. The benchmark included full-cohort binary classification of G31 (GPR evaluated using the 3%/1 mm criterion) and G32 (GPR evaluated using the 3%/2 mm criterion), continuous G32 regression, and joint G31–G32 endpoint modeling. A secondary exploratory analysis compared clearly separated G31 outcomes, defined as low-GPR (&lt;90%) and high-GPR (≥98%) groups. Predictions were obtained from pooled outer-fold out-of-fold evaluations. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis was performed for the extreme-outcome Logistic Regression model using held-out outer-fold records.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Predictive performance varied across GPR endpoints and task formulations. In the full-cohort analyses, G31 classification achieved a best ROC-AUC of 0.642 (95% CI: 0.563–0.718) and a PR-AUC of 0.710 against a failure prevalence of 0.592, whereas the best G32 classification ROC-AUC was 0.611 (95% CI: 0.527–0.692). Continuous G32 prediction showed limited added value over fold-specific null predictors, with a best learned-model MAE of 3.241 percentage points compared with 3.245 for the training-set median null predictor. In contrast, the exploratory G31 extreme-outcome analysis achieved a pooled outer-fold ROC-AUC of 0.831 (95% CI: 0.716–0.926), with a balanced accuracy of 0.700, sensitivity of 0.567, and specificity of 0.833. SHAP analysis identified prescribed dose, dose-normalized monitor units, leaf travel, and modulation-related complexity measures as leading contributors to model predictions.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The predictive performance of the UCoMX-centered plan-level predictor representation varied across the gamma criteria and task formulations evaluated. While full-cohort prediction at the 95% analytical threshold remained challenging, substantially stronger discrimination was observed for separated G31 outcomes. These findings demonstrate that the combined UCoMX-derived plan-level and treatment-characteristic representation contains meaningful predictive information under specific task formulations and provide a basis for developing more informative GPR prediction models through integration with additional dosimetric, geometric, or delivery-related predictors.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: A novel binder synthesized from low grade slag and calcined glauconite for wastewater treatment and gamma ray attenuation
items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Herein, low-grade slag (LGS) and calcined glauconite (CGL) were used as precursors to fabricate a novel binary hardened cement with enhanced engineering properties. Four mixtures were prepared at LGS-to-CGL mass ratios of 100:0, 90:10, 80:20, and 70:30. The 90:10 blend (AALGS-10% CGL) showed optimum performance, with the highest compressive strength (40.70 MPa) and bulk density (1.89 g/cm³), and the lowest water absorption (11.25%) and total porosity (21.23%). This blend was also applied to methylene blue dye (MBD) removal from contaminated water and showed the highest removal efficiency compared with other mixtures, with adsorption parameters including pH, dosage, contact time, initial MBD concentration, and temperature investigated. Kinetics were best described by the pseudo-first-order model, while equilibrium data fitted the Freundlich isotherm. Advanced modeling indicated a temperature-independent, multi-molecular adsorption mechanism, and thermodynamic analysis confirmed spontaneous adsorption. Gamma-ray attenuation was experimentally validated using Cs-137 (0.662 MeV) and Co-60 (1.173 and 1.332 MeV) sources with a NaI(Tl) detector. Theoretical shielding parameters—LAC, MAC, HVL, TVL, MFP, Z_eff, and N_eff—were computed via Phy-X/PSD and WinXcom over 0.015–15 MeV. At 0.662–1.33 MeV, Compton scattering dominated, with attenuation primarily governed by density and electron density. Fe₂O₃ enhanced photoelectric absorption below 0.1 MeV. AALGS-10% CGL showed the highest shielding efficiency due to its highest density. Accordingly, AALGS-CGL composites show potential as cost-effective and environmentally sustainable candidates for building materials, water remediation, and radiation shielding in nuclear and medical fields, although quantitative life-cycle and economic analyses are required to confirm these advantages, and further application-specific validation is needed before practical use can be recommended.</jats:p>

title: Experimental and theoretical exploration of gamma-ray attenuation in Fe, Co, Gd and Nd at selected photon energies

The mass attenuation coefficient (MAC), linear attenuation coefficient, total atomic cross-section, molar extinction coefficient, half-value layer, tenth-value layer, mean free path, and radiation protection efficiency were determined in this study. The MAC was measured using a well-geometry

The experimental and theoretical MAC values showed reasonable agreement across the selected energy range, with relative deviations within ±8%. The experimental MAC values decreased from 0.2483 to 0.0539 cm
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                    g
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    for Fe, from 0.2986 to 0.0526 cm
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                    g
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    for Co, from 1.7988 to 0.0538 cm
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>

                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                    g
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>

At a fixed sample thickness of 0.5 cm, Gd exhibited the highest RPE in the low-energy range of 122–662 keV, reaching a maximum of 87.6633%, whereas Co exhibited the highest RPE in the higher-energy range of 840–1330 keV, with a maximum value of 33.5426%. items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The astrophysical gamma rays in the MeV energy region have
  not yet been well-explored due to the limitation of detection
  technology in the past decades, and the famous gamma-ray “MeV gap”
  exists. Opening the window of MeV gamma-ray is not only critical for
  the gamma astronomy but also essential for rich frontier researches
  in astro-particle physics, such as detecting light dark matter,
  probing the primordial black hole and better understanding of
  nucleosynthesis. As a pilot experiment of the project for dark
  matter detection in space at Shanghai Jiao Tong University, a
  three-layer Compton camera with the energy resolution better than
  4% and position resolution of ∼1 mm is developed utilizing the
  novel scintillators. Here we show the design, detailed calibration
  and validation results of the novel Compton camera, and demonstrate
  its good ability of MeV gamma-ray source imaging for the upcoming
  in-orbit mission.</jats:p>

Failure-Mode-Based Health Assessment of Major Power Equipment in MVDC Converter Stations
items.abstract: <jats:p>Medium-voltage direct current (MVDC) converter stations integrate conventional power equipment and power-electronic components with distinct failure and degradation characteristics, making unified health assessment challenging. This study proposes a failure-mode-based health assessment method for major MVDC converter-station equipment. Major equipment is selected through risk priority number (RPN) analysis, while equipment health is independently evaluated using failure mode and effects analysis (FMEA), cross matrices, and condition indicators. The relationships between equipment failure modes and condition indicators are systematically established using FMEA and cross matrices. The selected indicators are classified into five condition grades using indicator-specific thresholds, and a folding function is applied to determine a representative health index (HI) by prioritizing the most severely degraded indicator. The proposed method is evaluated using 10 transformer cases derived from fault and condition assessment datasets and five submodule cases constructed from independent IGBT and capacitor accelerated degradation datasets. The transformer results generally exhibit assessment trends comparable to existing condition assessments, although differences are observed in certain cases. The submodule results demonstrate that degradation information from different components can be integrated into a representative HI under the constructed degradation scenarios. These findings demonstrate the applicability of the proposed framework to heterogeneous condition indicators and provide a basis for extending health assessment to other MVDC converter-station equipment.</jats:p>

title: HPLC-HRMS Identification of Antibiotic Degradation Products in Food Matrices After Exposure to E-Beam Irradiation
items.abstract: <jats:p>(1) Background: Recently, the widespread use of antibiotics has led to increased levels of their residues in natural aquatic environments, livestock waste, and food products. (2) Methods: This study presents an experimental investigation into the degradation of tetracycline and chloramphenicol in aqueous solutions and food matrices (milk, chicken, and honey) upon exposure to 7.5 MeV accelerated electrons at the doses of 0, 1, 3, 7, 10, and 20 kGy, using high-performance liquid chromatography coupled with high-resolution mass spectrometry (HPLC-HRMS). (3) Results: It was found that electron-beam irradiation of aqueous antibiotic solutions at the doses of 3 kGy and 10 kGy resulted in the removal of 98–99% of tetracycline and chloramphenicol, respectively, starting from initial concentrations of 20 mg/L. The behavior of the antibiotics differed significantly in food matrices. Chloramphenicol degradation rate constants were close in values in different food matrices and comparable to those observed in water. (4) Conclusions: HPLC-HRMS analysis revealed five degradation products for tetracycline and six for chloramphenicol in irradiated aqueous solutions, which exceeds the number of antibiotic degradation products identified in food matrices.</jats:p>

items.abstract: <jats:p>This study examines the effects of primary electron beam transverse profiles and nonideal phase space parameters on the STCF positron source. Geant4 simulations, combined with an analytical acceptance model for the adiabatic matching device, are used to evaluate the positron yield and peak energy deposition density for Gaussian and uniform beam distributions. The results show that a uniform beam provides no significant advantage over a Gaussian beam. Parameter scans further indicate that multiple Coulomb scattering in the conversion target largely suppresses the influence of microscopic angular deviations, rendering the initial beam divergence negligible for positron capture. The source is also robust against transverse orbit errors, with an allowable misalignment of 0.5 mm. These results provide quantitative guidance for the STCF positron source design and for future experimental studies at the Beam Test Platform.</jats:p>

A Customizable Open-Source HBM Controller
container-title: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
items.abstract: <jats:p>High-Bandwidth Memory (HBM) has become a fundamental component in high-performance computing, artificial intelligence acceleration, and networking, offering unmatched bandwidth and energy efficiency. However, the development of optimized HBM-based architectures is hindered by the proprietary nature of existing HBM controllers, which restricts configurability, transparency, and the ability to explore novel memory management strategies. This paper presents an open-source HBM controller designed to address these limitations by providing a configurable and flexible alternative to proprietary solutions. The proposed controller enables fine-grained memory command scheduling, dynamic bandwidth allocation, and workload-specific optimizations while maintaining compatibility with FPGA-based architectures. Moreover, we introduce a combined hardware/software approach to verification and validation, leveraging software-assisted profiling and debugging techniques to streamline performance analysis, correctness verification and integration in realistic settings. In addition to detailing the architecture and implementation, the paper discusses the challenges encountered during design and verification, highlighting key lessons learned that can aid practitioners working on similar projects. Hence, this work also serves as a reference for engineers and researchers aiming to build custom HBM controllers or optimize memory subsystems in FPGA-based designs. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed controller achieves competitive performance while providing the configurability and transparency required for advanced research and real-world deployment.</jats:p>

The Role of Gamma
Irradiation in Tailoring Carbon-Based
Catalysts for Oxygen Reduction in Air-Cathodes: A Review
items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Carbon-based catalysts have emerged as promising alternatives to noble-metal electrocatalysts for air-cathodes in metal-air batteries and fuel cells. Their limited intrinsic oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) activity and durability necessitate effective modification strategies. This review examines the role of gamma (γ) irradiation as a postsynthetic modification approach for carbon-based catalysts used in ORR. It discusses irradiation-induced structural and electronic changes, including defect generation, surface functionalization, pore development, and electronic structure tuning. These modifications increase active-site density, facilitate oxygen adsorption, and improve charge-transfer kinetics, leading to enhanced ORR activity, selectivity, and durability. It also highlighted the influence of irradiation dose and processing conditions, emphasizing the need for optimized irradiation parameters to maximize catalytic performance while avoiding structural degradation. A comprehensive assessment of γ-irradiation-driven engineering of carbon catalysts is analyzed for air-cathodes, establishing structure–property–performance relationships and highlighting γ-irradiation as a scalable, environmentally friendly route for developing high-performance ORR electrocatalysts.</jats:p>

Cervical Dentin Thickness in Endodontically Treated Teeth Compared with Healthy Controls and Root-to-Crown Ratio of Treated Teeth: A Retrospective Cone-Beam Computed Tomography Study
items.abstract: <jats:p>Background/Objectives: Cervical dentin thickness (CDT) and root-to-crown ratio (RCR) are associated with the structural stability of endodontically treated teeth. This study compared cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT)-derived CDT between endodontically treated and radiographically intact teeth in a Turkish population and described RCR in the treated teeth. Methods: CBCT scans of 794 endodontically treated teeth and 200 control teeth (2020–2025) were analyzed retrospectively. CDT was recorded as the smallest of four directional measurements on the axial slice at the cementoenamel junction (CEJ); RCR was calculated as root length divided by crown length. Between-group differences (Δ = treated − control) were analyzed with ANCOVA adjusted for tooth type and age; Group × ToothType and Group × Sex interactions were tested. Results: After adjustment (n = 994), CDT was lower in treated teeth (adjusted means 1.351 vs. 1.731 mm; Δ = −0.380 mm, 95% CI −0.458 to −0.303; p < 0.001). The Group × ToothType interaction was significant (p < 0.001), and after Bonferroni correction, significant differences were confined to the four molar tooth types (Δ = −0.704 to −1.031 mm). CDT ≤ 1.0 mm occurred in 20.0% of treated and 4.0% of control teeth. Neither sex nor the Group × Sex interaction was associated with CDT. In treated teeth, mean RCR was 1.409 ± 0.467, and 18.9% had RCR < 1.0; control-group RCR data were excluded because of an atypical distribution. Conclusions: After adjustment for tooth type and age, CBCT-derived CDT was lower in endodontically treated teeth, but significant differences were detected only in molars, where CDT reflects the dentin around the pulp chamber at the CEJ level rather than around individual roots; non-significant differences in other tooth types do not indicate equivalence. Given the cross-sectional design and possible artifact-related bias from root-filling materials, these differences are associations rather than causal effects.</jats:p>

Numerical simulation of sustained secondary electron multiplication in arrayed parallel-plate structures with a resistive layer
items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    To address the demand for sustained high-current beams in
  high-power microwave sources and high-current-density electron-beam
  devices, secondary electron multiplication has been increasingly
  explored for amplifying field-emitted electron beams. However,
  charge accumulation on secondary-electron-emission (SEE) materials
  can distort electric fields and suppress electron multiplication. An
  arrayed parallel-plate particle-in-cell (PIC) electron multiplier
  was investigated using SEE and resistive layers with different
  Al
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    O
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    concentrations. Measured field-emission coefficients
  of a carbon-nanotube cathode and secondary electron yield (SEY)
  curves of Al
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    O
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    films were incorporated into the model. A
  charge-dissipation model describes capacitive coupling between the
  layers and lateral charge transport in the resistive layer. Without
  the resistive layer, sustained multiplication causes nonuniform
  space-charge accumulation in the central region, reducing impact
  energy and suppressing multiplication. With the resistive layer,
  lower permittivity increases surface-potential sensitivity, while a
  larger resistive-to-SEE thickness ratio improves charge
  redistribution and higher conductivity accelerates dissipation,
  maintaining a higher steady-state multiplication level and
  stabilizing output.
                  </jats:p>

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    The availability of the theragnostic isotope
                    <jats:sup>47</jats:sup>
                    Sc in high radionuclidic purity and at activity levels relevant to preclinical research and clinical applications remains a key limitation to its broader medical application. To address this challenge, a proof-of-principle solid isotope harvesting was performed for the first time at the Facility for Rare Isotope Beams. A custom-built isotope-harvesting cassette, consisting of Ta and Al foils, was designed, with Al serving as a catcher material for the secondary beam fragment,
                    <jats:sup>47</jats:sup>
                    Ca. A total of 550 ± 27 µCi of
                    <jats:sup>47</jats:sup>
                    Ca was produced. Subsequent cation-exchange chromatography enabled efficient separation of
                    <jats:sup>47</jats:sup>
                    Ca from the Al matrix, achieving a (96 ± 5)% extraction and yielding
                    <jats:sup>47</jats:sup>
                    Ca with radionuclidic purity of 100%. An adapted
                    <jats:sup>47</jats:sup>
                    Ca/
                    <jats:sup>47</jats:sup>
                    Sc generator method was developed to isolate
                    <jats:sup>47</jats:sup>
                    Sc using extraction and cation-exchange chromatography. The generator provided (88 ± 1)% recovery of
                    <jats:sup>47</jats:sup>
                    Sc in a matrix directly suitable for radiolabeling. L3-based chelators achieved radiolabeling yields of up to 97%, with a molar activity of 100 µCi/nmol. These results demonstrate that solid isotope harvesting provides a viable and scalable alternative route for
                    <jats:sup>47</jats:sup>
                    Ca/
                    <jats:sup>47</jats:sup>
                    Sc production in support of future nuclear medicine applications, while establishing a transferable approach applicable to other radionuclides for scientific and applied research.
                  </jats:p>

title: Speleothem Clumped Isotope Thermometry: Opportunities and Challenges
Neutron lifetime puzzle and Dicke coherence in spontaneous decays
items.abstract: <jats:p>The long-standing discrepancy between beam and bottle measurements of the free-neutron lifetime—known as the neutron lifetime puzzle—remains an open anomaly in nuclear and particle physics. Here, we investigate whether collective quantum synchronization via macroscopic Dicke superradiance can influence free-neutron decay or mediate the relaxation of hypothetical excited neutron states. We show that superradiance is fundamentally obstructed in standard three-body weak beta decay by continuous final-state phase space and fermionic antisymmetrization, and remains inactive in terrestrial ultracold neutron traps due to low particle densities, even within the Koch–Hummel excited-neutron model. Extending this analysis to the primordial plasma prior to Big Bang nucleosynthesis, we demonstrate that rapid [Formula: see text] collisional dephasing and intense thermal photon backgrounds prevent a superradiant purge and instead enforce thermal detailed balance. Consequently, across the entire parameter space unconstrained by terrestrial experiments, an excited neutron state inevitably thermalizes before weak freeze-out, increasing the effective neutron statistical weight and severely overproducing primordial [Formula: see text], thereby excluding the standard realization of the Koch–Hummel hypothesis.</jats:p>

title: Neutron Reflectometry for the Study of Solid–Liquid Interfaces in Lithium-Ion Batteries
items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Neutron reflectometry (NR) has emerged as a powerful, nondestructive tool for probing buried solid-liquid interfaces in lithium-ion batteries (LIBs). Due to the unique interaction of neutrons with atomic nuclei, NR is highly sensitive to light elements (e.g., lithium and hydrogen) and isotope contrast (e.g., hydrogen and deuterium). Additionally, neutrons can penetrate deeply into cell housings. In the studies reviewed here the beam is transmitted through a substrate to avoid the strongly scattering solvent, enabling in situ and operando characterization under realistic electrolyte conditions. In this review, we categorize in situ NR studies as either static (quasi-equilibrium) or operando (time-resolved). Static measurements provide detailed structural information on anode/electrolyte and cathode/electrolyte interfaces. Operando measurements capture dynamic processes, such as solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI) formation/dissolution and intermediate stages during cycling, on timescales of seconds to minutes. This review highlights the unique role of NR in bridging interfacial structure and battery performance and provides a deeper understanding of the solid-liquid interface in LIBs with sub-nanometer resolution.</jats:p>

Alpha decay is found to be the dominant decay channel for

The beta decay and electron capture half-lives are also estimated using the empirical formula of Sobhani and Khalafi (S K Formula). The difference between alpha and β

title: OpenMC Modelling of Neutron Spectra in the EU DEMO HCPB Divertor and Comparison with Reference MCNP Results
items.abstract: <jats:p>This study presents the modelling and analysis of neutron spectra in the European demonstration fusion power plant (EU DEMO) helium-cooled pebble bed (HCPB) divertor using OpenMC. The OpenMC model was developed by converting an existing MCNP geometry model. The converted model was supplemented with material definitions, FENDL–3.2b and ENDF/B–VIII.0 nuclear data libraries, tally settings, variance reduction parameters, and a deuterium–tritium plasma neutron source. Neutron spectra were calculated for ten divertor components containing tungsten, a homogenized W-CuCrZr-H2O mixture, EUROFER, INCONEL alloy, titanium alloy and water. Statistical precision was assessed using median and flux-weighted relative uncertainties, both of which were below 10% in nine of the ten OpenMC regions. The OpenMC spectra were compared with previously calculated MCNP reference spectra. Energy groups with positive MCNP flux and an OpenMC/MCNP ratio not exceeding 20 were retained. Reference-normalized absolute spectral differences ranged from 8.36% to 17.65% in nine regions and reached 58.16% in the small water pipe. Unfiltered results are reported in the appendices. The analysis quantifies component-specific spectral differences and identifies the regions in which statistical precision limits the interpretation of individual energy groups.</jats:p>

title: Millet Production in India with special reference to Assam
items.abstract: <jats:p>This paper is an attempt to study the case of Millet production across districts of Assam, India during the period 2020-22. It also examines the problems faced by Farmers and impact of policies on Millet production. To study the problem, secondary data is collected from the Directorate of millet development, Statistical Organisation. Data collected are analysed using basic statistics and presented through diagrams and tables. Compound annual growth has been used to study the progress of millet production in Assam, India. The study finds that millet cultivation occupies a negligible portion in Agriculture in Assam. However, it has lot of developmental prospects as the environment of Assam is suitable for millet cultivation. Therefore, it has been recommended that government should support the millet growers through subsidy policies and setting appropriate prices. Moreover, policies are also required in the field of infrastructure development and expansion of the market. Policies also recommended training the millet growers so that they can offer more efforts to increase millet production and help in post-harvest management.</jats:p>

title: Groundnut Production and Export Markets in India
items.abstract: <jats:p>This article examines Indian groundnut production and exports from 2016–17 to 2025–26 and assesses Rayalaseema’s role using verified district production records. National production increased from 74.62 to 130.74 lakh tonnes, with the final observation a third advance estimate. Groundnut exports declined from 725,704.34 to 663,809.63 tonnes, while nominal dollar earnings fell from US$811.59 million to US$690.93 million. Indonesia, Vietnam and Malaysia were the largest destinations in 2025–26. An operational eight-district Rayalaseema grouping produced 308,160 tonnes in 2024–25, equivalent to 81.74% of Andhra Pradesh production and 2.58% of national production. These production shares do not establish its export contribution. District export volumes and quantified regional demand could not be verified. The article applies growth rates, compound annual growth, unit values, destination concentration, production shares and weighted yield formulas. It distinguishes measured shipments from potential demand and identifies the origin-linked records needed to calculate a defensible regional export share.</jats:p>

title: Torque lags from magnetic unlocking in neutron stars and gravitational-wave smearing
items.abstract: <jats:p>In canonical twisted-torus models of hydromagnetic equilibrium in neutron stars, the toroidal field is confined to regions where the poloidal field lines are closed. As spindown torques applied at the stellar surface need not be communicated efficiently to such magnetically unlocked regions, toroidal zones or magnetic voids can rotate faster than the electromagnetically braked part of the star. Continuous gravitational radiation from the associated non-corotating quadrupole can therefore be emitted at higher frequencies than poloidal ones to a degree that depends on the diffusive microphysics controlling angular momentum transport. Dissipative processes can suppress long-lived lags, and we estimate the relevant timescales and their sensitivity to microphysics. Nevertheless, we show that a quadrupole component whose pattern speed differs from the observed spin is shifted, or smeared, over a finite frequency band. Single-template or narrowband upper limits therefore constrain only the quadrupole contribution lying inside the searched frequency window, not necessarily the full frequency-integrated quadrupole. Using simple models, we quantify this spectral redistribution over finite observation windows and discuss its implications for continuous-wave searches.</jats:p>

title: A Special Rht-B1 Gene Allele Was Selected and Applied in Xinjiang Winter Wheat Cultivars
items.abstract: <jats:p>Xinjiang is a major wheat-producing region dominated by irrigated oasis agriculture under an arid continental climate, where winter wheat production faces strong regional environmental constraints. Here, we investigated genome-wide selection signatures and haplotype variation in Xinjiang winter wheat cultivars, using a genomic panel of 343 accessions for genome-wide analyses and a phenotypic panel of 406 accessions with field data. Xinjiang winter wheat cultivars exhibited pronounced regional differentiation and a distinct genomic background, with selected SNPs associated with multiple agronomic traits. Private SNPs showed relatively consistent trait associations, whereas enriched SNPs were associated with a broader range of traits related to plant architecture, yield components, and grain quality. Notably, the Rht-B1 locus showed an alternative enrichment pattern: rather than the canonical Rht-B1b allele, two haplotypes that are rare in the other Chinese wheat zones—the r-e-z haploblock deletion and Rht-B1a_6—were enriched in Xinjiang winter wheat cultivars. Both haplotypes were associated with reduced plant stature, and Rht-B1a_6 was additionally associated with higher grain protein content and whole-grain weight. These findings reveal rare genetic variation at the Rht-B1 locus enriched in Xinjiang winter wheat cultivars, suggesting that these variants may expand the genetic diversity available for semi-dwarf breeding and warrant further evaluation for yield and grain-quality improvement, while indicating their possible relevance to regional breeding and adaptation.</jats:p>

title: Thermal effects on stellar neutron capture reactions: a quantum dynamical approach
items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    The neutron capture process plays a vital role in creating the heavy elements in the universe. Astrophysical environments involved in these processes are characterized by two distinct reaction mechanisms: the slow and rapid neutron capture processes. In this work, the slow neutron capture process is described with the time-dependent coupled channels wave-packet (TDCCWP) method that uses both a many-body nuclear potential and an initial temperature-dependent state to account for the thermal environment. To evaluate the role of a mixed and entangled initial state in the temperature-dependent neutron capture cross section, TDCCWP calculations are compared with those from the coupled-channels density matrix (CCDM) method based on the Lindblad master equation. The importance of including temperature in the initial wave-function of the TDCCWP approach is compared to a thermalisation of the reaction rate using a Hauser–Feshbach style approach. TDCCWP calculations indicate a decrease of the n+

Lead Isotope Geochemistry and Alloy Characterisation of Three Eastern Zhou Bronze Swords from the Dadukou Museum, Chongqing: An Exploratory Case Study with Provenance Limits
items.abstract: <jats:p>The coexistence of Ba-style willow-leaf swords and Chu-style rounded-pommel swords in the Three Gorges region is key evidence for Ba–Chu interaction during the Eastern Zhou period. This study examines three Eastern Zhou bronze swords from the Dadukou Museum, Chongqing, determining alloy compositions by portable X-ray fluorescence for two of them and lead isotope ratios by multi-collector inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry for all three, and compares both with published Ba and Chu assemblages. The two swords analysed for composition are copper–tin–lead alloys with elevated tin (means of 19.5 and 28.5 wt%, from five spots each) whose tin and lead contents fall inside the published ranges for the Three Gorges assemblage (n = 21) and differ from the Jiangling Chu swords (n = 4). None of the three objects, however, falls within the empirical range of its comparison group in all five of the ratio expressions used: each lies outside its group in at least two of five, and the verdict on which side reverses when the ratios are normalised to 206Pb rather than 204Pb. The data therefore identify no deposit and no production site, and the results are reported as an exploratory case study, compatible with several scenarios of metal circulation, local casting and object movement. What the study establishes is the alloy type of the two swords analysed for composition and the lead isotope position of all three against the published Ba and Chu data, with the quality of that comparative material stated explicitly.</jats:p>
