title: Agrobiological and ecological determinants of legal regulation in Russian field crop production
items.abstract: <jats:p>This study examines the agrobiological foundations and regulatory framework governing field crop production in the Russian Federation. The research evaluates the alignment between agronomic crop classifications, plant physiology, phytosanitary dynamics, grain quality standards, and statutory requirements. Terminological analysis reveals conceptual overlap between field crop production and adjacent sectors, specifically vegetable growing and meadow management. To eliminate this ambiguity, the study distinguishes between a narrow legal interpretation restricted to grain cultivation and a broad interpretation encompassing all arable field crops. The analysis substantiates the necessity of codifying six biological crop groups alongside the statutory categories of "field crop production activity," "field crop farm" (as a commercial producer eligible for state support), and "field crop enterprise" (as a property complex). Comparative assessment of cultivar ontogenesis, vernalization thresholds, economic thresholds of weed harmfulness, and state quality standards confirms that legal norms must incorporate biological and ecological parameters. Based on these findings, six legislative proposals are formulated to establish producer rights, phytosanitary obligations, and quality requirements within a specialized federal law on field crop production.</jats:p>

title: WHEN CORRECT CODE IS NOT ENOUGH: ASSESSING THE PRODUCTION READINESS OF LLMGENERATED SOFTWARE
container-title: International Journal of Software Engineering & Applications
items.abstract: <jats:p>Large language models (LLMs) increasingly generate executable software, but functional correctness alone does not establish production readiness. This study evaluates GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna across 15 algorithmic and production-oriented tasks using five generations per model-task pair, yielding 225 generated programs plus 15 fixed references. The layered testbed combines nominal and hidden-edge-case checks, moderate and severe production-like stress, metamorphic validation, reference-normalized runtime and memory, structural quality, static analysis, implementation-strategy inspection, and generation cost. All 800 functional and 368 applicable robustness checks passed, while production-stress success fell to 95.16% for Sol, 95.60% for Terra, and 93.38% for Luna. Cross-model stress differences were not significant, but generation cost differed strongly. A Quick Sort case showed more than a 500x runtime spread among behaviorally correct implementations. The results show that production-oriented evaluation must extend beyond pass/fail correctness to include stress behavior, resources, implementation strategy, and cost</jats:p>

title: Upstream factors in recombinant adeno-associated virus production in human embryonic kidney cells
items.abstract: <jats:p>Transient plasmid transfection in human embryonic kidney 293 cells is widely used for recombinant adeno-associated virus production, yet upstream improvements are difficult to compare. We mapped process contrasts and assessed the feasibility of pooling. Five PubMed searches through 21 September 2026 yielded 272 unique records from 472 hits. Of 50 full-text candidates, 47 reports were retrieved and included. Forty-five studies contributed 87 rows from the completed September extraction plus 15 illustrative single contrasts, one from each newly assessed report: 102 rows in total, without complete extraction of those 15 reports. Thirteen rows had calculable approximate intervals. Two, Powers and Park, describe within-run cultures without established between-run precision, leaving eleven at biological-culture or study level, including dependent outcomes. Two independent medium contrasts for volumetric genome titer gave response ratios of 2.17 and 4.18 against study-specific controls. No parameter-outcome stratum met the threshold of three independent comparable estimates, so no pooled effect was calculated. Higher volumetric output sometimes coincided with lower cell-specific productivity, and multifactor processes could not be assigned to one setting. This analysis provides an unpooled evidence map. Single-reviewer extraction, partial extraction of the added reports and three unavailable full texts limit completeness.</jats:p>

Lighting spectrum and riboflavin degradation in food production buildings
items.abstract: <jats:p>When designing food production premises with artificial lighting (warehouses, bottling rooms, maturation rooms, cold storage rooms), the photosensitivity of food products must be taken into account. "Light taste" (goût de lumière) is a photochemical defect of white wines caused by radiation in the range of 370–450 nm. Modern standards for lighting of wine storage facilities, as a rule, regulate only illuminance (lux), but not the spectrum of sources. In this work, the spectral characteristics of three types of luminaires were measured and the rate of riboflavin degradation in a model wine was assessed. It is shown that a cool white LED has the highest sample means of the photochemical risk index and riboflavin degradation (74.4% over 72 h), whereas a warm LED demonstrates the lowest values (9.0% over 72 h); the ratio of the sample means of degradation is 8.3. The differences between the cool LED and the fluorescent lamp in terms of the risk index and riboflavin degradation did not reach statistical significance after correction for multiple comparisons. The correlation between the risk index and degradation for the three real sources is positive (ρ = 1.0 at n = 3), however, at n = 3 it does not reach statistical significance and is regarded as a descriptive tendency. Under the studied conditions, the spectral index descriptively corresponded to the relative degradation of riboflavin; a statistically significant relationship was not established.</jats:p>

title: The Effectiveness of Oxytocin Massage in Increasing Breast Milk Production in Postpartum Mothers : A Literature Riview
items.abstract: <jats:p>Background: Breast milk is the primary source of nutrition for infants and plays an important role in supporting growth, development, and protection against various diseases. However, postpartum mothers may experience problems with breast milk production and flow, particularly during the early postpartum period. Oxytocin massage is a nonpharmacological intervention that may support the milk ejection process and improve breastfeeding. This study aims to identify and synthesize the effectiveness of oxytocin massage in increasing breast milk production and flow in postpartum mothers. This study employs a literature review design. A literature search was conducted via Google Scholar and PubMed using a combination of keywords related to oxytocin massage, breast milk production, postpartum mothers, lactation, and breastfeeding. Studies were selected based on inclusion and exclusion criteria and documented using PRISMA guidelines. A total of 9 studies met the criteria and were included in the synthesis. Most studies indicated that oxytocin massage was associated with increased breast milk production, volume, output, and flow, as well as improved breastfeeding responses among postpartum mothers. Several studies also showed that oxytocin massage combined with other interventions, such as lavender essential oil and the Marmet technique, could support improvements in breast milk production. However, variations were found in sample size, intervention duration, massage techniques, outcome indicators, and additional interventions across the reviewed studies. Oxytocin massage exhibits a relatively consistent pattern of effectiveness in supporting breast milk production and flow in postpartum mothers. Nevertheless, successful breastfeeding is also influenced by proper latch, feeding frequency, maternal psychological well-being, and support from healthcare providers.</jats:p>

title: Contractual Stabilization Clauses and the State’s Regulatory Sovereignty: Reconsidering Production-Sharing Agreements in Light of Environmental and Human Rights Obligations.
items.abstract: <jats:p>The allocation of regulatory risk in petroleum production-sharing agreements is frequently described as a contest between investor certainty and sovereign discretion. That account is incomplete for South Sudan, where petroleum belongs to the people, constitutional petroleum principles expressly require environmental protection and intergenerational responsibility, and the Petroleum Act 2012 subordinates inconsistent contractual terms to applicable law. This article asks whether a contractual stabilization commitment can validly shift the cost of complying with subsequently strengthened environmental and human-rights standards from a petroleum operator to the public. Using doctrinal analysis of South Sudanese constitutional and petroleum law, international investment jurisprudence, and responsible-contracting standards, it distinguishes the enforceability of a contractual promise from a claim to immunity against regulation. It advances the doctrine of reserved regulatory responsibility: stabilization must be interpreted and drafted as a narrowly defined allocation of exceptional commercial risk, subject to non-derogable constitutional duties, proportionate change-in-law procedures, transparent fiscal authorization and effective remedies for affected communities. The article constructs a six-stage test addressing competence, regulatory character, investor-specific assurance, causation, remedy and public-interest scrutiny. Applied to pollution controls, decommissioning, land access, human-rights due diligence and arbitral counterclaims, the doctrine explains how contractual stability may coexist with legitimate expectations without privatizing future lawmaking. Its contribution is not an assertion that all stabilization is invalid, but a method for distinguishing compensable renegotiation risk from ordinary, foreseeable compliance costs and from obligations that no executive negotiator may lawfully bargain away.</jats:p>

title: FACTORS OF RURAL SMALLHOLDER FARMERS’ PARTICIPATION WILLINGNESS IN INTELLIGENT AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION: EVIDENCE FROM SHANDONG PROVINCE, CHINA
items.abstract: <jats:p>With the continuous innovation of information technology, intelligent agriculture has become the direction of agricultural modernisation. This paper conducts field surveys in four prefecture-level cities representing the northern, central, southern and eastern regions of Shandong Province, China. Using a regression analysis model, it analyses the factors that influence rural smallholder farmers’ willingness to participate in intelligent agriculture from the perspectives of individual characteristics, development cognition, production and operation capital, and social environment. The results show that individual characteristics, development cognition, production and operation capital, and social environment factors have a significant positive impact on farmers’ willingness to participate, among which social environment factors have the most significant impact, and changes in the social environment may have an important effect on willingness to participate. The paper also puts forward suggestions on stimulating rural smallholder farmers’ initiative in intelligent agriculture, strengthening policy guidance, improving infrastructure, and improving the organisational structure of rural smallholder farmers. This will help policymakers design more effective incentive mechanisms and support measures to inform policies that encourage the wider adoption of intelligent agriculture and thereby contribute to rural revitalisation.</jats:p>

title: Recombinant human lactoferrin production by Pichia pastoris on cheese whey in Kyrgyzstan
items.abstract: <jats:p>Recombinant human lactoferrin (rhLF) is a high-value glycoprotein with expanding applications in infant formula and functional foods. However, the high operational expenditure (OPEX) driven by refined synthetic fermentation media limits the laboratory-scale, economically viable bioprocess for rhLF production using Pichia pastoris (syn. Komagataella phaffii) GS115 cultivated on deproteinized cheese whey derived from the dairy sector in the Kyrgyz Republic. Laboratory-scale fermentations demonstrated that the nutrient-rich, waste-derived medium supported robust cellular growth and successfully enhanced target protein expression compared to standard glucose control media. A localized techno-economic analysis revealed that while regional liquid waste logistics and enzymatic pretreatment increased the media preparation cost per cubic meter, the superior biological performance of the yeast culture effectively counterbalanced these infrastructural overheads. Ultimately, utilizing regional dairy waste reduced the raw substrate production cost per gram of target protein and significantly increased the overall economic yield index. These metrics demonstrate that integrating regional agricultural byproducts can successfully bridge the gap between laboratory-scale precision fermentation and commercial feasibility in developing Central Asian bioeconomies.</jats:p>

title: Plant glycoengineering for recombinant protein function and reproducible production
items.abstract: <jats:p>Advances in genome editing, pathway reconstruction and site-resolved analysis have broadened plant glycoengineering, but transfer to new proteins and production settings remains unevenly tested. This critical narrative review examines N-glycan occupancy and processing, plant-associated O-glycosylation and reconstructed mammalian-type pathways in land plants and plant cell cultures. We distinguish host glycomes from measurements of purified products and individual sites, and compare structural outcomes with biological function and repeated production. Removal of selected core residues is supported across products and hosts, whereas occupancy, terminal extension and glycan retention remain sensitive to substrate accessibility, pathway organization and production format. Different objectives also require different glycans: matching a mammalian profile, modulating effector activity, prolonging circulation and promoting cellular uptake cannot be treated as interchangeable improvements. Manufacturing evidence distinguishes inherited edits and consistent glycan profiles from recovery of intact, active protein. Mechanistic research, technology development and product development require evidence matched to their different aims. Reliable comparisons therefore require product-resolved measurements, matched comparators and explicit quantification denominators. Gaps remain in coordinated N- and O-glycan control, direct comparisons across unrelated proteins and hosts, and validation of complex pathways over independent production runs. We propose an iterative decision and evaluation framework with separate entry routes for supported and uncertain glycan-function relationships. It guides candidate interventions and product-specific tests without predicting an unknown protein’s optimal glycoform. Shared reporting practices, complementary benchmark proteins and independently tested mechanistic models could make engineering more predictive while defining where product-specific revalidation remains necessary.</jats:p>

title: From genes to food systems through integrated molecular biology and multi-omics approaches in crop and aquaculture production systems
From Sporting Lives to Cultural Identities
container-title: The International Journal of Critical Cultural Studies
items.abstract: <jats:p xml:lang="en">Football functions not only as a sporting institution but also as a cultural site where racial identity, belonging, and social recognition are negotiated. Although existing scholarship has examined race and representation in football, sustained textual analysis of how Black footballers construct cultural identity through autobiography remains comparatively underdeveloped. This study examines John Barnes’s The Autobiography and Ian Wright’s A Life in Football: My Autobiography to investigate how autobiographical narration transforms sporting experiences into narratives of cultural identity and belonging. Employing qualitative textual analysis and comparative close reading, the study draws on Stuart Hall’s theory of cultural identity and representation, Sidonie Smith and Julia Watson’s life-writing framework, and Paul Ricoeur’s concept of narrative identity. The analysis focuses on the construction of the sporting self, Black identity and cultural positioning, and the relationship between sporting experience, memory, and cultural identity. The findings demonstrate that Barnes and Wright employ distinct but related narrative strategies to interpret their sporting lives. Barnes questions the adequacy of public representations attached to his footballing achievements and situates his identity within personal history and cultural belonging. Wright, meanwhile, emphasizes how football provides opportunities for recognition and how past experiences acquire significance through retrospective reflection. Their narratives reveal that cultural identity is neither fixed nor reducible to sporting achievement but continually interpreted through memory, self-representation, and social experience. By reading football autobiographies as cultural and literary texts, this study contributes to life-writing scholarship by demonstrating how autobiographical narration actively constructs and reinterprets Black cultural identity.</jats:p>

title: Production of Authentic Paintings Inspired by Hybridization of Igbo Coral Beads and Hausa Calabash Decoration in Nigeria
container-title: RESEARCH JOURNAL OF HUMANITIES AND CULTURAL STUDIES
items.abstract:
<jats:p>This study produced paintings through hybridization of material culture from two selected African
communities. Hybridization in art happens when material cultures from two or more communities
combine to create new forms. Current contemporary African art has been reported to have
European styles infused. This infusion has been criticized by scholars to lack portrayal of African
identity. Scholars have also argued that authentic African paintings could be achieved when two
or more African material cultures are hybridized. This study aimed at identifying. This study aimed
at identifying Igbo coral beads material culture and Hausa calabash decoration material culture
used in their selected rites of passage and which could be hybridized. After hybridization, new
compositions of material culture were created. This new outcome was used in the production of
paintings. The paintings incorporated the application element and principle of art and design,
such as colour, shapes, rhythm, variety, emphasis, texture, line and geometric patterns inspired by
the collected forms. The resultant paintings confirmed that hybridized designs of Igbo Coral beads
and Fulani calabash decoration could be successfully used as a source of inspiration in the
production of paintings. The results of this study should also enable African artists to develop their
original paintings inspired by material culture from different African communities. This hybridized
process will also promote cultural harmony between selected African communities.</jats:p>

A Deep Learning Parallel Search Method for the Effective Multiplication Factor of the Neutron Diffusion Equation
items.abstract: <jats:p>Calculating the effective multiplication factor (keff) is fundamental to nuclear reactor criticality safety analysis. A parallel search method using a physics-informed neural network (PINN) with a fully connected architecture is proposed. The steady-state neutron diffusion equation is first converted into a pseudo-transient form. The PINN then approximates the space–time neutron flux by minimizing the equation residual and losses enforcing physical constraints. Based on this flux, a fundamental-mode rate is introduced to indicate whether the system is supercritical or subcritical. Accordingly, calculating keff becomes a search for the point where this rate is zero. In addition, a coarse-to-fine interval-search algorithm is used to evaluate candidate values independently across multiple GPUs. Four test cases yield relative errors in keff ranging from 0.03 to 50 pcm. For the 2D homogeneous square case, the relative error in keff is 0.03396 pcm. Under the same material data and boundary conditions, traditional methods yield 0.12522 pcm. With 8 GPUs, independent candidate evaluations achieve a speedup of 7.71 and a parallel efficiency of 96.35%. The resulting parallel implementation combines accuracy and efficiency for calculating keff in neutron diffusion problems.</jats:p>

title: Pre-Halal Certification Barriers in Cosmetic Production: Insights from Brunei’s Female-Dominated Muslim MSMEs
items.abstract:
<jats:p>This study examines the pre-certification barriers encountered by cosmetic Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in Brunei in preparing for halal certification, particularly those related to production readiness and regulatory preparation. While halal certification has become increasingly important within the expanding global halal cosmetics industry, existing studies have largely focused on certification processes rather than the earlier challenges faced by cosmetic producers. Adopting a qualitative approach, data were collected through one-on-one semi-structured interviews with eight local cosmetic producers operating primarily at the micro and small enterprise level (MSMEs). The findings reveal four major themes: limited access to raw materials, absence of manufacturing and laboratory testing facilities, import and export constraints and challenges in maintaining product quality control. The barriers in obtaining halal certification are deemed to interconnect broadly with structural and operational limitations within Brunei’s cosmetic industry. The study further highlights how these challenges particularly affect female-led MSMEs, which dominate the local cosmetic sector. Overall, the study contributes to existing halal cosmetics literature by shifting attention towards the pre-certification stage and emphasizing the importance of reinforcing production infrastructure and regulatory coordination to improve MSME readiness for halal certification.
 
 
   </jats:p>

title: In from the cold: intermediary strategies for sourcing from a stigmatized supply network after a geopolitical shift
container-title: International Journal of Operations & Production Management
items.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>As geopolitical shifts reshape global sourcing, firms increasingly reconsider suppliers in regions previously excluded by sanctions, boycotts and other geopolitical instruments. Such exclusions often leave a lasting stigma, and suppliers in these regions struggle to establish legitimacy as buyers discount their signals. This research examines how supply chain intermediaries undertake legitimation work to overcome suppliers' legitimacy deficits that otherwise deter reintegration.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Design/methodology/approach</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We conduct a longitudinal multiple-case study in the Uzbekistan cotton–textile industry (2019–2026), a revelatory instance of reintegration after the lifting of a global boycott. The three cases are buyer–supplier relationships in this setting, each brokered by the same three intermediaries. We draw abductively on 46 interviews with buyers, suppliers and intermediaries, over 80 h of observations, and 2,231 pages of archival documents.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Findings</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Uzbek suppliers face three legitimacy deficits: cognitive illegibility, pragmatic incompatibility and moral fragility. In response, intermediaries employ three strategies: (1) cognitive bridging to render suppliers comprehensible; (2) network grafting to make exchange workable; and (3) norm cascading to embed global standards into supplier practices so that compliance becomes credible and durable. Together, these strategies move suppliers from exclusion to accepted sourcing relationships with global buyers.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Originality/value</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We extend supply chain geopolitics research to reintegration, showing how a previously excluded region re-enters global sourcing following a geopolitical shift. We theorize intermediated legitimation as the mechanism enabling this, with legitimation work shifting to the intermediary. Contrary to the sequence assumed in prior literature, cognitive legitimacy emerges as the gateway to pragmatic and moral legitimacy.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Biotechnological Production of Bacillus subtilis Lipase and Its Application in an Oil‐Free Cosmeceutical Cream Formulation
items.abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Lipases are versatile biocatalysts with extensive industrial applications, yet their incorporation into dermatological products remains limited due to stability and safety concerns. In this study, a lipase‐producing strain of
                    <jats:italic>Bacillus subtilis</jats:italic>
                    was cultivated; its lipase production was optimized, purified, and biochemically characterized, and incorporated into an oil‐free cosmetic formulation to evaluate its functionality and dermal safety. Production optimization revealed that 1.5% olive oil induced the highest enzyme activity (220.8 U/mL) on day 4, while an initial pH of 6.0 and 1.75% nitrogen supported maximal yields of 159.64 ± 0.22. SDS‐PAGE analysis showed a single band near 19 kDa, indicating enzyme homogeneity. The purified lipase exhibited optimal activity at pH 6.0 (157.73 U/mL) and 37°C (155.88 U/mL), with strong stimulation by Fe
                    <jats:sup>2+</jats:sup>
                    (52.21 ± 0.32 U/mL) and Ni
                    <jats:sup>2+</jats:sup>
                    (19.05 ± 0.28 U/mL), while Zn
                    <jats:sup>2+</jats:sup>
                    and Cd
                    <jats:sup>2+</jats:sup>
                    inhibited activity. The lipase‐based formulation showed higher antioxidant activity than the control, increasing from 13.89 to 16.82 units across 10–50 mL volumes. Patch testing showed a mean irritation score of 0.1, classifying it as nonirritant, and the formulation also exhibited 22.87% tyrosinase inhibition. These findings highlight
                    <jats:italic>B. subtilis</jats:italic>
                    lipase as safe, stable, and effective for oil‐free cosmetic applications.

Discordance Between p53 Immunohistochemistry and TP53 Mutational Analysis in Endometrial Cancer
items.abstract: <jats:p>Molecular classification of endometrial cancer has become necessary to determine treatment options for these patients. p53 is assessed by immunohistochemistry, which can reveal a wild-type or abnormal expression, consisting of overexpression, absence of expression, cytoplasmic expression, or subclonal expression. Given that DNA polymerase epsilon (POLE) will often be sequenced in panels including TP53, some discordance between the immunohistochemical expression of p53 and the mutational status of TP53 can be observed and lead to confusion regarding the correct molecular classification and thus treatment options. Thus, the aim of this review is to present studies exploring this question and provide evidence on how to interpret this discordance.</jats:p>

title: Challenges in leprosy diagnostics
Musculoskeletal Manifestations of Sickle Cell Disease: What the Radiologist Should Know
items.abstract: <jats:p>Objective: To review the musculoskeletal manifestations of sickle cell disease (SCD), using Bahraini patients as an example, and raise awareness among radiologists and non-radiologist physicians of these imaging findings to facilitate early recognition and improve patient outcomes through timely medical or surgical management. Materials and Methods: This review analyzes findings from previous studies on musculoskeletal manifestations of SCD using various imaging modalities, including plain radiography, CT, MRI, and ultrasound. Specific attention was given to marrow changes, avascular necrosis, septic arthritis, osteomyelitis, and other complications. These findings were subsequently identified in Bahraini patients by searching the radiology information system (RIS) at the main public hospital in Bahrain, and representative images were selected for presentation in this review. Results: Musculoskeletal abnormalities in SCD arise from marrow hyperplasia, red marrow reconversion, and extramedullary hematopoiesis. Vaso-occlusive crises can lead to bone infarctions, osteomyelitis, and septic arthritis, which present unique diagnostic challenges. Pediatric patients often develop sickle cell dactylitis, while spontaneous hematomas are less common but have significant complications. Conclusion: Early recognition of SCD-related musculoskeletal manifestations is crucial for accurate diagnosis and effective management. Radiologists in high-prevalence regions must familiarize themselves with these findings to contribute to comprehensive, multidisciplinary treatment strategies that optimize patient outcomes.</jats:p>

A Comparative Evaluation of Multi-Architecture Ordinal Learning for Five-Class Diabetic Retinopathy Grading: Ensemble Performance and Explainability Analysis
items.abstract: <jats:p>Background/Objectives: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a major cause of diabetes-related vision loss. Accurate five-class severity grading remains challenging due to class imbalance, the ordered nature of disease severity, and visual similarities between adjacent grades. This study evaluates a multi-architecture ordinal learning framework combining SwinV2, EVA-02, and ConvNeXtV2 with Consistent Rank Logits (CORAL)-based classification. Methods: The models were trained on multiple retinal datasets using Ben Graham preprocessing and APTOS-specific fine-tuning, while four-view test-time augmentation was applied during held-out test inference. Equal-weight soft voting, learned weighting, and stacking were evaluated using out-of-fold (OOF) predictions and nested validation. Performance was assessed through class-specific metrics, ordinal error analysis, and qualitative explanations using Grad-CAM and LIME. Results: The three-model ensemble achieved an OOF Macro-F1 of 0.7419 and Severe-class F1 of 0.5046. Under nested validation, equal-weight soft voting achieved a Macro-F1 of 0.7368 and Severe-class F1 of 0.4880. On the held-out APTOS 2019 test set, the ensemble achieved a Macro-F1 of 0.7263 and Severe-class F1 of 0.4058, compared with 0.7304 and 0.4286 for EVA-02, respectively. Paired bootstrap comparisons showed no statistically significant differences in these test metrics. Error analysis showed that 83.1% of incorrect OOF predictions differed by one severity grade, while 98.5% differed by no more than two grades. The CORAL–Softmax comparison was limited to EVA-02 using a single random seed. Conclusions: The held-out test contained only 39 Severe images, limiting the precision of class-specific estimates. Overall, the findings highlight the importance of rigorous ensemble validation and class-specific evaluation for DR grading.</jats:p>

title: Molecular Testing in Oncocytic (Hürthle Cell) Bethesda III/IV Thyroid Nodules: A Systematic Review and Diagnostic Test Accuracy Meta-Analysis
items.abstract: <jats:p>Background/Objectives: Oncocytic (Hürthle) cell-predominant indeterminate thyroid nodules challenge molecular testing; oncocytic-specific accuracy has not been pooled. The objective is to estimate the benign call rate (BCR), diagnostic accuracy and alteration-specific malignancy risk of molecular tests in oncocytic Bethesda III/IV nodules. Methods: PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science and Cochrane Library were searched from January 2010 to October 2026 for studies with extractable FNA molecular-testing data for an oncocytic Bethesda III/IV subgroup; 75 of 2774 records were included. This study involved a two-round model-assisted screening and extraction, each value verified by investigators; a stratified re-screening sample of 400 excluded records identified no falsely excluded study (0/300 at title/abstract; 0/100 at full text); one dataset per center and period was used; QUADAS-2 and GRADE were used. Results: Bivariate and univariate binomial–normal models estimated the accuracy among the resected nodules (scenario A) and with unoperated test-negative nodules as benign (scenario B). The pooled BCR was 74.2% (95% CI, 67.9–79.6; k = 8 datasets) for Afirma GSC, 59.6% (48.4–69.9; k = 8) for ThyroSeq v3 and 24.7% (20.0–30.1; k = 15) for Afirma GEC. In scenario A, the sensitivity/specificity were 87.5% (76.9–93.6) and 46.5% (36.2–57.1) for GSC (k = 4) and 93.9% (82.9–98.0) and 29.9% (23.4–37.5) for ThyroSeq v3 (k = 9). In scenario B, the specificity was 87.4% (k = 5) and 76.3% (k = 6); NPVs near 99% are upper bounds contingent on unoperated test-negative nodules being benign—if 4% were missed cancers, the NPV would fall to approximately 95%. The pooled malignancy rates were 9% with no alteration, 22% with CNA only and 30% with RAS-like alterations; for TP53/TERT alterations, the crude rate was 68% (17 of 25). The certainty was low to very low. Conclusions: In oncocytic Bethesda III/IV nodules, a negative GSC or ThyroSeq v3 result lowers the malignancy risk, if the unoperated test-negative nodules are benign, whereas a positive result is weakly informative. GSC yields more benign calls and was more specific in indirect comparisons, which may reflect the differences in populations and surgical selection as well as test performance.</jats:p>

title: Steatotic liver disease in cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome
items.abstract: <jats:p>The cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome has reoriented chronic metabolic disease management from organ-specific care toward integrated multisystem risk assessment. Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) commonly coexists with obesity, type 2 diabetes (T2D), chronic kidney disease (CKD), heart failure (HF), and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD); however, a binary classification based solely on the presence or absence of steatosis fails to capture its clinical significance. This review distinguishes intrinsic hepatic heterogeneity from two categories of clinical modifiers. Steatosis, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) activity, and fibrosis define the pathological state of the liver, whereas etiological and genetic factors and the surrounding CKM comorbidity burden modify the interpretation and prognosis of these findings. Fibrosis burden shows the most robust association with liver-related events and mortality and serves as the primary indication for hepatology referral. Etiology and genetics may partly dissociate hepatic from cardiovascular risk, although polygenic risk scores have not demonstrated consistent incremental clinical value. T2D, CKD, and HF substantially alter the overall risk associated with MASLD, while HF-related venous congestion can confound liver stiffness measurements. The 2026 CKM guideline, the 2026 European guideline on cardiovascular disease and CKD, and contemporary hepatology pathways collectively support staged fibrosis assessment and bidirectional cardiovascular and kidney evaluation. Resmetirom and semaglutide improve histological surrogate endpoints in MASH, whereas their effects on hepatic decompensation, liver transplantation, and mortality await confirmation in ongoing long-term outcome trials. Future cohorts and trials should jointly capture hepatic, cardiovascular, and kidney phenotypes and determine whether refined liver phenotyping improves prediction, decision-making, and multiorgan clinical outcomes beyond established CKM models.</jats:p>

title: Evaluating Large Language Models in Interdisciplinary Orthodontic–Periodontal Clinical Decision-Making: A Synthetic Case-Based Comparison with Expert Decisions
items.abstract: <jats:p>Background/Objectives: This study evaluated agreement between structured decisions generated by large language models (LLMs) and expert-based clinical reference decisions in interdisciplinary orthodontic–periodontal decision-making and whether agreement varied across clinical decision domains. Methods: Fifty synthetic multimodal clinical cases integrating orthodontic and periodontal variables were developed. After excluding two cases used for pilot testing and calibration, 48 cases were independently evaluated by three orthodontists and three periodontists to derive expert-based reference decisions. The same cases were evaluated by ChatGPT-5.6, Claude Opus 4.8 High, and Gemini Pro using standardized specialty-specific prompts. LLM–expert agreement was assessed using exact agreement rates and Cohen’s κ, and inter-expert reliability was assessed using Krippendorff’s α. Results: Inter-expert reliability and LLM–expert agreement varied across decision domains. For shared items, exact agreement ranged from 73.5–91.2% for periodontal readiness, 66.7–87.2% for periodontal risk, and 51.4–75.7% for modification of the orthodontic approach. For specialty-specific decisions, agreement was 87.5–89.6% (κ = 0.750–0.792) for orthodontic treatment-plan modification, 78.7–83.3% (κ = 0.739–0.798) for treatment timing, 64.6–75.0% (κ = 0.516–0.552) for periodontal disease control, and 69.6–84.8% (κ = 0.289–0.664) for mucogingival surgery. Models also differed when selecting among multiple interventions. Conclusions: LLM–expert agreement varied across stages of interdisciplinary decision-making, suggesting that domain-specific assessment may be more informative than a single overall metric. Given the synthetic, standardized design, these findings should not be interpreted as evidence of independent diagnostic or treatment-planning performance in real-world clinical settings.</jats:p>

title: HRCT Imaging Phenotypes and Bronchiolocentric Involvement in Connective Tissue Disease-Associated Interstitial Lung Disease
items.abstract: <jats:p>Background/Objectives: Connective tissue disease-associated interstitial lung disease (CTD-ILD) encompasses heterogeneous radiological manifestations that may not be fully captured by conventional predominant HRCT pattern classification. This study aimed to comprehensively characterize HRCT abnormalities in CTD-ILD and explore imaging phenotypes derived from morphological and distributional features, with particular attention to bronchiolocentric involvement. Methods: We retrospectively evaluated 123 patients with CTD-ILD from a single-center registry. HRCT examinations were independently assessed by two thoracic radiologists using a standardized protocol. Imaging phenotypes were explored using multiple correspondence analysis followed by clustering of predefined HRCT features. Associations with pulmonary function, underlying CTD, fibrosis extent, and other external characteristics were subsequently evaluated. Results: NSIP was the predominant HRCT pattern (56.1%), followed by UIP (22.0%) and BIP (12.2%). Three imaging-derived phenotypes were identified and showed significant differences in fibrotic disease extent and pulmonary function, particularly FVC, TLC, and DLCO. The predominant HRCT pattern differed across underlying CTDs. Bronchiolocentric abnormalities were observed across several predominant patterns and CTDs and were not restricted to patients classified as having BIP. Conclusions: CTD-ILD demonstrated substantial imaging heterogeneity extending beyond predominant HRCT pattern classification. Integrated assessment of morphological and distributional HRCT features may provide a more granular characterization of this heterogeneity. The identified imaging phenotypes represent an exploratory framework and should not yet be considered validated classification or risk stratification tools. Their clinical relevance requires further evaluation in larger, independent cohorts, including assessment of inter-reader reproducibility and longitudinal outcomes.</jats:p>

title: Fluorescence polarization patterns by spatial shaping with interfering laser pulse components
items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>We report on polarization patterns generated by spatial laser beam shaping applied on two-photon excited fluorescence of a dye. For this purpose, a focused spatially modulated laser beam component is overlapped with an unfocused Gaussian beam component in common path configuration and the induced fluorescence is recorded polarization dependent. This allows for producing desired spatial polarization light fields and leads to polarization selective fluorescence intensity patterns which can well be visualized. The devised spatial polarization shaping method is prospective for optical and biophotonic imaging applications.</jats:p>

title: Diagnostic Performance of the EfficientNetB4 and YOLOv12 Models in Brain Tumor Detection and Localization in Pediatric Brain MRI Images
items.abstract: <jats:p>Objectives: This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of the EfficientNetB4 and YOLOv12 models in the detection and localization of brain tumors using pediatric brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Methods: This retrospective methodological diagnostic accuracy study analyzed pediatric brain MRI examinations acquired at a university hospital between 2010 and 2024. A total of 460 pediatric patients were included in the study, comprising 230 age- and sex-matched patients with brain tumors diagnosed based on radiology reports and confirmed pathologically, and 230 controls with no evidence of tumors. A total of 1380 T1- and T2-weighted MRI images obtained in the axial, sagittal, and coronal planes were preprocessed and annotated in collaboration with a radiologist. The EfficientNetB4 and YOLOv12 deep learning (DL) models were trained, and their performance was evaluated based on accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, and F1-score. Image processing and analysis were performed using the Python programming language, while image annotation was carried out using the Roboflow platform. Results: In the classification of pediatric brain MRI scans with and without tumors using DL models, the EfficientNetB4 model achieved an accuracy of 97.1%, a sensitivity of 94.9%, a precision of 99.2%, a specificity of 99.2%, and an F1 score of 97%. For tumor localization, the YOLOv12 model demonstrated an mAP50 of 89%, an mAP75 of 76%, an mAP50–95 of 76%, and an F1 score of 88.5%. The average precision (AP) values for the tumor-negative and tumor-positive classes were calculated as 0.98 and 0.88, respectively. During the training process, a decrease in loss values and an increase in validation performance were observed in both models. Conclusions: DL-based approaches have demonstrated high diagnostic performance in the detection and localization of pediatric brain tumors on MRI. The findings indicate that these models have the potential to serve as clinical decision-support tools that can assist radiologists.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    The Plasma Deposition Source (PDS) is a gridless source for plasma ion-assisted deposition (PIAD) of electron beam evaporated optical coatings. PDS geometry, electrical and water-cooling feedthroughs provide a retrofittable configuration to most vacuum deposition chambers. The PDS utilises an inductively heated (100 kHz) LaB
                    <jats:sub>6</jats:sub>
                    hot hollow cathode, providing large-surface-area thermionic emission of a DC glow discharge at low vacuum pressure in the deposition chamber (typically 2 × 10
                    <jats:sup>−4</jats:sup>
                    mbar). The PDS incorporates a pressure differential between axially separated cathode and anode regions, with typical pressures of 2 × 10
                    <jats:sup>−3</jats:sup>
                    mbar and 2 × 10
                    <jats:sup>−4</jats:sup>
                    mbar, respectively, providing enhanced LaB
                    <jats:sub>6</jats:sub>
                    hollow cathode performance, self-sustaining plasma operation and reduced substrate heat loading and particulate contamination from the cathode. Retarding field energy analyser and Langmuir probe plasma diagnostic measurements and Monte Carlo simulation are described and used to characterise and optimise plasma output and establish fundamental understanding of PDS operation. The PDS provides an optimal ion energy range (5–50 eV) and enhanced ion current density (ICD; ∼0.4 mA cm
                    <jats:sup>−2</jats:sup>
                    at 90 cm distance from the PDS to substrates) suitable for PIAD of densified amorphous optical thin films. Controllable PIAD over an extended deposition area is achieved using a tuneable magnetic field provided by a solenoid formed axially on the exterior of the anode assembly. Automated PDS control is described, providing stable output of plasma ion energy and current density. PIAD of densified single TiO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    and SiO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    layers (typical deposition rates of 0.6 and 0.7 nm s
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    , respectively) is demonstrated as a function of PDS parameters and plasma ion adatom arrival rate. The influence of the impinging plasma ions is shown to be a thresholding process, where a minimum ICD is required to achieve film densification with a typical ion-to-deposited adatom ratio of ⩾1.2. PIAD of an 11-layer TiO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    /SiO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    multilayer notch filter with no spectral drift over an extended substrate deposition area is also demonstrated.
                  </jats:p>

title: Beyond Aneuploidy Screening: Opportunistic Detection of Pathogen-Associated Reads from Unmapped Reads in Routine Non-Invasive Prenatal Testing
items.abstract: <jats:p>Background: Routine non-invasive prenatal testing (NIPT) generates millions of sequencing reads per sample, including a fraction that remains unmapped to the human genome and is typically excluded from aneuploidy analysis. We evaluated whether these reads could be repurposed to identify pathogen-associated sequencing signals. Methods: An in-house bioinformatic workflow was applied to a pilot cohort of 2000 prenatal cell-free DNA datasets and subsequently to an expanded cohort of 8595 samples. In the expanded analysis, detection required ≥2 high-confidence pathogen-associated read pairs assigned to the same target pathogen. Six selected samples were further assessed by deep resequencing, and analytical limit-of-detection (LOD) experiments were performed for cytomegalovirus (CMV) and Toxoplasma gondii. Results: In the expanded cohort, 23 of 8595 samples (0.27%) met the analytical detection criterion: CMV (n = 13), parvovirus B19 (n = 3), varicella-zoster virus (n = 3), herpes simplex virus (n = 2), and T. gondii (n = 2). No samples met the criterion for Treponema pallidum. Deep resequencing yielded approximately 33- to 239-fold increases in high-confidence pathogen-associated read pairs, with corresponding signals observed across multiple genomic regions. Sequencing-depth metrics did not differ significantly between samples that did and did not meet the analytical detection criterion after adjustment for multiple comparisons, with negligible to small effect sizes. At the observed LODs, the criterion was met in 20/20 CMV replicates at a nominal input of 250 copies and 19/20 T. gondii replicates at a nominal input of 1 copy. Conclusions: Human-unmapped reads from routine NIPT can be reanalyzed to identify pathogen-associated sequencing signals. These findings support the analytical feasibility of this approach but do not establish maternal infection or clinical diagnostic performance. Prospective studies with orthogonal microbiological testing and linked clinical information are required.</jats:p>

title: Age-Related Sarcopenia: Pathogenesis, Biomedical Concepts, Bioanalytical Challenges and Proteomic Biomarker Discovery
items.abstract: <jats:p>Sarcopenia of old age plays an integral part in the frailty syndrome and reduces the quality of life in a considerable number of aged individuals. This article outlines the biomedical concepts, bioanalytical challenges, intended applications, and diverse issues that hamper the swift clinical implementation of fit-for-purpose proteomic biomarkers of skeletal muscle aging. The pathobiochemical impact of aging on the human skeletal muscle proteome is discussed, and how the age-related loss of muscle mass and decline in contractile strength can negatively affect the neuromuscular system. Since the proper physiological functioning of the muscular system is of central importance for whole-body homeostasis in the senescent organism, the identification of proteomic biomarkers is crucial for improving the efficient and swift clinical assessment of sarcopenia. New biomarker candidates can be helpful to improve differential diagnosis, such as pre-sarcopenia, acute sarcopenia, and severe sarcopenia, the prognosis of sarcopenic progression, and the role of influencing co-factors, such as general lifestyle, physical activity levels, medication, obesity, diabetes, and other chronic comorbidities, as well as therapeutic monitoring of new treatment options to counteract age-related muscle wasting. Suitable tissue and biofluid markers from human studies of sarcopenia are described. Interesting biomarker candidates for screening sarcopenia in tissue samples are contractile proteins and metabolic enzymes, which are indicative of fast-to-slow muscle transitions. Minimally invasive biomarkers include muscle-derived enzymes, carboxy-terminal agrin fragments, irisin, titin fragments, myostatin, fibroblast growth factor, collagen, inflammatory proteins, growth differentiation factors, and apolipoproteins.</jats:p>

title: Admission CT Radiomic Features of Hematoma and Perihematomal Edema, 24-Hour Systemic Inflammatory Indices, and Functional Outcome in Acute Intracerebral Hemorrhage
items.abstract: <jats:p>Background: We assessed whether CT radiomics predicts 24 h systemic inflammatory indices after intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) and improves prediction of functional outcome. Methods: Among 719 patients with spontaneous ICH, 538 had a 24 h blood count with differential. We used repeated nested fivefold cross-validation to predict the systemic inflammatory response index (SIRI) and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio from hematoma and perihematomal edema features. Poor outcome was defined as a 3-month modified Rankin Scale score of 4–6. Results: All inflammatory indices correlated more strongly with outcome at 24 h than at baseline (all p < 0.001). Measured 24 h SIRI had a borderline association with poor outcome (adjusted OR per SD 1.35, 95% CI 0.99–1.83, p = 0.054). The radiomic signature correlated weakly with measured SIRI (mean cross-validated r = 0.28, R2 = 0.03). It was associated with poor outcome in the prespecified model (OR per SD 1.69, 95% CI 1.08–2.65, p = 0.022), but this association was not robust across sensitivity analyses. It was borderline with inverse probability weighting (p = 0.049) and nonsignificant for ordinal outcome (p = 0.084) and 30-day mortality (p = 0.43). The signature derived using the original threefold cross-validation was also nonsignificant in that model. The signature alone discriminated less well than the ICH score (AUC 0.727 vs. 0.792, p = 0.005) and performed similarly to ICH volume plus intraventricular hemorrhage (AUC 0.737, p = 0.54). Adding the signature to the clinical model did not improve discrimination (AUC 0.891 vs. 0.894, p = 0.24) or net benefit. Conclusions: Admission CT radiomics captured little of the variation in 24 h SIRI and added no demonstrable prognostic value beyond established clinical and imaging predictors.</jats:p>

title: ANTI-MÜLLERIAN HORMONE: PHYSIOLOGICAL ROLE, AGE-RELATED DYNAMICS, AND LABORATORY DIAGNOSTICS
items.abstract: <jats:p>This article focuses on anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH), which is used to assess ovarian reserve, select stimulation protocols in assisted reproductive technology programs, and evaluate women with suspected polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) or primary ovarian insufficiency (POI). Based on 18 publications from 2020-2024, the review examines the physiological role of AMH, its age-related dynamics, and laboratory measurement methods. AMH is produced by granulosa cells of growing follicles, inhibits primordial follicle activation, and reduces follicular sensitivity to follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH). Its serum concentration reflects the functional ovarian reserve, namely the pool of small antral follicles, rather than the primordial follicle pool. AMH levels increase from birth to early adulthood and gradually decline until menopause. They are influenced by hormonal contraception, body mass index, and gynecological disorders. AMH levels below age-specific reference values are associated with earlier menopause at the population level; however, they cannot accurately predict its onset in an individual woman. Differences between laboratory assay systems, resulting from the lack of a universal international standard and variations in calibrators, may affect gonadotropin dosing and PMOS diagnosis. The WHO reference reagent 16/190 is compatible with only some assay methods. Until a universal calibrator becomes available, results should be interpreted in the context of the patient&#x27;s age and clinical status, with the same assay method used for longitudinal monitoring.</jats:p>

Metabolic Response on Preoperative [18F]FDG PET/CT as a Predictor of Pathological Complete Response After Neoadjuvant Dual HER2 Blockade: A Multicentre Real-World Study
items.abstract: <jats:p>Background/Objectives: The accurate prediction of pathological complete response (pCR) before surgery could inform surgical planning in HER2-positive breast cancer. We assessed how accurately the change in the primary tumour maximum standardised uptake value (SUVmax) between baseline and preoperative [18F]FDG PET/CT predicts pCR after neoadjuvant chemotherapy with trastuzumab and pertuzumab. Methods: We retrospectively studied 260 patients with stage I–III HER2-positive breast cancer from five centres who had PET/CT within 1 week before neoadjuvant therapy and within 1 week before surgery. The percentage reduction in SUVmax (ΔSUVmax) was analysed as a continuous variable against pCR (ypT0/is ypN0); breast and axillary pCR were secondary endpoints. Incremental value over a prespecified clinicopathological model was assessed with bootstrap optimism correction, and an optimal threshold was explored with the Youden index. Results: pCR occurred in 130 patients (50.0%), and 165 (63.5%) had no residual uptake. ΔSUVmax discriminated pCR with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.68 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.63–0.74; adjusted odds ratio per 10-percentage-point increase in ΔSUVmax, 1.50, 95% CI 1.26–1.77) and raised the optimism-corrected AUC of the clinicopathological model from 0.68 to 0.75. The Youden-optimal threshold was 100% (no residual uptake); thresholds of 89–93% performed almost identically. No residual uptake had a positive predictive value of 64% (80% in oestrogen receptor [ER]-negative [<1%] vs. 52% in ER-positive [>10%] tumours) and a negative predictive value (NPV) of 74%. None of the 12 patients with ΔSUVmax < 30% achieved pCR (NPV 100%, 95% CI 76–100). ΔSUVmax was also associated with breast pCR (AUC 0.69) and axillary pCR (AUC 0.68). Preoperative SUVmax alone discriminated pCR similarly (AUC 0.69), and the baseline scan did not demonstrate additional predictive value beyond it. Conclusions: Preoperative metabolic response adds modestly to clinicopathological factors in predicting pCR after dual HER2 blockade. The absence of residual uptake does not reliably indicate pCR, particularly in ER-positive disease, and preoperative PET/CT cannot replace surgical pathology.</jats:p>

title: Gastric Submucosal Adiposity Associated with Morbid Obesity
items.abstract: <jats:p>Gastric submucosal fat accumulation, also referred to as gastric lipohyperplasia, is an uncommon and poorly characterized histopathological finding that has been associated with obesity and insulin resistance. Although often asymptomatic, extensive accumulation may have clinical significance and should be distinguished from other lipomatous lesions of the gastrointestinal tract. We report the case of a 43-year-old male with morbid obesity (BMI: 46.2) and benign essential hypertension who underwent laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy. Histopathological examination of the gastric specimens revealed preserved corpus mucosa without significant inflammation, intestinal metaplasia, or changes suggestive of a proton pump inhibitor effect. However, extensive accumulation of mature adipose tissue was identified within the submucosa, without significant structural atypia. In the context of the patient’s clinical history, the findings were consistent with obesity-associated gastric submucosal fat accumulation. Previous studies have suggested an association between gastric submucosal fat deposition, increased BMI, and insulin resistance, although its pathogenesis and clinical implications remain incompletely understood. This case highlights an uncommon histopathological finding in a patient with morbid obesity, emphasizes the importance of recognizing submucosal fat accumulation in gastric surgical specimens, and underscores the need to distinguish this entity from gastric lipomas and lipomatosis.</jats:p>

title: Advances in adiabatic rotational and vibrational raman excitation of molecular hydrogen
Tuberculous Lymphadenitis: A Comprehensive Clinical Review of Epidemiology, Diagnostics, and Management
items.abstract: <jats:p>Tuberculous lymphadenitis (TBLN) remains the most prevalent form of extrapulmonary tuberculosis worldwide, accounting for nearly one third of extrapulmonary tuberculosis (EPTB) cases. Its paucibacillary nature continues to challenge clinicians, often mimicking malignant or noninfectious granulomatous diseases and delaying accurate diagnosis. This review synthesizes recent advances in epidemiology, clinical presentation, and diagnostic strategies, with particular emphasis on histopathology and molecular assays. Therapeutic approaches are discussed, including the recognition and management of paradoxical upgrading reactions, which remain a frequent source of clinical uncertainty. By integrating classical pathological features with innovations in nucleic acid amplification and antigen detection, this article provides a comprehensive framework for clinicians and pathologists to improve diagnostic accuracy and optimize patient outcomes.</jats:p>

title: Combined laser irradiation effects at the cutaneous infl ammatory response during tattoo pigment removal (an experimental study)
items.abstract: <jats:p>The authors present results of an experimental study with Wistar rats on the effectiveness of combined laser irradiation at wavelengths 532 nm and 1064 nm for tattoo pigment removal. The aim of this study was to assess morphological changes in the skin and depth of laser light penetration exposure in the discussed combined modality compared to monochromatic irradiation. In the control groups, patients were treated separately with laser wavelengths 532 nm and 1064 nm, while in the experimental group both wavelengths were applied consequently. Histological examination revealed that the combined method gives the deepest penetration (120-150 μm) and nearly complete destruction of pigment in both superficial and deep dermal layers, though it causes a pronounced inflammatory reaction. Monochromatic 532 nm irradiation showed superficial effects (40-70 μm) with pigment retention in deep layers and epidermal atrophy, whereas 1064 nm irradiation demonstrated intermediate penetration depth (80-110 μm) with uniform pigment destruction and minimal damage to surrounding tissues. These findings confirm that the choice of laser therapy should be based on the depth of pigment location and clinical objectives. The combined approach is optimal for complete pigment removal, while monochromatic 1064 nm irradiation may be recommended for cases requiring minimal damage to superficial skin layers.</jats:p>

title: Evaluation of the Sensitivity of a Malaria Rapid Diagnostic Test (Acro Malaria P.f./P.v./Pan Rapid Test Cassette) and pfhrp2/pfhrp3 Gene Deletions in Makenene, Central Cameroon, 2021
items.abstract: <jats:p>Background: Rapid diagnostic tests (RDTs) are used as first line for malaria detection in clinical practice and in surveillance programmes in Cameroon. Most are designed to identify the P. falciparum histidine-rich protein 2 (PfHRP2). False-negative RDT results have several causes, including low parasite density, prozone effect and poor test quality or handling, but also P. falciparum parasites lacking the HRP2 protein following pfhrp2 gene deletion. This study aimed to evaluate the sensitivity of a new HRP2-based RDT (Acro Malaria P.f./P.v./Pan Rapid Test Cassette) and to investigate whether the false-negative HRP2-based RDT results were due to confirmed pfhrp2 or pfhrp3 deletions. Methods: A retrospective analysis was performed on the 406 samples collected in Makenene in the Central Region of Cameroon, between September and October 2021. The P. falciparum PCR-positive samples were tested using the RDT, real-time PCR being used as the reference standard because it also detects submicroscopic infections. Samples that were PCR-positive but RDT-negative were analysed for pfhrp2 and pfhrp3 genes. Results: Of the 406 samples analysed using real-time PCR, 185 tested positive for P. falciparum parasites (prevalence 45.6%; 95% CI 40.6–50.6%). Of these 185 PCR-positive samples, 179 were detected by the HRP2-based RDT, giving a sensitivity of 96.8% (95% CI 94.2–99.3%). Six samples (3.2%; 95% CI 1.2–6.9%) were not detected by the RDT. Of these six false-negative samples, four (66.7%) were pfhrp2-deleted and three (50.0%) were pfhrp2/pfhrp3-deleted. The parasites lacking pfhrp2, pfhrp3 and pfhrp2/pfhrp3 represented four samples (2.2%), three samples (1.6%) and three samples (1.6%) of the 185 PCR-confirmed P. falciparum isolates, respectively. The three isolates with a pfhrp3 deletion were the same three isolates that carried the dual pfhrp2/pfhrp3 deletion; the categories therefore overlap and the percentages are not additive. Conclusions: These preliminary observations suggest that deletions of pfhrp2 and pfhrp3 genes contribute to false-negative HRP2-based RDT results, although the small number of false negatives (n = 6) means these proportions should be interpreted with caution. These figures nevertheless remain low and suggest that HRP2-based RDTs remain valuable for malaria detection in clinical practice and in surveillance programmes in Cameroon.</jats:p>

Numerical analysis of bone cell growth potential in beam-based lattice structures
items.abstract: <jats:p xml:lang="en">Porous structures have been shown to possess considerable potential for promoting bone regeneration. This capacity is attributable to the ability of such structures to emulate the mechanical and biological environment of natural bone. These cells have been shown to promote cell adhesion, proliferation, and nutrient transport, which renders them particularly well-suited for applications in tissue engineering. The present study evaluates four beam-based lattice structures -Cubic Body-Face Centered Cubic (CBFCC), Cubic Face-Centered Cubic (CFCC), Kelvin, and Octet Truss- in terms of their geometric and flow-related properties to assess their suitability for bone regeneration. Scaffolds with porosities of 50%, 60%, 70%, and 80% were modeled to investigate the effects of geometry. To this end, numerical analyses were conducted under laminar flow conditions to evaluate permeability, wall shear stress (WSS), and flow velocity. The findings of the study suggest a correlation between increasing porosity and the following outcomes: increased flow inlet areas, reduced pressure drops, and enhanced permeability. The observed scaffold permeability values were found to fall within the range reported for human trabecular bone, thereby supporting effective nutrient transport and metabolic waste removal. WSS analysis revealed that 30.28% to 74.64% of the scaffold surfaces were within the optimal range of 10–30 mPa, which is conducive to bone cell development. The flow velocities remained within physiological laminar limits, thereby ensuring appropriate mechanical stimulation and uniform flow distribution throughout the scaffolds. In summary, the beam-based lattice architectures exhibited a balanced relationship between structural characteristics and flow performance. This study provides a comprehensive evaluation of their potential for bone regeneration and establishes a foundation for future experimental validation.</jats:p>

title: Nickel-Ion and Polyaniline Co-Intercalation into Layered Vanadium Oxide as Stable Cathodes for Photo-Enhanced Aqueous Zinc Ion Batteries
items.abstract: <jats:p>Layered hydrated vanadates have emerged as promising electrode materials owing to their multivalent redox chemistry and structurally open frameworks. This study developed bifunctional electrodes of polyaniline (PANI) and Ni2+ ion pre-intercalated vanadium oxide (NiVO-PANI), which can simultaneously achieve electrochemical energy storage and solar energy conversion in traditional aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs) and photo-enhanced zinc-ion batteries (PZIBs). The synergistic effect of Ni2+ ions and PANI intercalation not only enhances the stability of the material against dissolution and structural collapse but also optimizes the charge transport kinetics and improves the light response ability. The optimized NiVO-PANI-4 composite demonstrates exceptional cycling stability, delivering 269.7 mAh g−1 at 1 A g−1 and maintaining 87.8 mAh g−1 at 5 A g−1 after 1000 cycles. Through comprehensive ex situ characterization and electrochemical analysis, we explored the charge storage mechanism and reaction kinetics of NiVO-PANI-4. Remarkably, under light illumination, the PZIB system exhibits significantly enhanced electrochemical performance, confirming the successful integration of photoelectric conversion and energy storage functions. This work provides fundamental insights for designing high-performance photoactive electrodes with synergistic optoelectronic and electrochemical properties.</jats:p>

title: Disability in rheumatoid arthritis: capability is the target to achieve
Advances in molecular diagnostics in dermatology: from genomic testing to single-cell and spatial omics
items.abstract: <jats:p>Skin diseases are highly heterogeneous at both the clinical and molecular levels. Traditional diagnostic and therapeutic approaches rely on clinical findings and histopathology. This model cannot meet clinical needs for precise classification, prognosis, and personalized treatment. These needs are especially pressing for genetic, inflammatory, infectious, and neoplastic skin diseases. Molecular diagnostics has evolved from PCR to high-throughput genomic sequencing and, more recently, to single-cell and spatial omics. This evolution is shifting dermatology from morphology-based phenotypic diagnosis toward molecular analysis of tissue ecosystems. PCR, quantitative PCR, and digital PCR provide the foundation for routine targeted molecular testing. Targeted gene panels, whole-exome sequencing, whole-genome sequencing, and metagenomic next-generation sequencing have greatly improved molecular diagnosis. They are especially useful for genetic diseases, difficult infections, and skin tumors. Single-cell omics can resolve cellular heterogeneity and interaction networks among cell subsets within skin tissue. Spatial omics preserves anatomical location information. It reveals the spatial distribution of inflammation and tumor microenvironments. Together, these technologies have generated many mechanistic findings in psoriasis, atopic dermatitis, cutaneous lupus erythematosus, melanoma, and other diseases. However, most remain in basic and translational research. They have not yet been widely adopted in routine clinical practice. Currently, high-dimensional molecular testing faces a gap between technical discovery and clinical translation. Complex omics cannot directly replace traditional pathological diagnosis. Future efforts should improve testing standardization and validate findings in independent multicenter cohorts. They should identify streamlined biomarkers that can meaningfully improve clinical decisions. They should also integrate multi-omics, artificial intelligence, and clinical pathology. These steps will help bring next-generation molecular diagnostics into dermatology practice and advance precision medicine for skin diseases.</jats:p>

title: From Recombinant DNA Assembly to Drug Target Protein Validation: A Review of Biological Engineering Techniques
items.abstract: <jats:p>Target-based discovery requires accurate validation of disease-related proteins as potential drug targets, but identifying proteins associated with disease per se does not guarantee that they could be efficient drug targets. Therefore, this review shows how recombinant DNA technology may aid the target validation process. In this review, researchers first introduce the role of recombinant DNA construction in making candidate target genes experimentally accessible. Then, the contributions of expression systems, purification strategies, affinity tags, biochemical assays, cell-based assays, and structural or computational tools to target evaluation are reviewed. Moreover, the review argues that recombinant DNA technology should not be understood solely as a cloning method but as the starting point for an integrated biological engineering workflow. Each step provides a different type of evidence, from protein production and quality control to molecular activity and cellular relevance. Overall, this paper emphasises the importance of linking gene-level design to protein-level functional evidence to improve the reliability of drug target validation.</jats:p>

title: Artificial Intelligence in Plant Disease Management: Advances in Image Analysis, Spectral Diagnostics and Predictive Modelling
container-title: International Journal of Latest Technology in Engineering, Management & Applied Science
items.abstract: <jats:p>Plant diseases caused by fungi, bacteria, viruses and nematodes continue to threaten agricultural productivity and food security. Conventional diagnosis involves symptom examination, microscopy, pathogen isolation, serological techniques and molecular assays. Although these approaches provide essential diagnostic evidence, they may require specialised facilities, trained personnel and considerable time. Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a promising approach for analysing plant images, spectral signatures and environmental information to support disease recognition and prediction. Deep-learning models have demonstrated high classification performance using plant disease image datasets, while hyperspectral and multispectral imaging offer opportunities for detecting physiological changes associated with infection before visible symptoms appear. Predictive modelling can estimate disease risk using weather, crop and environmental variables. Recent multimodal systems and large language models further extend these applications by combining image recognition with textual and agricultural knowledge. However, performance obtained under controlled conditions does not necessarily translate into reliable field diagnosis. Similar symptoms may arise from different pathogens or abiotic stresses, and AI predictions alone cannot establish pathogen identity or viability. This short review critically examines emerging AI applications in plant disease management from a microbiological perspective, with emphasis on diagnostic limitations, laboratory validation, economic considerations and field applicability. Integrating AI with conventional plant diagnostic methods offers a more reliable approach to disease surveillance and management.</jats:p>

title: Two‐Step Tapering‐Collapse Method Enables Element‐Interdiffused Cladding for Enhanced Laser Amplification in Yb:YAG Single Crystal Fibers
items.abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The development of high‐power single‐crystal fiber (SCF) lasers is critically hindered by the lack of a reliable cladding scheme to confine the optical mode and ensure beam quality. Here, we propose and demonstrate a two‐step tapering‐collapse method for the first time to fabricate a high‐quality cladding on Yb:YAG SCFs based on elemental interdiffusion. This in‐situ formed transition layer with graded elemental composition effectively reduces the abrupt structural and thermomechanical discontinuities at the interface between the core and cladding. Consequently, the numerical aperture of the SCF is significantly reduced from 0.280 to 0.199. In a master oscillator power amplifier configuration, the clad SCF delivers a remarkable 52.1% enhancement in slope efficiency compared to its bare counterpart, accompanied by a substantially improved near‐field beam profile. This work establishes a facile and effective route to high‐performance clad SCFs, offering a promising path to unlock their potential as gain media for next‐generation lasers.</jats:p>

title: Hypolipidemic effects of laser therapy and kinesiotherapy in lipid metabolic disorders (a 3-month follow-up)
items.abstract: <jats:p>In recent years, significant progress has been achieved in  pharmacotherapy (PT) of lipid metabolism disorders (LMD) in patients with coronary artery disease (CAD). In most cases, pharmacotherapy produces a favorable effect; and  target levels of cholesterol and its fractions are achieved. However, hypolipidemic drugs (HLDs) are prescribed for long-term use, and their prolonged administration may cause various adverse effects. In clinical practice, there are patients with LMD who are resistant to hypolipidemic therapy (HLT), in whom the administration of optimal doses of these drugs does not reduce cholesterol and its fractions to target levels, while increased  preparation dose promotes the development of adverse effects. To optimize the treatment of such patients, we combined laser therapy and therapeutic unloading exercises. 58 patients with CAD and LMD resistant to HLT were examined. At the baseline, depending on the treatment modality,  patients were divided into two comparable groups according to their clinical and functional characteristics and maintenance drug therapy: main group (MG) ( 29 patients) received a combination of laser therapy (intravenous laser blood irradiation, ILBI, and cutaneous exposure to infrared laser radiation) and kinesitherapy in the form of therapeutic unloading exercises (TUE);  control group (CG) – 29 patients continued to receive basic medicamentous therapy. Results of data obtained  indicate a significant hypolipidemic effect after treatment  in the main group (1 and 3 months of follow-up); these patients   received ILBI and external infrared laser therapy sessions  in combination with physical unloading  rehabilitation. One and three- month follow-up in  this group showed a significant reduction of total cholesterol (TC by 27.9% and 33.2%, respectively) and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C by 34.0% and 42.6%, respectively) as well as significant increase in high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C by 28.2% and 29.9%, respectively),  significant decrease in the atherogenic index (AI by 51.1% and 57.5%, respectively) and triglyceride levels (TG by 47.1% and 47.7%, respectively). At the same time, no significant changes in the lipid profile dynamics were observed in the control group in 1 and 3 months after the treatment.</jats:p>

title: CRISPR-Cas technology in medicine: advances in therapeutics, delivery, diagnostics and clinical translation
items.abstract: <jats:p>Clustered Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats and CRISPR-associated proteins have revolutionized health sector through specific genome editing, molecular diagnostics, and targeted therapeutics. Numerous CRISPR reviews span monogenic disorders, viral infections, and cancer, however, fast pace advancements in precision editing, delivery, and clinical translation warrant reassessment. Therefore, this review highlights recent developments in CRISPR technologies, including base and prime editing (high-fidelity) HFCas variants, CRISPR activation, RNA editing, and emergent viral and non-viral delivery platforms. It summarizes applications across solid tumors, neurological, cardiovascular, metabolic, hematological disorders and infectious diseases such as malaria, HIV and monkeypox, emphasizing disease modeling, functional genomics and point-of-care diagnostics. Finally, it compares CRISPR delivery platforms, reviews current clinical trials, and discusses key translational challenges and future directions for CRISPR-based diagnostics and therapeutics.</jats:p>
