Target recycling-mediated FEN1-Controlled CRISPR/Cas12a trans-cleavage for sensitive and accurate pulmonary hypertension MicroRNA analysis
items.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Pulmonary hypertension (PH), including PH secondary to chronic renal failure, is a progressive cardiopulmonary disorder with poor outcomes. Circulating microRNAs (miRNAs) are promising noninvasive analytes for biomarker research and disease monitoring; however, conventional miRNA assays require complex instrumentation and thermal cycling, and CHA-coupled CRISPR/Cas12a systems often suffer from error-prone signal transduction, background leakage, and false positives.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We developed a target-recycling-mediated, FEN1-gated CRISPR/Cas12a trans-cleavage assay. A rationally designed dual-loop sensing probe integrates target miRNA recognition, autonomous target recycling, and split-initiator release. FEN1, a structure-specific flap endonuclease, cleaves the “2” flap generated by the SP/SL complex, converting the CHA product into a complete Cas12a activator. This FEN1-mediated gating acts as a structure-selective checkpoint that suppresses nonspecific Cas12a activation by mismatched or incompletely hybridized intermediates, thereby reducing background and improving discrimination of nucleotide mismatches</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The assay achieved a limit of detection of 0.72 fM and a linear range of 1 fM–100 pM, with excellent specificity, recoveries of 97.6–103.2%, high reproducibility, and favorable storage stability. In spiked human serum, the results correlated well with qRT-PCR, supporting matrix tolerance and analytical reliability.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This assay directly addresses the long-standing trade-off between amplification efficiency and specificity in CHA–CRISPR cascades. By combining target recycling with FEN1-gated Cas12a activation, it provides a robust and generalizable platform for miRNA detection and offers a promising technical route for developing miRNA-based tools for PH monitoring and biomarker research.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

HEPTAPOD: Orchestrating high energy physics workflows towards autonomous agency
items.abstract: <jats:p>Many workflows in high-energy-physics (HEP) stand to benefit from recent advances in transformer-based large language models (LLMs). While early applications of LLMs focused on text generation and code completion, modern LLMs now support orchestrated agency: the coordinated execution of complex, multi-step tasks through tool use, structured context, and iterative reasoning. We introduce the HEP Toolkit for Agentic Planning, Orchestration, and Deployment (HEPTAPOD), an orchestration framework designed to integrate external LLMs into general HEP workflows spanning theoretical calculations, simulation, and data analysis. The framework enables LLMs to interface with domain-specific tools and to construct and manage diverse HEP pipelines while preserving transparency, reproducibility, and human oversight. To demonstrate these capabilities, we present a representative case study in the context of a Beyond the Standard Model (BSM) Monte Carlo signal validation that spans model generation, event simulation, and analysis within an established, reproducible workflow. HEPTAPOD provides a structured and auditable layer between human researchers, LLMs, and computational infrastructure, establishing a foundation for transparent, human-in-the-loop systems.</jats:p>

title: Synergistic Interfacial Engineering of Tin Oxide-Based Photoanodes and Electrodes for Photovoltaic and Energy Storage Devices
Confined iodine and accelerated redox kinetics enable high-rate Zn-iodine batteries
items.abstract: <jats:p>Zinc-iodine batteries have attracted considerable attention owing to their high safety and low cost. However, their further development is hindered by the polyiodide shuttle effect and sluggish iodine redox kinetics. Here, we employed a synergistic strategy combining pore size regulation and nitrogen doping to design an iodine-loaded, nitrogen-doped reduced graphene oxide cathode (I2@RGO-3) for enhanced iodine confinement and redox kinetics. The abundant microporous/mesoporous structure of the RGO framework physically confines electroactive iodine species, while the graphitic-N-rich interface facilitates interfacial charge transfer and promotes iodine redox kinetics. The as-prepared I2@RGO-3 cathode demonstrates an outstanding rate capability, delivering a specific capacity of 172.23 mAh g-1 at 0.5 A g-1, and even at a high current density of 20 A g-1, it still retains 110.52 mAh g-1, corresponding to a capacity retention of approximately 64.17%. It also exhibits stable cycling performance over 5,000 cycles. The synergistic strategy of pore size regulation and atomic doping proposed in this contribution provides new insights into the design of high-performance zinc-iodine battery cathodes.</jats:p>

title: Air Stability of Cathode Prelithiation Agents for High‐Energy Lithium‐Ion Batteries: Degradation Mechanisms and Stabilization Strategies
items.abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    High‐energy‐density lithium‐ion batteries are constrained by irreversible lithium loss during the first cycle, which reduces initial Coulombic efficiency and attainable energy density. Cathode prelithiation compensates for lithium consumed by solid–electrolyte interphase (SEI) formation and interfacial side reactions through highly active lithium sources, thereby increasing the reversible capacity of full cells. However, the high lithium chemical potential and reactivity of prelithiation agents promote reactions with atmospheric H
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    O and CO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    , causing active‐lithium loss, surface passivation, and impaired processability. This Review examines the associated degradation mechanisms and stabilization strategies. Air‐induced degradation is classified into two evidence‐supported pathways: hydrolysis and carbonation of binary lithium compounds, and surface‐lithium loss from lithium‐rich transition‐metal oxides, potentially accompanied by near‐surface reconstruction. Stabilization strategies based on protective coatings, bulk‐structure regulation, and intrinsically stable materials are evaluated in terms of environmental isolation, reaction kinetics, and lithium‐donation capability. Remaining challenges include nonstandardized testing, insufficient long‐term durability, and limited manufacturing compatibility. Establishing multiscale structure–property relationships among lithium‐compensation capability, air stability, and engineering performance is essential for practical implementation.
                  </jats:p>

title: “I was very ill … . Am working hard”: Disability and denial in Ernest Hemingway’s letters to his Polish translator
items.abstract: <jats:p>In November 1958 Ernest Hemingway invited his Polish translator, Bronisław Zieliński to spend three days in Ketchum, Idaho. At the age of 44, Zieliński was visiting the United States for the first time in his life, under the auspices of the Ford Foundation. When Hemingway received Zieliński’s first letter and called him back, just a week before the actual meeting, he sensed in the translator a kindred spirit, with whom he could share his passion for literature and hunting. The corpus of personal documents testifying to the friendship between Hemingway and Zieliński, which was cut short by the author’s death, consists of thirty-one surviving letters, notes, cards, and telegrams, as well as Zieliński’s travel diary and numerous photographs. This article focuses on the marginalization of health issues in the correspondence between Hemingway and Zieliński. Disability – both physical and cognitive – is the tip of the iceberg Hemingway repeatedly obscures with accounts of work (that must be done); work thus becomes the antidote to any weakness. Zieliński, for his part, reflects this attitude. The letters show that the novelist was aware of the race against time, but the two correspondents were also racing against the growing paranoia of the Cold War, which appears in their letters as an unnamed and insurmountable global disability that subsumes and overshadows personal challenges of a physical or cognitive nature. Both Hemingway and Zieliński were careful not to reveal too much political opinion in their letters (which might have been read by one or more secret services). Zieliński, however, tends to misinterpret Hemingway’s silence, due to bouts of mental illness, in the context of Cold War hostilities. From today’s perspective, this (mis)reading amounts to politicizing disability and to conceptualizing the Cold War as a form of disability of the global order, incapacitating communication between friends.</jats:p>

title: Electrochemical Study of the Adsorption and Protective Film Mechanism of Siam Leaf Extract on High Strength Low Alloy Steel in Combined Sour and Sweet Corrosive Conditions
items.abstract: <jats:p>Corrosion of high-strength low-alloy (HSLA) steel in oil and gas production systems is a major challenge, particularly under environments containing dissolved carbon dioxide (CO₂) and hydrogen sulphide (H₂S). The combined presence of these corrosive gases can accelerate metal dissolution and compromise the integrity of pipelines and related infrastructure. This study investigates the corrosion inhibition potential of siam (Chromolaena odorata) leaf extract on HSLA steel exposed to combined CO₂–H₂S brine, with emphasis on its electrochemical performance, adsorption behaviour and surface protection characteristics. The inhibitor was evaluated at concentrations of 100, 200, 300, 400 and 500 mg/L against an uninhibited control. Open-circuit potential (OCP), electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) and potentiodynamic polarisation (PDP) were employed to assess changes in corrosion behaviour. Surface morphological examination was conducted using scanning electron microscopy (SEM), while elemental composition and possible corrosion-product phases were considered through energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) and X-ray diffraction (XRD), respectively. The electrochemical results indicated a concentration and time dependent improvement in corrosion resistance, with 400 mg/L producing the most favourable performance. At this concentration, the inhibition efficiencies reached 79.7% and 82.3% based on EIS and PDP measurements, respectively. The OCP shifted to a more positive potential, reaching −579 mV after 120 h, while the charge-transfer resistance increased, indicating improved resistance to interfacial corrosion reactions. A slight reduction in performance was observed at 500 mg/L, suggesting that increased extract concentration did not necessarily result in enhanced protection. The SEM observations further indicated comparatively improved surface preservation at 400 mg/L, supporting the electrochemical findings. The results implies that Siam leaf is a potential plant-derived corrosion inhibitor for HSLA steel in combined sweet and sour corrosive environments. Its application may provide a basis for developing more environmentally considerate corrosion-control alternatives for oil and gas infrastructure.</jats:p>

title: Cyberknife® stereotactic radiotherapy versus hippocampus-sparing whole brain radiotherapy with boost in patients with multiple brain metastases—the CyberChallenge trial (ARO v-2021-05): a study protocol for a prospective, open-label, randomized, two-arm, phase II study
items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Patients suffering from malignancies in advanced stages often develop brain metastases, which limit both the life span and quality of life. Most innovative treatment options are single or multifraction stereotactic radiotherapy (SRT) and hippocampus-sparing whole brain radiotherapy with simultaneously integrated boost to large metastases (HS-WBRT ± SIB) as they are suspected to be beneficial regarding toxicity without compromising efficacy. However, especially in the patient cohort with extensive brain metastases (≥ 4), the literature is extremely sparse. In particular, today it is not clear which patients benefit the most from which treatment option, while quality-adjusted life days (QALD) are regarded as the measure that quantifies benefit most reliably in this study.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      The CyberChallenge trial is a prospective, open-label, randomized, two-arm, phase II study comparing SRT with HS-WBRT ± SIB, each combined with best supportive care. Patients with 4–15 brain metastases without previous irradiation to the brain are included, but no lymphoma or small-cell lung cancer is allowed. The planned sample size is
                      <jats:italic>n</jats:italic>
                       = 192 (96 per group), derived by simulation for a Mann–Whitney
                      <jats:italic>U</jats:italic>
                      test with 80% power at a one-sided significance level of 2.5%. A group-sequential interim analysis with O’Brien-Fleming boundaries, performed once the primary outcome has been observed in 50% of participants, is currently ongoing. The primary endpoint is quality-adjusted life days (QALD), derived from health-related quality of life (EORTC QLQ-C15-PAL) and overall survival. Secondary endpoints include symptom burden, functional independence, radiation side effects, long-term cognitive status, assessment of neuronal networks using navigated transcranial magnetic stimulation (nTMS) and several parameters of oncologic efficacy. An accompanying translational program assesses blood biomarkers.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Discussion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The aim of the CyberChallenge study is to prospectively assess which patients profit the most from which highly innovative radiation technique for multiple brain metastases, taking into account factors such as size and number of brain metastases, tumor characteristics, further tumor therapy and patient characteristics. Quality-adjusted life days (QALD) are regarded as the most relevant outcome for these severely ill patients and are therefore defined as the primary endpoint.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Trial registration</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      ClinicalTrials (NCT): NCT05378633. Registration date: 2022-05-18. Date of enrollment of the first participant: 2022-04-07. Retrospectively registered. Link: Study Details | NCT05378633 | The CyberChallenge Trial How Much is Too Much - What is the Role of Cyberknife Radiosurgery in Patients With Multiple Brain Metastases? | ClinicalTrials.gov.

title: Filling Transition and Microchannel Replication in Injection-Molded High-Flow PFA Microfluidic Chips
items.abstract: <jats:p>Perfluoroalkoxy polymer (PFA) is suitable for chemically resistant microfluidic devices, but complete cavity filling does not necessarily ensure accurate replication of microscale channels. In this study, the filling transition and microchannel replication of injection-molded high-flow PFA substrates were investigated using a three-factor, three-level L9 orthogonal array. Nozzle temperature, mold temperature, and holding pressure were varied, and macroscopic filling was evaluated using projected fill-area ratio and part mass. The actual mold-rib geometry was measured by three-dimensional surface profilometry, and molded channels with nominal widths of 100, 300, and 500 μm were evaluated from optical cross-sectional images. Complete filling was achieved under five of the nine molding conditions, with projected fill-area ratios of 95.74–96.77% and part masses of 1.749–1.757 g. Nozzle temperature had the largest effect on macroscopic filling, followed by mold temperature and holding pressure. Under complete-filling conditions, the opening-width, bottom-width, and depth replication ratios were 77.1–113.2%, 89.6–99.0%, and 83.7–96.5%, respectively. These results show that macroscopic filling and local microchannel replication should be evaluated separately when defining the molding window for PFA microfluidic substrates.</jats:p>

title: Regulation of proton transference for stable and efficient reactive capture of CO2 from air
Energy‐Efficient, High‐Performance Ammonia Decomposition Over Iron Wool Under Magnetic Induction Heating
items.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Ammonia decomposition reaction is one of the main pillars of carbon‐free energy storage strategies using renewable materials and energy resources. However, the full potential of NH
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    as an energy carrier has been largely limited by the high energy requirements and complexity of thermocatalytic systems. In this study, a rational, step‐by‐step design and fabrication of iron wool‐based catalytic systems induced by magnetic induction heating have been developed and demonstrated. Iron wool, a cheap and abundant material, achieved >99% conversion at a temperature of 520 °C, a gas hourly space velocity (GHSV) of 18,000 mL g
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                     h
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    , and specific energy consumption (SEC) of 1.45 kWh/mol H
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    . The formation and propagation of iron nitride species led to structural degradation and reorganization of the iron wool, diminishing its heating efficiency and its catalytic performance during cyclic operations. Mixing iron wool with SiRAlOx‐supported Ni led to full ammonia decomposition at an elevated GHSV of 30,000 mL g
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                     h
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    after only ca. 6 min for temperatures below 470 °C. Furthermore, using SiRAlOx‐supported Ru (1.5–3.3 wt% Ru) resulted in a decreased SEC of 0.73 kWh/mol H
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    while the catalytic stability was largely maintained, as evidenced by a 4%–13% temperature drop.
                  </jats:p>

title:
Domain refinement and constrained polar dynamics enable high-energy-storage in mixed-valence Pr-doped NaNbO
                    <sub>3</sub>
                    -based lead-free ceramics
items.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    The development of high-performance dielectric ceramics is critical for advanced pulsed power capacitors, yet reconciling mutually exclusive energy-storage parameters remains a formidable challenge. Here, we achieve a superior recoverable energy density (W
                    <jats:sub>rec</jats:sub>
                    ) of ~5.4 J/cm
                    <jats:sup>3</jats:sup>
                    with a high efficiency (η) of ~90.2% in a lead-free Pr
                    <jats:sub>6</jats:sub>
                    O
                    <jats:sub>11</jats:sub>
                    -doped NaNbO
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    -BaTiO
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    -SrZrO
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    composition near the morphotropic phase boundary. This material also delivers exceptional charge-discharge capabilities, including a power density of ~254.7 MW/cm
                    <jats:sup>3</jats:sup>
                    , a discharge energy density of ~1.4 J/cm
                    <jats:sup>3</jats:sup>
                    , and an ultrafast discharge rate below 30 ns. Multiscale structural analyses reveal that mixed-valence Pr
                    <jats:sup>3+</jats:sup>
                    /Pr
                    <jats:sup>4+</jats:sup>
                    effectively disrupts the long-range ferroelectric ordering, promoting the formation of highly dynamic and polymorphic polar nanoregions. The electricfield response of these polar nanoregions is further constrained by local defect dipoles arising from Pr-induced charge imbalances, which delays polarization saturation while suppressing hysteresis. In addition, the Pr-doping-induced grain refinement, together with a wide bandgap inherited from the NaNbO
                    <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                    matrix, synergistically enhances dielectric breakdown strength. Collectively, the synergy between domain refinement and constrained polar dynamics enables the concurrent optimization of W
                    <jats:sub>rec</jats:sub>
                    and η, offering a broadly applicable strategy for designing advanced dielectrics for capacitive energy-storage applications.
                  </jats:p>

title: Vocal cord paralysis due to oesophageal dilatation in a post-radiotherapy head and neck oncology patient
Codebase release 1.0 for HEPTAPOD
items.abstract: <jats:p>Many workflows in high-energy-physics (HEP) stand to benefit from recent advances in transformer-based large language models (LLMs). While early applications of LLMs focused on text generation and code completion, modern LLMs now support orchestrated agency: the coordinated execution of complex, multi-step tasks through tool use, structured context, and iterative reasoning. We introduce the HEP Toolkit for Agentic Planning, Orchestration, and Deployment (HEPTAPOD), an orchestration framework designed to integrate external LLMs into general HEP workflows spanning theoretical calculations, simulation, and data analysis. The framework enables LLMs to interface with domain-specific tools and to construct and manage diverse HEP pipelines while preserving transparency, reproducibility, and human oversight. To demonstrate these capabilities, we present a representative case study in the context of a Beyond the Standard Model (BSM) Monte Carlo signal validation that spans model generation, event simulation, and analysis within an established, reproducible workflow. HEPTAPOD provides a structured and auditable layer between human researchers, LLMs, and computational infrastructure, establishing a foundation for transparent, human-in-the-loop systems.</jats:p>

title: Early postnatal leukocyte profiles in very preterm infants with ureaplasma positivity versus clinically non-septic bacterial infection
items.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>To compare peripheral leukocyte profiles between very preterm infants with PCR-detected Ureaplasma and those with clinically non-septic bacterial infection.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Study design</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This retrospective cohort study included very preterm infants admitted to Shenzhen Maternity &amp; Child Healthcare Hospital between 2022 and 2024. Infants were classified into a Ureaplasma group based on positive real-time PCR testing or a bacterial infection group based on clinically non-septic bacterial infection with negative Ureaplasma testing. Complete blood count parameters during postnatal days (PD) 1-3 and PD4-7were compared using the Mann–Whitney U test, and multiple linear regression was used to adjust for gestational age (GA), birth weight (BW), intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR), preterm premature rupture of membranes (PPROM), vaginal delivery and multiple pregnancies, with a Generalized Linear Model (GLM) applied as a sensitivity analysis.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      Among 205 infants, 78 (38.0%) were Ureaplasma-positive. In the PD 1-3, the Ureaplasma group had higher total leukocyte, neutrophil, lymphocyte, and monocyte counts. In the PD 4-7, differences were mainly neutrophil-related, with higher total leukocyte and neutrophil counts. After adjustment, Ureaplasma positivity remained associated with higher neutrophil counts in the PD 1-3 (B = 3.488, 95% CI 1.469-5.507;
                      <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                       &lt; 0.001). A sensitivity analysis using a Generalized Linear Model (GLM) confirmed the robustness of this association across both intervals (
                      <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                       &lt; 0.001 and
                      <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                       = 0.031, respectively).
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Very preterm infants with PCR-detected Ureaplasma had higher leukocyte and neutrophil counts than those with clinically non-septic bacterial infection during the first postnatal week.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Deep learning dose prediction from free breathing CT to triage deep inspiration breath hold in left breast cancer radiotherapy
items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Deep-inspiration breath hold (DIBH) reduces cardiac dose in left-sided breast cancer radiotherapy but increases imaging and planning workload. To screen the dosimetric acceptability of free-breathing (FB) plans before DIBH-CT acquisition, we developed a deep learning model to predict 3D dose distribution from FB-CT alone. We analyzed 120 left-sided breast cancer patients treated with a field-in-field technique, developing a 3D U-Net (96 patients) using FB-CT images and structure masks and evaluating it on a held-out internal test set (24 patients). For the primary decision metric, mean heart dose (MHD), the mean absolute error was 1.14 ± 0.81 Gy. Classifying whether the predicted FB-plan MHD exceeded 7 Gy yielded an accuracy of 0.79, sensitivity of 0.83, specificity of 0.75, and an AUC-ROC of 0.90 (95% CI: 0.58–1.00). After Holm-Bonferroni correction, differences in left lung V
                    <jats:sub>20Gy</jats:sub>
                    and PTV D
                    <jats:sub>95%</jats:sub>
                    and D
                    <jats:sub>90%</jats:sub>
                    remained significant; MHD showed a small mean signed bias (predicted − ground truth: 0.08 Gy, 95% CI: −0.52 to 0.68 Gy) but wider patient-level limits of agreement (Bland-Altman 95% limits: −2.69 to 2.86 Gy). The model demonstrates promising but imprecisely estimated classification performance and may reduce unnecessary DIBH-CT acquisitions and workload, though this is unquantified. Multicenter and prospective validation are warranted.
                  </jats:p>

title: Computed tomography-based artificial intelligence and radiomics for chemotherapy- and radiotherapy-related cardiotoxicity: A mini-review
items.abstract: <jats:p>Cancer therapy-related cardiovascular toxicity often remains clinically silent until myocardial dysfunction or vascular disease develops. Computed tomography (CT), integral to cancer screening, staging, radiotherapy planning, and follow-up, serves as a valuable yet underutilized source of cardiovascular information. This narrative minireview, derived from a nonsystematic PubMed search, examines the potential of artificial intelligence (AI) and radiomics to improve CT-based assessments of cardiovascular injury during oncologic therapy. An overview of the pathological basis of treatment-related cardiotoxicity is provided, along with applications of dedicated cardiac CT, including coronary artery calcium scoring, coronary CT angiography, and CT-derived fractional flow reserve. Opportunistic cardiovascular screening on routine non-electrocardiogram-gated chest CT is also emphasized. AI-enabled automated cardiac quantification and the capability of radiomics to extract quantitative features of myocardium and coronary plaques for risk prediction are highlighted. Integration of CT with other modalities, clinical decision-support systems, and multidisciplinary care is discussed. Current challenges, such as data standardization, model interpretability, and radiation exposure, are addressed, along with future directions involving therapy-specific models and multi-omics integration. Most existing CT-based AI and radiomics studies are retrospective, necessitating external validation and prospective evaluation to establish clinical utility.</jats:p>

title: A permissioned blockchain-based transactive architecture for smart contract-driven P2P energy trading in prosumer communities
items.abstract: <jats:p xml:lang="en">The growth of distributed renewable generation has increased the number of prosumers who both generate and consume electricity. This paper proposes a permissioned blockchain architecture for peer-to-peer (P2P) energy settlement in prosumer communities. A structured review of 62 peer-reviewed studies published between 2015, and June 2026 informs the design. The architecture combines a private Ethereum network using Quorum Byzantine Fault Tolerant (QBFT) consensus, four interacting smart contracts, a multi-oracle metering bridge, and a network-feasibility oracle operated by the distribution system operator (DSO). Its contributions are interval-level energy allocation with controls against double assignment, shared-capacity accounting across concurrent contracts, a specification for four forms of oracle redundancy, a smart-contract state-transition model covering normal and error paths, and a token-flow model that reconciles payments and collateral under normal delivery, surplus, shortfall, DSO curtailment, and oracle timeout. The evaluation comprises a synthesis of the coded literature, security threat modelling, and an illustrative settlement reconciliation. Empirical performance evaluation is deferred to a companion testnet study.</jats:p>

title: Advances in deep inspiration breath-hold technique for radiotherapy of right-sided breast cancer
items.abstract: <jats:p>Deep inspiration breath-hold (DIBH) has become increasingly common in the postoperative radiotherapy of left-sided breast cancer, owing to its well-established role in sparing the heart and ipsilateral lung. For right-sided tumors, however, the clinical benefit of this technique is considerably less well defined. In most studies to date, DIBH has been shown to reduce both V20 and mean lung dose in right-sided breast cancer, with larger gains observed when regional nodal irradiation is included. The liver also appears to derive a dosimetric advantage. Cardiac findings are more mixed: While some reports indicate measurable reductions in whole-heart and right coronary artery doses, the decreases are typically small and exhibit substantial interpatient variability. Meanwhile, contralateral breast doses seem largely unaffected. Regarding breath-hold monitoring, the vast majority of investigations have utilized real-time position management or the optical surface monitoring system, whereas active breathing control has seen comparatively limited application in this context. Taken together, the existing evidence supports the use of right-sided DIBH for lung and liver protection; however, its value for the heart and contralateral breast remains uncertain, and further prospective studies are warranted to clarify these issues.</jats:p>

title: Self-Propagating High-Temperature Synthesis of Aluminum Oxynitride: A Review
container-title: International Journal of Self-Propagating High-Temperature Synthesis
items.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      Self-propagating high-temperature synthesis (SHS) has emerged as a promising alternative to conventional solid-state and carbothermal reduction methods for producing aluminum oxynitride (γ-AlON), a transparent polycrystalline ceramic known for its outstanding optical and mechanical properties. This review presents a comprehensive overview of the development of SHS-based routes for AlON synthesis over the past two decades, ranging from early combustion of aluminum powders in air to more advanced chemically activated processes capable of producing phase-pure powders suitable for transparent ceramic applications. The review first examines the thermodynamic and kinetic features of aluminum combustion in air, which provide the foundation for understanding the counterintuitive formation of nitrides and oxynitrides in an oxygen-containing atmosphere. A key issue in this field is the stoichiometric limitation of the Al–Al
                      <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                      O
                      <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                      –N
                      <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                      system, which initially hindered the direct synthesis of phase-pure AlON. Several strategies developed to overcome this challenge are discussed, including thermally coupled SHS with external heat supplied by “chemical fovens”, combined centrifugal casting–SHS process based on highly exothermic thermite-type reactions involving CrO
                      <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                      , MoO
                      <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                      , and Fe
                      <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                      O
                      <jats:sub>3</jats:sub>
                      , with AlN serving as a solid nitrogen source to produce cast AlON ingots, and chemically activated SHS using magnesium or potassium perchlorates as internal oxidizers to enhance combustion temperature while maintaining stoichiometric control. Overall, this review highlights the process of SHS technology for AlON powder synthesis and outlines the remaining challenges, particularly in controlling impurities and improving the optical quality of ceramics fabricated from SHS-derived powders.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: A Concise Review of Catalytically Active Materials Produced via Self-Propagating High-Temperature Synthesis
container-title: International Journal of Self-Propagating High-Temperature Synthesis
items.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>More than half a century has passed since the advent of self-propagating high-temperature synthesis (SHS) [1]. During this period, numerous SHS-based methods have been established for fabricating both structural and functional materials, including catalytically active systems. Although recent reviews [2–5] have outlined the principal synthesis strategies and catalytic performances of SHS-derived materials, the field continues to advance rapidly, and many new studies have emerged in recent years. The present review therefore aims to systematize and summarize these latest developments in SHS preparation of catalytic materials and to evaluate their performance across a broad spectrum of chemical processes.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: From energy crisis to solar boom: the political economy of decentralized clean energy transition in Pakistan
items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Since 2022, Pakistan has experienced a rapid surge of rooftop solar photovoltaic (PV) adoption as households and businesses increasingly shift toward distributed solar systems to reduce dependence on the national grid. This unprecedented shift raises critical questions for energy governance, energy system sustainability, and energy justice, particularly regarding how distributed, user-driven innovations can reshape a clean energy transition beyond formal policy and planning frameworks. The paper examines the drivers of this solar power boom through an integrative political economy framework combining market, socio-technical, and governance dynamics. It draws on 38 semi-structured interviews with policymakers, representatives of regulatory bodies, electricity utilities, solar businesses, industry experts, and think tanks, alongside documentary analysis. The study offers a distinctive explanation of how distributed, people-led solar adoption can drive rapid transformation and reshape established electricity systems in a large developing country such as Pakistan, despite structural and institutional constraints.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Our findings show that rising tariffs, declining grid reliability, and governance inertia combined with falling global solar PV prices and affordable equipment imported from China have accelerated solar PV adoption in Pakistan. Informal market practices, alongside formal net-metering arrangements, have shaped this transition. However, the transition has generated uneven socio-economic outcomes and new distributional tensions associated with partial grid defection. The findings further reveal growing tensions between rapidly expanding distributed solar PV systems and existing regulatory frameworks, cost recovery and grid operations in Pakistan’s electricity sector. These tensions highlight emerging governance and equity challenges for sustainable energy transitions in Pakistan, with broader implications for the Global South.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The paper contributes to debates on sustainable energy transitions in the Global South by advancing an integrative political economy perspective on decentralized clean energy systems. It demonstrates how interactions among market pressures, socio-technical diffusion, and institutional dynamics can simultaneously disrupt incumbent energy regimes and reproduce underlying infrastructural dependencies in the processes of clean energy transition. This underscores the need for adaptive policy frameworks and inclusive governance approaches that integrate distributed energy systems into national policy and planning frameworks.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

items.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    We investigated the effects of Ar and Kr heavy-ion irradiation at 1.0 × 10
                    <jats:sup>7</jats:sup>
                    ions cm
                    <jats:sup>−2</jats:sup>
                    on unbiased AlGaN/GaN high-electron-mobility transistors (HEMTs). After irradiation, the drain current and transconductance degraded by less than 10%, and the threshold voltage shifted slightly for both ions. In contrast, Kr-irradiated HEMTs exhibited greater degradation in gate leakage current and off-state breakdown voltage than Ar-irradiated devices, which is attributed to Schottky contact deterioration and defect generation in the AlGaN barrier. Stopping and range of ions in matter (SRIM) simulations revealed that Kr ions generate more vacancies throughout the HEMT layer than Ar ions owing to larger nuclear energy loss, consistent with these results.
                  </jats:p>

title:
Synergistic Iodide/Capacitive Ion Storage in a Fluorinated Carbon Black Matrix Toward 1.9 V High‐Energy‐Density Zn‐I
                    <sub>2</sub>
                    Batteries
items.abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Aqueous zinc‐iodine (Zn‐I
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    ) batteries hold promise for high‐safety, large‐scale energy storage. However, their performance is hindered by the polyiodide shuttle effect and the low voltage plateau (∼1.2 V). Herein, we enhance the capacitive behavior under high voltage by introducing a fluorinated carbon black (CF
                    <jats:sub>20</jats:sub>
                    ) matrix into a I
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    /activated carbon (AC) cathode. The CF
                    <jats:sub>20</jats:sub>
                    matrix attracts more ions into AC at high potential and enhances the capacitive ions storage behavior. When both AC and iodine are counted, the specific cathode capacity increases from 117.9 mAh g
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    (up to 1.6 V) to 163.4 mAh g
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    (up to 1.9 V), equivalent to 329.8 mAh g
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    counting iodine only. Meanwhile, the CF
                    <jats:sub>20</jats:sub>
                    matrix effectively chemisorbs polyiodides, acting as a shuttle suppressor. The full cell retains >85% initial capacity after 6500 cycles at 4 A g
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    . When the mass loading is increased to 32.46 mg cm
                    <jats:sup>−2</jats:sup>
                    , it delivers a record areal capacity of 2.92 mAh cm
                    <jats:sup>−2</jats:sup>
                    . When paired with a ∼7 um Zn foil (N/p = 1.4), the full cell retains 83% capacity over 900 cycles, demonstrate an energy density as high as 204 Wh kg
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    . This work provides a viable paradigm to activate capacitive contribution in Zn‐I
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    system toward high‐voltage, high‐energy‐density aqueous batteries.
                  </jats:p>

title: A Note on the Spillover of Geopolitical Risks in Nigeria Into Global Energy Markets
items.abstract: <jats:p>This study investigates whether domestic geopolitical risks in Nigeria extend into global energy-related uncertainties. To fulfil this objective, it employs time-varying Granger causality tests covering the period from January 2012 to October 2022. Observable spillovers are identified during significant events such as the EndSARS protests, herdsmen attacks, and the kidnapping of Chibok schoolgirls. These findings illustrate how Nigeria’s geopolitical turmoil impacts not only the country’s oil production and local economy but also the global energy markets. The results indicate a feedback loop where Nigeria’s geopolitical challenges amplify uncertainties around the world’s energy supply, which can further compromise Nigeria’s internal security.</jats:p>

title: Irradiation Response of a Hot-Forged Co-Free FeNiCrMn High-Entropy Alloy
items.abstract: <jats:p>Developing Co-free high-entropy alloys is critical for their possible application in next-generation nuclear reactors. This study investigates the heavy-ion irradiation response of a hot-forged FeNiCrMn high-entropy alloy (5 MeV Fe2+ at 300 °C to 1 and 10 dpa) to determine how pre-existing dislocation networks govern defect evolution. Comprehensive microstructural characterization via EBSD, TEM, and STEM-EDS reveals a dynamic defect evolution. The dislocation line density initially decreased at 1 dpa but by 10 dpa reached the same level as in the pristine sample and was accompanied by an increase in Frank loop density and formation of a dislocation network, consistent with stress-assisted loop unfaulting. The pre-existing dislocation network is proposed to act as a biased sink for interstitials, promoting vacancy supersaturation that accelerates void nucleation, resulting in the formation of nanoscale voids at 1 dpa. This dislocation network could restrict long-range diffusion of point defects, suppressing radiation-induced segregation (RIS) at the grain boundaries even after 10 dpa. These findings highlight a critical microstructural trade-off. While the dislocation network appears to suppress the grain boundary segregation, it simultaneously promotes early-stage void nucleation. Finally, this study suggests that tailoring the initial dislocation density in Co-free HEAs requires a balance between competing degradation mechanisms.</jats:p>

title:
Tuning Photocatalytic Performance of CuSbS
                    <sub>2</sub>
                    /CdS Nanoparticles by Microwave Irradiation Method
items.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Combining CuSbS2 (CAS) with n-type semiconductors is a promising strategy to enhance photocatalytic performance. In this work, CAS/CdS nanoparticles were synthesized via a two-step microwave irradiation method. The effects of CdS reaction solvent and CAS loading amount on crystal structure, morphology, interfacial properties, and photocatalytic activity of CAS/CdS nanoparticles were investigated. The optimal catalyst, prepared using ammonia (AH) as the solvent with a CAS loading of 0.08 g, achieved a total Rhodamine B (RhB) removal efficiency of 90.4%, including dark adsorption, and an adsorption-normalized photocatalytic degradation efficiency of 83.9% under simulated solar light. This corresponds to a pseudo-first-order rate constant of 0.0101 min
                    <jats:sup>-1</jats:sup>
                    , which is 5.3 times higher than that of pure CAS. Active species trapping experiments identified photogenerated holes (h
                    <jats:sup>+</jats:sup>
                    ) as the primary reactive species. The performance enhancement is attributed to the synergistic effects of a large specific surface area (94.818 m
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                    /g), intimate interfacial contact, and efficient charge separation facilitated by the construction of type-II heterojunction. This work clarifies the synergistic regulation mechanism of solvent and loading amount on the structure-activity relationship of CAS/CdS, providing a potentially strategy for designing high-performance sulfide-based photocatalysts.
                  </jats:p>

title: HPLC-HRMS Identification of Antibiotic Degradation Products in Food Matrices After Exposure to E-Beam Irradiation
items.abstract: <jats:p>(1) Background: Recently, the widespread use of antibiotics has led to increased levels of their residues in natural aquatic environments, livestock waste, and food products. (2) Methods: This study presents an experimental investigation into the degradation of tetracycline and chloramphenicol in aqueous solutions and food matrices (milk, chicken, and honey) upon exposure to 7.5 MeV accelerated electrons at the doses of 0, 1, 3, 7, 10, and 20 kGy, using high-performance liquid chromatography coupled with high-resolution mass spectrometry (HPLC-HRMS). (3) Results: It was found that electron-beam irradiation of aqueous antibiotic solutions at the doses of 3 kGy and 10 kGy resulted in the removal of 98–99% of tetracycline and chloramphenicol, respectively, starting from initial concentrations of 20 mg/L. The behavior of the antibiotics differed significantly in food matrices. Chloramphenicol degradation rate constants were close in values in different food matrices and comparable to those observed in water. (4) Conclusions: HPLC-HRMS analysis revealed five degradation products for tetracycline and six for chloramphenicol in irradiated aqueous solutions, which exceeds the number of antibiotic degradation products identified in food matrices.</jats:p>

title: Exploratory Assessment of Subjective Experiences and Physiological Measures Following Three-Wavelength LED Irradiation of the Head
items.abstract: <jats:p>In this exploratory study, we evaluated short-term changes in subjective perceptions and measured physiological indices following three-wavelength LED irradiation of the head. In 36 adults, paraspinal skin surface temperature, subjective relaxation rating on the visual analog scale (VAS), mean heart rate, and RMSSD were measured before intervention, after the 20-min intervention, and approximately 10 min later. The low-configuration batch was enrolled first and the high-configuration batch later, without randomized batch assignment; participants were randomized to the active-light or sham-light condition within each batch. The overall Time effect for skin surface temperature was significant, but adjusted contrasts between each postintervention assessment and baseline were not, and no clear differences in temporal trajectories between light conditions were observed. VAS scores varied over time, with temporal trajectories differing by light condition; however, differences for specific groups or time points remain unconfirmed. Mean heart rate and RMSSD showed no clear changes, with RMSSD residual diagnostics indicating a need for cautious interpretation. Muscle tension, stress, and actual scalp light exposure were not directly measured, precluding conclusions regarding muscle relaxation or therapeutic benefits.</jats:p>

title: Fluoride Gel pH, Color, and Concentration Influence Enamel Fluoride Retention After Low-Energy 445 nm Diode Laser Irradiation: An Ex Vivo Study
items.abstract: <jats:p>Objectives: This ex vivo study investigated the influence of fluoride gel acidity and colorimetric profile on 445 nm diode laser–enhanced enamel fluoride retention, surface microhardness, and morphology. Methods: Enamel discs prepared from caries-free permanent human teeth were allocated to four groups according to gel formulation: dye-free acidulated phosphate fluoride (APF), dye-free neutral-pH fluoride, red-pigmented neutral-pH fluoride, and red-pigmented APF. Each group was further divided into laser-irradiated and non-irradiated subgroups. Irradiation was performed in continuous-wave (CW) mode at a working distance of 5 cm using a laboratory optical system that expanded the beam to a 10 mm diameter at the enamel surface. The delivered power was verified with a calibrated laser power meter to ensure that 350 mW effectively reached the enamel surface for 30 s, corresponding to an energy density of 13.375 J/cm2 and a power density of 0.445 W/cm2. Fluoride content was quantified by particle-induced gamma-ray emission (PIGE) at baseline, immediately after fluoridation, and after laser irradiation followed by 7 days of immersion in double-distilled water at 36 °C. Vickers microhardness testing and scanning electron microscopy (SEM) were performed on irradiated specimens. Thermographic monitoring was used to record the enamel surface temperature during irradiation. Results: The dye-free APF group combined with laser irradiation achieved the highest fluoride retention (1290.23 ± 18.47 ppm, n = 30), significantly exceeding all other groups (p < 0.0001). Microhardness did not differ significantly among groups (p > 0.05), and SEM revealed no morphological surface alterations after irradiation. The mean temperature rise at the enamel surface during the 30 s irradiation was 11.81 ± 0.33 °C. Conclusion: Under the present experimental conditions, dye-free APF gel combined with low-energy 445 nm diode laser irradiation provided the most effective enamel fluoride retention among the formulations tested. Differences in gel pH, color, and fluoride concentration influenced the magnitude of this effect.</jats:p>

title: Combined laser irradiation effects at the cutaneous infl ammatory response during tattoo pigment removal (an experimental study)
items.abstract: <jats:p>The authors present results of an experimental study with Wistar rats on the effectiveness of combined laser irradiation at wavelengths 532 nm and 1064 nm for tattoo pigment removal. The aim of this study was to assess morphological changes in the skin and depth of laser light penetration exposure in the discussed combined modality compared to monochromatic irradiation. In the control groups, patients were treated separately with laser wavelengths 532 nm and 1064 nm, while in the experimental group both wavelengths were applied consequently. Histological examination revealed that the combined method gives the deepest penetration (120-150 μm) and nearly complete destruction of pigment in both superficial and deep dermal layers, though it causes a pronounced inflammatory reaction. Monochromatic 532 nm irradiation showed superficial effects (40-70 μm) with pigment retention in deep layers and epidermal atrophy, whereas 1064 nm irradiation demonstrated intermediate penetration depth (80-110 μm) with uniform pigment destruction and minimal damage to surrounding tissues. These findings confirm that the choice of laser therapy should be based on the depth of pigment location and clinical objectives. The combined approach is optimal for complete pigment removal, while monochromatic 1064 nm irradiation may be recommended for cases requiring minimal damage to superficial skin layers.</jats:p>

title: 6-Tungsto-6-molybdophosphoric Acid Promoted Facile Synthesis of 2,3-Dihydro-2-phenylquinazolin-4(1H)-ones Under Ultrasound Irradiation
container-title: Orbital: The Electronic Journal of Chemistry
items.abstract: <jats:p>A facile synthesis of 2,3-dihydro-2-phenylquinazolin-4(1H)-ones has been carried out via cyclocondensation reaction of anthranilamide with various aromatic aldehydes using 6-tungsto-6-molybdophosphoric acid (H3PW6Mo6O40)as a catalyst in ethanol under ultrasonic irradiation. The Keggin-type 6-tungsto-6-molybdophosphoric acid was prepared using the etherate method and characterized by FT-IR spectroscopy and thermal analysis. The effect of several reaction parameters on the rate of reaction was investigated. The distinct features of this protocol include shorter reaction time, operational simplicity, mild reaction conditions, excellent yield, inexpensive and reusable catalyst.</jats:p>

title: CO2 Hydrogenation to Methanol over Metal–Organic Framework Catalysts: Reaction Pathways and Catalyst Design Strategies
items.abstract: <jats:p>Conversion of CO2 into fuels and value-added chemicals is an emerging area that enables the evolution toward a circular carbon economy. CO2 can be utilized to produce methanol, ethanol, methane and light olefins through renewable hydrogen. Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) are an excellent platform for thermocatalytic CO2 hydrogenation to methanol, as their metal nodes, organic linkers, defects and confined pore environments can be engineered to enhance CO2 adsorption, H2 activation and stabilization of crucial reaction intermediates. However, many MOFs still suffer from drawbacks such as low thermal stability, limited mass transport, weak metal-support interaction and potential framework destruction under hydrogenation conditions, which can limit methanol productivity and long-term catalyst stability. This review summarizes recent progress in MOF-based catalysts and MOF-derived materials for CO2 hydrogenation to methanol, with a focus on reaction pathways, pore confinement, active-site design, catalyst stability, and structure-performance relationships. The advantages and remaining limitations of MOF systems are discussed in comparison with conventional heterogeneous catalysts, and future strategies are proposed for developing more selective, durable, and energy-efficient catalysts for sustainable methanol synthesis.</jats:p>

title: CFD Simulation and Optimization of Adiabatic Reaction Process of C-2 Hydrogenation
container-title: International Journal of Theoretical & Computational Physics
items.abstract: <jats:p>In this paper, the computational fluid dynamics (CFD) method has been used to simulate the gas flow and the catalytic hydrogenation process of the C-2 hydrogenation adiabatic reactor in a practical ethylene production unit of a chemical plant. The laminar finite-rate model was used for the chemical reaction model. The standard k -ε two-equation model was used for the turbulence Model. The exponent-function kinetic model was used for the reaction dynamics model. The simulation results were in good agreement with the actual industrial data obtained from the C-2 hydrogenation reactor, and the distributions of reaction parameters such as temperature and component concentrations in the reactor were further analyzed. Based on the validated CFD models, the structure and operating conditions of the reactor, as well as hydrogen load distribution ratios, are simulated for comparing the comprehensive performance metrics of ethylene selectivity and acetylene conversion rate; as a result, we can obtain the optimal temperature of 312 K, the optimal hydrogen/acetylene ratio of 0.10 as well as the optimal hydrogen load distribution ratio of 4:4:2, and the diameter/height ratio exerts a marginal effect on the selectivity, conversion rate and harmonic mean of the reactor.</jats:p>

Risperidone: Adverse cutaneous reaction managed without drug discontinuation
items.abstract: <jats:p>Antipsychotic agents can cause skin rashes in some patients, affecting compliance. Although more common with typical antipsychotics, atypical antipsychotics such as olanzapine and clozapine have also been associated with these reactions. While there is no way to predict such reactions, the mechanisms causing such reactions are being actively researched. We present a case study of a 36-year-old female who developed cutaneous reactions with oral risperidone. It was observed that reducing the dose of oral risperidone led to complete resolution of skin rashes, a novel approach that differed from previous reports requiring complete discontinuation.</jats:p>

title: Appraisal and evidentiality in interlingual news reporting
items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    This paper examines evidentiality and appraisal in the presentation of interlingual news sources on the Joint
          Comprehensive Plan of Action (JCPOA), or the Iran nuclear deal, in the Iranian newspaper
                    <jats:italic>Kayhan</jats:italic>
                    to understand the origins
          of news writers’ knowledge, how they express the reliability of sources, and the rhetorical effects of these choices. The analysis uses
                    <jats:italic>MAXQDA</jats:italic>
                    to code for evidentiality (
                    <jats:xref>Aikhenvald 2004</jats:xref>
                    ) and appraisal (sub)systems
            (
                    <jats:xref>Martin & White 2005</jats:xref>
                    ), with particular focus on how evidential choices interact with
          evaluative stance. The results indicate that coverage is not neutral, despite multiple sourcing. The high frequency of quotative
          evidentiality may contribute to the neutrality of coverage; however, the dominance of appraisal systems expressing meanings of distance and
          condemnation within the matrix clauses introduces and reinforces bias. Evidential choices and appraisal resources function as
          ‘authorisation’ and ‘rationalisation’ (
                    <jats:xref>Van Leeuwen 2007</jats:xref>
                    ) that selectively endorse or discredit

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objectives</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Iodinated contrast media (ICM) are essential for diagnostic imaging but impose a substantial environmental burden due to their widespread use. This prospective observational study evaluates the efficiency of a novel toilet filtration system (TFS) for recovering ICM after contrast-enhanced CT (ceCT) and explores factors that contribute to successful implementation of the system.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Materials and methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This prospective observational study included consecutive outpatients scheduled for ceCT using Iomeprol as ICM. Patients were informed about the TFS, ICM excretion, and environmental implications. They were asked to wait at least 30 min after scanning and to use the TFS for their first post-ceCT urination. The removal efficiency of the TFS was determined by measuring ICM concentrations in influent and effluent streams. The proportion of administered ICM recovered was calculated from the cartridge’s contents.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Of 395 consecutive patients undergoing ceCT, 277 (70%) consented to participate, and 273 patients (median age 65.5; IQR: 57.2–73.4; 151 men) successfully used the TFS. The median interval between contrast administration and urination was 36 min (IQR: 31–41). Most patients (81%) waited at least 30 min before voiding. Removal efficiency of the TFS exceeded 99.9% for ICM. Limited ICM excretion led to recovery of 2.78 kg out of 18.41 kg administered Iomeprol (15.1%; 1.36 kg iodine).</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>While ICM is efficiently removed using a novel TFS (> 99.9%), ICM excretion during the 30-min post-examination waiting period was limited. The approach can recover approximately 71 kg of ICM per year per 10,000 ceCT examinations, a number that could be further improved through efforts to increase ICM excretion.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Key Points</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      <jats:bold>
                        <jats:italic>Question</jats:italic>
                      </jats:bold>
                      TFS have the potential to reduce the amount of contrast media entering wastewater, but their effectiveness is unclear.
                    </jats:p>
                    <jats:p>
                      <jats:bold>
                        <jats:italic>Findings</jats:italic>
                      </jats:bold>
                      TFS achieved excellent contrast removal, and was well accepted by patients, but contrast excretion within the median 36-min waiting period is limited to 15%.
                    </jats:p>
                    <jats:p>
                      <jats:bold>
                        <jats:italic>Critical relevance statement</jats:italic>
                      </jats:bold>
                      The novel toilet-based filtration system enables substantial iodine recovery from excreted ICM in urine, but limited post-ceCT excretion during short waiting times highlights the need for process adaptations to further increase overall excretion and maximise iodine recovery rates.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

                    Fixed-horizon mine-capacity screens can confound capacity with unequal processed-material support. We evaluate a pre-scheduling audit that declares the target, measures support coverage and decomposes a calendar contrast into common-support and terminal components. In 12,000 paired synthetic draws with 18 Mt reference support, five-period median processed support was 4.34 Mt at 1 Mt/y and 13.02 Mt at 3 Mt/y. Reversal occurred in 250/12,000 draws (2.08%), 250/499 calendar wins (50.1%), 6/76 wins with a positive larger-policy calendar response (7.9%), and 110/292 wins with at least one positive common-support response (37.7%; retrospective). All-draw mean regret was US$0.457 million. The retrospective share ranged from 15% to 88% across 9–21 Mt supports. items.abstract: <jats:p>Material Flow Cost Accounting (MFCA) is a management accounting method that helps measure and analyze material flow and related costs in the production process. By using MFCA, companies can better understand how materials are used, identify areas of waste or material loss, and determine its impact on overall production costs. Thus, MFCA helps companies improve production efficiency, reduce waste, and optimize resource usage. Food loss refers to the reduction in the quantity of consumable food products at various stages of the food supply chain, including production, post-harvest, and processing. Food loss can occur due to various factors, such as handling errors, damage, or inefficiencies in production and distribution processes. This study aims to determine the potential for food loss after implementing MFCA in the food industry. This research is a qualitative descriptive study using a case study method. Data collection techniques used in this study include interviews, observations, and documentation studies. The results show that the total production cost of PD. AIDAH in June was IDR 125,636,389. After implementing MFCA, PD. AIDAH's total final product cost was 92.55% of the total production cost or IDR 116,273,889. PD AIDAH experienced food loss of 7.45% of the total production cost or IDR 9,362,500</jats:p>

The Role of Gamma
Irradiation in Tailoring Carbon-Based
Catalysts for Oxygen Reduction in Air-Cathodes: A Review
items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Carbon-based catalysts have emerged as promising alternatives to noble-metal electrocatalysts for air-cathodes in metal-air batteries and fuel cells. Their limited intrinsic oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) activity and durability necessitate effective modification strategies. This review examines the role of gamma (γ) irradiation as a postsynthetic modification approach for carbon-based catalysts used in ORR. It discusses irradiation-induced structural and electronic changes, including defect generation, surface functionalization, pore development, and electronic structure tuning. These modifications increase active-site density, facilitate oxygen adsorption, and improve charge-transfer kinetics, leading to enhanced ORR activity, selectivity, and durability. It also highlighted the influence of irradiation dose and processing conditions, emphasizing the need for optimized irradiation parameters to maximize catalytic performance while avoiding structural degradation. A comprehensive assessment of γ-irradiation-driven engineering of carbon catalysts is analyzed for air-cathodes, establishing structure–property–performance relationships and highlighting γ-irradiation as a scalable, environmentally friendly route for developing high-performance ORR electrocatalysts.</jats:p>

title: Ritual, Material Culture, and Interaction in the Epiclassic Basin of Mexico: Contextualizing a Temple Assemblage from Chicoloapan
items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Central Mexico’s Epiclassic period (AD 550–850) was a time of significant social change, including the breakdown of the Teotihuacan state, the relocation of large numbers of people, and the development of new practices. However, the specific activities that shaped Epiclassic communities and their interactions with each other remain poorly understood. Here, we consider how suprahousehold ritual forged social relations within a community while contributing to broader shifts in religious practice and interaction among regional settlements. We present an analysis of artifacts and features from extensive excavations in a temple complex at Chicoloapan, a settlement in the southern Basin of Mexico. A comparison of materials from the complex—including censers, musical instruments, and figurines—to those from domestic contexts suggests that community and household rituals were closely linked and involved similar material culture. Beyond the settlement, many of these practices and materials reflected and reinforced shared religious concepts, social ties, and exchange patterns among different groups. This research sheds light on the internal dynamics of an Epiclassic community and relates local practices to wide-ranging cultural developments.</jats:p>

title: Witness Privilege and Material Truth Single Fact Witness Under the New Indonesian Criminal Procedure Code from a Positivist Legal Perspective
items.abstract:
<jats:p>Article 218 of the Indonesian Criminal Procedure Code (Law Number 20 of 2025) allows family members of the defendant to withdraw as witnesses, while Article 220 allows those bound by confidentiality obligations to request an exemption from testimony. This article asks how both norms should be applied, from a legal positivist perspective, when the holder of privilege is the sole factual witness. Using doctrinal legal research with legal, historical, and conceptual approaches as well as hypothetical illustrations, this article examines the norms in Kelsen and Hart, with Dworkin's critique of judicial discretion as an external test. First, the two provisions differ in determining where decisions stand: under Article 218, the decision is in the hands of witnesses, with the additional key held by the defendant through Article 219, whereas under Article 220 that right lies with the judge. Second, these three theories meet at the core of the issue: the withdrawal of legitimate family witnesses, this case falls within the core of Article 218 not its penumbra, and the resulting acquittal is not a legal loophole. The open texture is limited to the 'unless otherwise specified' clause and to the judicial criteria under Article 220. Third, the judge's room is limited to freedom to choose witnesses, maximize other evidence, and assess exemption requests based on explicit criteria. De lege ferenda, this article proposes removing the defendant's consent requirement in Article 219, transferring the remaining judge's authority into the content of Article 220, and examining narrow exceptions for domestic violence against children.
 </jats:p>

title: Reducing Roof Heat Gain with Local-Material Air-Cavity Overlays: A Green-Building Retrofit for RCC Roofs in Bangladesh
items.abstract: <jats:p>Flat reinforced cement concrete (RCC) roofs overheat top-floor rooms across South Asia and drive a growing demand for air conditioning, yet commercial roof insulation is rarely affordable in Bangladesh. This study evaluates two passive retrofit overlays built from locally sourced materials as a low-cost green-building envelope measure: a sealed air cavity formed by inverted mud pots and a ventilated cavity formed by a corrugated sheet open at both ends, each under a 50 mm surki topping. Pairs of identical masonry model rooms with 70 mm RCC slabs, one bare and one overlaid, were monitored in Khulna on 20 clear days between November and April under five cases of progressively covered side walls. The two overlays were tested in different periods, so each was compared only with its own reference room. With daily means as the unit of analysis, the sealed overlay lowered the midday ceiling temperature by 3.0 °C (95% CI 1.4–4.5 °C; up to 9 °C in single readings) and the ventilated overlay by 1.7 °C (95% CI 0.7–2.7 °C; up to 5 °C), both significant (p ≤ 0.004). The midday ceiling heat flow, estimated from the ceiling-to-room temperature difference rather than measured, fell by about 79% (95% interval 52–100%) and 40% (16–73%). Indoor air was 0.9 °C cooler under the sealed overlay, a difference close to the measurement uncertainty (p = 0.048), and the 0.3 °C reduction under the ventilated overlay was not significant. In the evening the ceiling under the ventilated overlay was about 1 °C warmer than the bare-slab ceiling, showing the release of stored heat. The sealed cavity reduces the calculated roof U-value by about 45%, although neither overlay alone meets the roof U-value limit that the National Building Code of India sets for warm-humid climates (the Bangladesh National Building Code sets no such limit). Both overlays are practical first-step retrofits that reduce the cooling load left for efficient air conditioning or rooftop solar systems.</jats:p>

title: Geotechnical and Geochemical Evaluation of Saline Soils for Compressed Earth Blocks in Hot Arid Climates
items.abstract: <jats:p>Compressed earth blocks (CEB) are emerging as a low-impact masonry alternative for arid regions worldwide, from the Sahel and North Africa to the southwestern United States and northern Mexico. However, the compatibility between the base soil and the chemical stabilizer is a critical prerequisite for the mechanical performance and durability of the block. In this article, we present the physical and chemical comparative analysis of four soils (S1–S4) derived from the Colorado-River-Delta and the Mexicali Valley in the Mexico–US border irrigated arid region, as a basis for CEB mix design and as a comparison point for other saline, irrigated arid soils. Nine standardized tests were conducted: natural moisture content, specific gravity of solids, particle-size distribution (sieving and sedimentation), Atterberg limits, standard Proctor compaction, methylene blue value, linear shrinkage, and pH. Results are organized in two functional groups: S1 and S3, sandy and dimensionally stable (non-plastic/low-plasticity: CL, linear shrinkage 0–3%), suitable as a granular skeleton; and S2 and S4, with a high fine fraction and higher shrinkage (8–10%), which require controlled dosing. No single soil simultaneously meets the CRATerre/UNE 41410 (International Centre for Earth Construction/Una Norma Española: Spanish Standard) grading and plasticity thresholds, so physical blending (S1 + S2 or S1 + S4) is identified as the primary corrective strategy. This finding is consistent with grading-correction strategies reported for comparable arid-zone soils in Morocco, Algeria, and New Mexico. The pH values (7.78–8.43) indicate slightly alkaline conditions compatible with cementitious stabilizers; however, the slightly alkaline pH together with the region's documented history of saline irrigation from the Colorado-River-Delta represents a risk of secondary ettringite formation. This study offers a transferable diagnostic protocol for other irrigated arid regions confronting the same lime/cement–sulfate incompatibility risk.</jats:p>

title: Effect of Cell Width on Electromagnetic Fields and Electrolyte Circulation in an Industrial Multipolar Magnesium Electrolysis Cell
items.abstract: <jats:p>A sequentially coupled electromagnetic–gas–liquid model of a 135 kA industrial multipolar magnesium electrolysis cell was developed in COMSOL Multiphysics 6.3 to compare two operating cell designs: a narrow cell (NC, 4168 mm) and a wide cell (WC, 4368 mm). An electromagnetic-only modified wide-cell control (MWC, 4268 mm) retained the WC electrode dimensions but reduced the magnesium collection chamber width. Under identical nominal electrode gaps and operating conditions, the calculated maximum electric potential decreased from 1.67 V (NC) to 1.56 V (WC), and the area-averaged normal current density on gas-evolving surfaces was approximately 7–8% lower in the WC. Maximum magnetic flux density magnitudes remained near 33 mT in all configurations, whereas the volume-averaged magnetic flux density magnitudes over the electrode domains were 4.7327, 4.2651, and 4.2420 mT for the NC, MWC, and WC configurations, respectively. The volume-averaged Lorentz force density magnitude over the selected electrolyte region increased from 3.4967 to 10.975 N m−3 between the NC and WC configurations. title: Road material stock and circularity potential in growing cities: the case of Singapore
items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    In dense and land-constrained cities, road infrastructure systems may transition from expansion-led growth towards a greater reliance on maintenance, with implications for material demand and circularity. Using Singapore as an illustrative case, this study applies a bottom-up material flow analysis to quantify material stocks and flows in the urban road network from 1990 to 2022. Total road material stock increased from approximately 37.2 Mt in 1990 to 50.6 Mt in 2022. Granite aggregate accounted for the largest share of this stock, with smaller contributions from bitumen and steel slag aggregate. Although net stock growth was primarily associated with recorded road-network expansion, maintenance generated a persistent annual material demand through wearing course renewal. The cohort-based maintenance model estimates that 615 lane-km required resurfacing in 2022, generating 0.214 Mt of removed asphalt. Under the baseline assumption, 98% of this material was recovered as reclaimed asphalt pavement (RAP). However, the use of RAP was constrained by the maximum incorporation limits applied to wearing- and base-course asphalt demand, indicating that high recovery does not necessarily result in high internal reuse. Road material stock per capita is approximately 9 t cap
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    in 2022, reflecting Singapore’s compact urban form and intensive use of shared infrastructure. Material efficiency declined from approximately 460–423 vehicle-kilometres per tonne between 2012 and 2022. The findings offer transferable insights for other high-density cities facing limited scope for network expansion, underscoring the need to shift policy attention from supporting infrastructure growth towards extending asset lifetimes, optimising renewal cycles, and improving material circularity in existing road networks.
                  </jats:p>
